text: Japanese daimyō Dom Justo Takayama is exiled to the Philippines by shōgun Tokugawa Ieyasu for being Christian.
name: Tokugawa Ieyasu

text: The first Council of People's Commissars is formed, including Vladimir Lenin, Leon Trotsky and Joseph Stalin.
name: Vladimir Lenin

text: Beer Hall Putsch: In Munich, Adolf Hitler leads the Nazis in an unsuccessful attempt to overthrow the German government.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: In Munich, Adolf Hitler narrowly escapes the assassination attempt of Georg Elser while celebrating the 16th anniversary of the Beer Hall Putsch.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: John F. Kennedy is elected as the 35th President of the United States, defeating incumbent Vice President Richard Nixon, who would later be elected president in 1968  and 1972.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson signs into law an antitrust exemption allowing the National Football League to merge with the upstart American Football League.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Iraq disarmament crisis: UN Security Council Resolution 1441: The United Nations Security Council unanimously approves a resolution on Iraq, forcing Saddam Hussein to disarm or face "serious consequences".
name: Saddam Hussein

text: Napoleon Bonaparte leads the Coup of 18 Brumaire ending the Directory government, and becoming First Consul of the successor Consulate Government.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Prince George, Duke of Cornwall (later George V of the United Kingdom), becomes Prince of Wales and Earl of Chester.
name: George V of the United Kingdom

text: Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany abdicates after the German Revolution, and Germany is proclaimed a Republic.
name: Wilhelm II

text: Battle of Stalingrad: German forces of the 6th Army under general Friedrich Paulus reach finally the river bank of the Volga, capturing 90% of the ruined city of Stalingrad and splitting the remaining Soviet forces into two narrow pockets.
name: Friedrich Paulus

text: Robert McNamara is named president of the Ford Motor Company, becoming the first non-Ford family member to serve in that post. He resigns a month later to join the newly elected John F. Kennedy administration.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Henry Morton Stanley locates missing explorer and missionary, David Livingstone in Ujiji, near Lake Tanganyika, famously greeting him with the words, "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?"
name: David Livingstone

text: Southern Airways Flight 49 from Birmingham, Alabama is hijacked and, at one point, is threatened with crashing into the nuclear installation at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After two days, the plane lands in Havana, Cuba, where the hijackers are jailed by Fidel Castro.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Tycho Brahe observes the supernova SN 1572.
name: Tycho Brahe

text: Adolf Hitler is arrested in Munich for high treason for his role in the Beer Hall Putsch.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Patent number US1781541 is awarded to Albert Einstein and Leó Szilárd for their invention, the Einstein refrigerator.
name: Albert Einstein

text: Leon Trotsky is expelled from the Soviet Communist Party, leaving Joseph Stalin in undisputed control of the Soviet Union.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: World War II: Soviet Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov arrives in Berlin to discuss the possibility of the Soviet Union joining the Axis Powers.
name: Vyacheslav Molotov

text: Iran hostage crisis: In response to the hostage situation in Tehran, U.S. President Jimmy Carter orders a halt to all petroleum imports into the United States from Iran.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: USSR: Yuri Andropov becomes the General Secretary of the Communist Party's Central Committee, succeeding Leonid I. Brezhnev.
name: Yuri Andropov

text: In New York City, American Airlines Flight 587, an Airbus A300 en route to the Dominican Republic, crashes minutes after takeoff from John F. Kennedy International Airport, killing all 260 on board and five on the ground.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: US President Jimmy Carter issues Executive Order 12170, freezing all Iranian assets in the United States in response to the hostage crisis.
name: Jimmy Carter

text: Lech Wałęsa, the leader of Poland's outlawed Solidarity movement, is released after eleven months of internment near the Soviet border.
name: Lech Wałęsa

text: Second Boer War: Battle of Chieveley, a British armored train is ambushed and partially derailed. British lose the battle, with 80 soldiers captured, along with war correspondent Winston Churchill.
name: Winston Churchill

text: The Holocaust: German SS leader Heinrich Himmler orders that Gypsies are to be put "on the same level as Jews and placed in concentration camps".
name: Heinrich Himmler

text: The Anglo-Irish Agreement is signed at Hillsborough Castle by British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and Irish Taoiseach Garret FitzGerald.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: While travelling during the Ninth Crusade, Prince Edward becomes King of England upon Henry III of England's death, but he will not return to England for nearly two years to assume the throne.
name: Henry III of England

text: King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden was killed at the Battle of Lützen during the Thirty Years' War.
name: Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden

text: David Livingstone becomes the first European to see the Victoria Falls in what is now Zambia-Zimbabwe.
name: David Livingstone

text: Henry VIII of England concludes the Treaty of Westminster, a pledge of mutual aid against the French, with Ferdinand II of Aragon.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: Elizabethan era begins: Queen Mary I of England dies and is succeeded by her half-sister Elizabeth I of England.
name: Elizabeth I of England

text: President John F. Kennedy dedicates Washington Dulles International Airport, serving the Washington, D.C., region.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Vietnam War: Acting on optimistic reports that he had been given on November 13, U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson tells the nation that, while much remained to be done, "We are inflicting greater losses than we're taking...We are making progress."
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Actor Arnold Schwarzenegger's tenure as the governor of California began.
name: Arnold Schwarzenegger

text: World War II: German leader Adolf Hitler and Italian Foreign Minister Galeazzo Ciano meet to discuss Benito Mussolini's disastrous Italian invasion of Greece.
name: Benito Mussolini

text: United States President John F. Kennedy sends 18,000 military advisors to South Vietnam.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: American Civil War: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address at the dedication ceremony for the military cemetery at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Cold War: In Geneva, U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet Union General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev meet for the first time.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Serbian communist representative and future Serbian and Yugoslav president Slobodan Milošević publicly declares that Serbia is under attack from Albanian separatists in Kosovo as well as internal treachery within Yugoslavia and a foreign conspiracy to destroy Serbia and Yugoslavia.
name: Slobodan Milošević

text: The French actress Sarah Bernhardt receives the press at the Savoy Hotel in New York at the outset of her first visit since 1896. She talked about her impending tour with a troupe of more than 50 performers and her plans to play the title role in Hamlet.
name: Sarah Bernhardt

text: Cuban Missile Crisis ends: In response to the Soviet Union agreeing to remove its missiles from Cuba, U.S. President John F. Kennedy ends the quarantine of the Caribbean nation.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat becomes the first Arab leader to officially visit Israel, when he meets Israeli prime minister Menachem Begin and speaks before the Knesset in Jerusalem, seeking a permanent peace settlement.
name: Menachem Begin

text: Andrei Chikatilo, one of the Soviet Union's most prolific serial killers, is arrested; he eventually confesses to 56 killings.
name: Andrei Chikatilo

text: The Danish astronomer Ole Rømer presents the first quantitative measurements of the speed of light.
name: Ole Rømer

text: Claude Monet's paintings shown at Gallery Durand-Ruel in Paris.
name: Claude Monet

text: Albert Einstein's paper that leads to the mass-energy equivalence formula, E = mc², is published in the journal Annalen der Physik.
name: Albert Einstein

text: World War II: Battle of Stalingrad: General Friedrich Paulus sends Adolf Hitler a telegram saying that the German 6th Army is surrounded.
name: Friedrich Paulus

text: World War II: Cairo Conference: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Chinese Premier Chiang Kai-shek meet in Cairo, Egypt, to discuss ways to defeat Japan.
name: Winston Churchill

text: U.S. President John F. Kennedy is assassinated and Texas Governor John Connally is seriously wounded by Lee Harvey Oswald, who also kills Dallas Police officer J. D. Tippit after fleeing the scene. Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson is sworn in as the 36th President of the United States afterwards.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Juan Carlos is declared King of Spain following the death of Francisco Franco.
name: Francisco Franco

text: British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher withdraws from the Conservative Party leadership election, confirming the end of her Prime-Ministership.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: John Milton publishes Areopagitica, a pamphlet decrying censorship.
name: John Milton

text: Edwin Hubble's discovery, that the Andromeda "nebula" is actually another island galaxy far outside our own Milky Way, is first published in The New York Times.
name: Edwin Hubble

text: Iran-Contra affair: Ronald Reagan signs the top secret National Security Decision Directive 17 (NSDD-17), giving the Central Intelligence Agency the authority to recruit and support Contra rebels in Nicaragua.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Queen lead singer Freddie Mercury announces in a statement that he is HIV-positive. He dies the following day.
name: Freddie Mercury

text: Theodosius I makes his adventus, or formal entry, into Constantinople.
name: Theodosius I

text: British naturalist Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species is published.
name: Charles Darwin

text: Lee Harvey Oswald, the assassin of President John F. Kennedy, is killed by Jack Ruby on live television. Robert H. Jackson takes a photograph of the shooting that will win the 1964 Pulitzer Prize in Photography.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Albert Einstein presents the field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences.
name: Albert Einstein

text: Agatha Christie's murder-mystery play The Mousetrap opens at the Ambassadors Theatre in London's West End after a premiere in Nottingham, UK.  It will become the longest continuously running play in history.
name: Agatha Christie

text: State funeral of John F. Kennedy; after lying in state at the United States Capitol, a Requiem Mass takes place at Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle and the President is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Pope John Paul II appoints Joseph Cardinal Ratzinger (the future Pope Benedict XVI) Prefect of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: In the Hawaiian Islands, Captain James Cook becomes the first European to visit Maui.
name: James Cook

text: A national Thanksgiving Day is observed in the United States as proclaimed by President George Washington at the request of Congress.
name: George Washington

text: United States President Abraham Lincoln proclaims November 26 as a national Thanksgiving Day, to be celebrated annually on the final Thursday of November.  Following the Franksgiving controversy from 1939 to 1941, it has been observed on the fourth Thursday in 1942 and subsequent years.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Casablanca, the movie starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, premieres in New York City.
name: Humphrey Bogart

text: Iran-Contra affair: U.S. President Ronald Reagan announces the members of what will become known as the Tower Commission.
name: Ronald Reagan

text: Emperor Marcus Aurelius grants his son Commodus the rank of "Imperator" and makes him Supreme Commander of the Roman legions.
name: Marcus Aurelius

text: At the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris, Alfred Nobel signs his last will and testament, setting aside his estate to establish the Nobel Prize after he dies.
name: Alfred Nobel

text: Also sprach Zarathustra by Richard Strauss is first performed.
name: Richard Strauss

text: Vietnam War: The Pentagon tells U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson that if planned operations are to succeed, the number of American troops in Vietnam has to be increased from 120,000 to 400,000.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Pope John Paul II returns the relics of Saint John Chrysostom to the Eastern Orthodox Church.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: In Stratford-upon-Avon, William Shakespeare and Anne Hathaway pay a £40 (equivalent to £14,557 in 2023) bond in lieu of posting wedding banns, which enables them to marry immediately.
name: William Shakespeare

text: At Gresham College, twelve men, including Christopher Wren, Robert Boyle, John Wilkins, and Sir Robert Moray decide to found what is later known as the Royal Society.
name: Christopher Wren

text: World War II: Tehran Conference: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin meet in Tehran, Iran, to discuss war strategy.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Vietnam War: National Security Council members agree to recommend that U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson adopt a plan for a two-stage escalation of bombing in North Vietnam.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Vietnam War: In response to U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson's call for "more flags" in Vietnam, Philippine President-elect Ferdinand Marcos announces he will send troops to help fight in South Vietnam.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher resigns as leader of the Conservative Party and, therefore, as Prime Minister. She is succeeded in both positions by John Major.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson establishes the Warren Commission to investigate the assassination of President John F. Kennedy.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Michael Jackson releases Thriller, the best-selling music album of all time.
name: Michael Jackson

text: Henry V of England enters Paris alongside his father-in-law King Charles VI of France.
name: Charles VI of France

text: Courtiers Christopher Hatton and Thomas Heneage are knighted by Queen Elizabeth I of England.
name: Elizabeth I of England

text: American Civil War: In his second State of the Union Address, President Abraham Lincoln reaffirms the necessity of ending slavery as ordered ten weeks earlier in the Emancipation Proclamation.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Sergei Kirov is assassinated, paving way for the repressive Great Purge, and Vinnytsia massacre by General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, Joseph Stalin.
name: Joseph Stalin

text: American Civil Rights Movement: In Montgomery, Alabama, seamstress Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat to a white man and is arrested for violating the city's racial segregation laws, an incident which leads to that city's bus boycott.
name: Rosa Parks

text: Patrice Lumumba is arrested by Mobutu Sese Seko's men on the banks of the Sankuru River, for inciting the army to rebellion.
name: Mobutu Sese Seko

text: Vietnam War: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson and his top-ranking advisers meet to discuss plans to bomb North Vietnam.
name: Lyndon B. Johnson

text: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 6231, another Boeing 727, crashes northwest of John F. Kennedy International Airport.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: St Paul's Cathedral, rebuilt to the design of Sir Christopher Wren following the Great Fire of London, is consecrated.
name: Christopher Wren

text: At Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris, Napoleon Bonaparte crowns himself Emperor of the French.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: French President Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte overthrows the Second Republic.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte becomes Emperor of the French as Napoleon III.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: At Tremont Temple in Boston, British author Charles Dickens gives his first public reading in the United States.
name: Charles Dickens

text: World War II: During the Manhattan Project, a team led by Enrico Fermi initiates the first artificial self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction.
name: Enrico Fermi

text: The Granma reaches the shores of Cuba's Oriente Province. Fidel Castro, Che Guevara and 80 other members of the 26th of July Movement disembark to initiate the Cuban Revolution.
name: Fidel Castro

text: In a nationally broadcast speech, Cuban leader Fidel Castro declares that he is a Marxist-Leninist and that Cuba will adopt Communism.
name: Fidel Castro

text: Vietnam War: After a trip to Vietnam at the request of U.S. President John F. Kennedy, U.S. Senate Majority Leader Mike Mansfield becomes the first American official to comment adversely on the war's progress.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Fidel Castro becomes President of Cuba, replacing Osvaldo Dorticós Torrado.
name: Fidel Castro

text: War of the Second Coalition: Battle of Hohenlinden: French General Jean Victor Marie Moreau decisively defeats the Archduke John of Austria near Munich. Coupled with First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte's earlier victory at Marengo, this will force the Austrians to sign an armistice and end the war.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: In a meeting off the coast of Malta, U.S. President George H. W. Bush and Soviet General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev release statements indicating that the Cold War between NATO and the Warsaw Pact may be coming to an end.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Kings Louis IX of France and Henry III of England agree to the Treaty of Paris, in which Henry renounces his claims to French-controlled territory on continental Europe (including Normandy) in exchange for Louis withdrawing his support for English rebels.
name: Henry III of England

text: At Fraunces Tavern in New York City, U.S. General George Washington bids farewell to his officers.
name: George Washington

text: World War II: In Yugoslavia, resistance leader Marshal Josip Broz Tito proclaims a provisional democratic Yugoslav government in-exile.
name: Josip Broz Tito

text: US Navy aircraft from USS John F. Kennedy and USS Independence attack Syrian missile sites in Lebanon in response to an F-14 being fired on by an SA-7. One A-6 Intruder and A-7 Corsair are shot down. One American pilot is killed, one is rescued, and one is captured.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: King Manuel I of Portugal issues a decree ordering the expulsion of Jews from the country.
name: Manuel I of Portugal

text: Thirteen-year-old Charles IX becomes king of France, with Queen Mother Catherine de' Medici as regent.
name: Catherine de' Medici

text: E. D. Nixon and Rosa Parks lead the Montgomery bus boycott.
name: Rosa Parks

text: German-born Swiss physicist Albert Einstein is granted an American visa.
name: Albert Einstein

text: Pope Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras I simultaneously revoke mutual excommunications that had been in place since 1054.
name: Pope Paul VI

text: Louis the Stammerer (son of Charles the Bald) is crowned king of the West Frankish Kingdom at Compiègne.
name: Louis the Stammerer

text: In his Apostolic constitution Ineffabilis Deus, Pope Pius IX proclaims the dogmatic definition of Immaculate Conception, which holds that the Blessed Virgin Mary was conceived free of Original Sin.
name: Pope Pius IX

text: Pope Pius IX promulgates the encyclical Quanta cura and its appendix, the Syllabus of Errors, outlining the authority of the Catholic Church and condemning various liberal ideas.
name: Pope Pius IX

text: Cold War: The Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty is signed by U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev in the White House.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: French physicist Augustin-Jean Fresnel, in a memoir read to the Academy of Sciences, coins the terms linear polarization, circular polarization, and elliptical polarization, and reports a direct refraction experiment verifying his theory that optical rotation is a form of birefringence.
name: Augustin-Jean Fresnel

text: Martin Luther burns his copy of the papal bull Exsurge Domine outside Wittenberg's Elster Gate.
name: Martin Luther

text: Isaac Newton's derivation of Kepler's laws from his theory of gravity, contained in the paper De motu corporum in gyrum, is read to the Royal Society by Edmond Halley.
name: Isaac Newton

text: The first Nobel Prize ceremony is held in Stockholm on the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.
name: Alfred Nobel

text: British Prime Minister Winston Churchill receives the Nobel Prize in Literature.
name: Winston Churchill

text: Arab-Israeli conflict: Prime Minister of Israel Menachem Begin and President of Egypt Anwar Sadat are jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
name: Menachem Begin

text: A surprise attack by forces under the command of Charles Emmanuel I, Duke of Savoy, and his brother-in-law, Philip III of Spain, is repelled by the citizens of Geneva. (Commemorated annually by the Fête de l'Escalade.)
name: Philip III of Spain

text: Glorious Revolution: James II of England, while trying to flee to France, throws the Great Seal of the Realm into the River Thames.
name: James II of England

text: French Revolution: King Louis XVI of France is put on trial for treason by the National Convention.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: Guglielmo Marconi transmits the first transatlantic radio signal from Poldhu, Cornwall, England to Saint John's, Newfoundland.
name: Guglielmo Marconi

text: Guglielmo Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal (the letter "S" [•••] in Morse Code), at Signal Hill in St John's, Newfoundland.
name: Guglielmo Marconi

text: The Lebensborn Project, a Nazi reproduction program, is founded by Heinrich Himmler.
name: Heinrich Himmler

text: The Holocaust: Adolf Hitler declares the imminent extermination of the Jews at a meeting in the Reich Chancellery.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Iraq War: Operation Red Dawn: Former Iraqi President Saddam Hussein is captured near his home town of Tikrit.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: Roald Amundsen's team, comprising himself, Olav Bjaaland, Helmer Hanssen, Sverre Hassel, and Oscar Wisting, becomes the first to reach the South Pole.
name: Roald Amundsen

text: Giacomo Puccini's comic opera Gianni Schicchi premieres at the Metropolitan Opera in New York City.
name: Giacomo Puccini

text: Symphony No. 9 ("From the New World" a.k.a. the "New World Symphony") by Antonín Dvořák premieres in a public afternoon rehearsal at Carnegie Hall in New York City, followed by a concert premiere on the evening of December 16.
name: Antonín Dvořák

text: Richard Pavlick is arrested for plotting to assassinate U.S. President-Elect John F. Kennedy.
name: John F. Kennedy

text: Eichmann trial: Adolf Eichmann is sentenced to death after being found guilty by an Israeli court of 15 criminal charges, including charges of crimes against humanity, crimes against the Jewish people, and membership of an outlawed organization.
name: Adolf Eichmann

text: U.S. President Jimmy Carter announces that the United States will recognize the People's Republic of China and sever diplomatic relations with the Republic of China (Taiwan).
name: Jimmy Carter

text: English Interregnum: The Protectorate: Oliver Cromwell becomes Lord Protector of the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland.
name: Oliver Cromwell

text: The Holocaust: Schutzstaffel chief Heinrich Himmler orders that Roma candidates for extermination be deported to Auschwitz.
name: Heinrich Himmler

text: Jeltoqsan: Riots erupt in Alma-Ata, Kazakh SSR, in response to Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev's dismissal of ethnic Kazakh Dinmukhamed Kunaev, the First Secretary of the Communist Party of Kazakhstan, and his replacement with Gennady Kolbin, an ethnic Russian from the Russian SFSR.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Margaret II, Countess of Hainaut and Holy Roman Empress and her son William I, Duke of Bavaria, sign a peace treaty ending the Hook and Cod wars.
name: William I

text: Pope Paul III excommunicates Henry VIII of England.
name: Henry VIII of England

text: The first account of a blood transfusion is published, in the form of a letter from physician Richard Lower to chemist Robert Boyle, in Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society
name: Robert Boyle

text: Simón Bolívar declares the independence of Gran Colombia in Angostura (now Ciudad Bolívar in Venezuela).
name: Simón Bolívar

text: First performance of the Unfinished Symphony by Franz Schubert.
name: Franz Schubert

text: Fernando Collor de Mello defeats Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the second round of the Brazilian presidential election, becoming the first democratically elected President in almost 30 years.
name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva

text: Kublai Khan renames his empire "Yuan" (元 yuán), officially marking the start of the Yuan dynasty of Mongolia and China.
name: Kublai Khan

text: Premiere performance of The Nutcracker by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky in Saint Petersburg, Russia.
name: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky

text: Henry II of England is crowned at Westminster Abbey.
name: Henry II of England

text: American Revolutionary War: George Washington's Continental Army goes into winter quarters at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania.
name: George Washington

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler appoints himself as head of the Oberkommando des Heeres.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: The Sino-British Joint Declaration, stating that China would resume the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong and the United Kingdom would restore Hong Kong to China with effect from July 1, 1997, is signed in Beijing by Deng Xiaoping and Margaret Thatcher.
name: Margaret Thatcher

text: Mikhail Gorbachev, leader of the Soviet Union, releases Andrei Sakharov and his wife from exile in Gorky.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: Richard I of England is captured and imprisoned by Leopold V of Austria on his way home to England after the Third Crusade.
name: Richard I of England

text: French presidential election: Having won the popular vote in a landslide, Louis Napoleon Bonaparte is inaugurated in the chamber of the National Assembly as the first (and only) president of the French Second Republic.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: Adolf Hitler is released from Landsberg Prison.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: Pope John Paul II announces the institution of World Youth Day.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: Medal of Honor: Public Resolution 82, containing a provision for a Navy Medal of Valor, is signed into law by President Abraham Lincoln.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: The Turkish fortress of Izmail is stormed and captured by Alexander Suvorov and his Russian armies.
name: Alexander Suvorov

text: Ludwig van Beethoven conducts and performs in concert at the Theater an der Wien, Vienna, with the premiere of his Fifth Symphony, Sixth Symphony, Fourth Piano Concerto and Choral Fantasy.
name: Ludwig van Beethoven

text: American Civil War: Savannah, Georgia, falls to the Union's Army of the Tennessee, and General Sherman tells President Abraham Lincoln: "I beg to present you as a Christmas gift the city of Savannah".
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: Itō Hirobumi, a samurai, becomes the first Prime Minister of Japan.
name: Itō Hirobumi

text: The Dreyfus affair begins in France, when Alfred Dreyfus is wrongly convicted of treason.
name: Alfred Dreyfus

text: World War II: Adolf Hitler signs the order to develop the V-2 rocket as a weapon.
name: Adolf Hitler

text: The pivotal Third Plenum of the 11th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party is held in Beijing, with Deng Xiaoping reversing Mao-era policies to pursue a program for Chinese economic reform.
name: Deng Xiaoping

text: Lech Wałęsa is elected President of Poland.
name: Lech Wałęsa

text: As part of the Glorious Revolution, King James II of England flees from England to Paris after being deposed in favor of his son-in-law and nephew, William of Orange and his daughter Mary.
name: James II of England

text: George Washington resigns as commander-in-chief of the Continental Army at the Maryland State House in Annapolis, Maryland.
name: George Washington

text: The novel Emma by Jane Austen is first published.
name: Jane Austen

text: The Tampere conference, where Vladimir Lenin and Joseph Stalin meet for the first time, is held in Tampere, Finland.
name: Vladimir Lenin

text: Kiritimati, also called Christmas Island, is discovered by James Cook.
name: James Cook

text: The Plot of the rue Saint-Nicaise fails to kill Napoleon Bonaparte.
name: Napoleon Bonaparte

text: World War II: Pope Pius XII makes a Christmas Eve appeal for peace.
name: Pope Pius XII

text: Vetranio meets Constantius II at Naissus (Serbia) and is forced to abdicate his imperial title. Constantius allows him to live as a private citizen on a state pension.
name: Constantius II

text: Count Roger II of Sicily is crowned the first king of Sicily.
name: Roger II of Sicily

text: Pope Pius IV is elected, four months after his predecessor's death.
name: Pope Pius IV

text: American Revolutionary War: General George Washington and the Continental Army cross the Delaware River at night to attack Hessian forces serving Great Britain at Trenton, New Jersey, the next day.
name: George Washington

text: Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin meets in Egypt with its president Anwar Sadat.
name: Menachem Begin

text: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as President of the Soviet Union (the union itself is dissolved the next day). Ukraine's referendum is finalized and Ukraine officially leaves the Soviet Union.
name: Mikhail Gorbachev

text: The opera Agrippina by George Frideric Handel premiered in Venice.
name: George Frideric Handel

text: American Revolutionary War: In the Battle of Trenton, the Continental Army under General George Washington executes a successful surprise attack and defeats a garrison of Hessian forces serving Great Britain.
name: George Washington

text: Louis XVI of France gives his public assent to Civil Constitution of the Clergy during the French Revolution.
name: Louis XVI of France

text: Henry Lee III's eulogy to George Washington in congress declares him as "first in war, first in peace and first in the hearts of his countrymen".
name: George Washington

text: Marie and Pierre Curie announce the isolation of radium.
name: Pierre Curie

text: British Prime Minister Winston Churchill addresses a joint meeting of the U.S. Congress.
name: Winston Churchill

text: World War II: George S. Patton's Third Army breaks the encirclement of surrounded U.S. forces at Bastogne, Belgium.
name: George S. Patton

text: Charles Darwin embarks on his journey aboard HMS Beagle, during which he will begin to formulate his theory of evolution.
name: Charles Darwin

text: Soviet General Secretary Joseph Stalin orders the "liquidation of the kulaks as a class".
name: Joseph Stalin

text: Pope John Paul II visits Mehmet Ali Ağca in Rebibbia's prison and personally forgives him for the 1981 attack on him in St. Peter's Square.
name: Pope John Paul II

text: World War II: Operation Anthropoid, the plot to assassinate high-ranking Nazi officer Reinhard Heydrich, commences.
name: Reinhard Heydrich

text: Reapers' War: Louis XIII of France swears the Catalan constitutions, being appointed Count of Barcelona and thus establishing the personal union of the Principality of Catalonia with the Kingdom of France.
name: Louis XIII of France

text: Former President of Iraq Saddam Hussein is executed.
name: Saddam Hussein

text: American Civil War: Abraham Lincoln signs an enabling act that would admit West Virginia to the Union, thus dividing Virginia in two.
name: Abraham Lincoln

text: World War II: The Royal Navy defeats the Kriegsmarine at the Battle of the Barents Sea. This leads to the resignation of Grand Admiral Erich Raeder a month later.
name: Erich Raeder

text: The first President of Russia, Boris Yeltsin, resigns from office, leaving Prime Minister Vladimir Putin as the acting President and successor.
name: Vladimir Putin

text: Michael VIII Palaiologos is proclaimed co-emperor of the Empire of Nicaea with his ward John IV Laskaris.
name: John IV Laskaris

text: Twenty-year-old Francis, Duke of Brittany, succeeds to the French throne following the death of his father-in-law, Louis XII.
name: Louis XII

text: Bouvet Island, the world's remotest island, is discovered by French explorer Jean-Baptiste Charles Bouvet de Lozier.
name: Jean-Baptiste Charles Bouvet de Lozier

text: The hymn that becomes known as "Amazing Grace", previously titled "1 Chronicles 17:16-17, Faith's Review and Expectation", is first used to accompany a sermon led by John Newton in the town of Olney, Buckinghamshire, England.
name: John Newton

text: American Revolutionary War: One thousand five hundred soldiers of the 6th Pennsylvania Regiment under General Anthony Wayne's command rebel against the Continental Army's winter camp in Morristown, New Jersey in the Pennsylvania Line Mutiny of 1781.
name: Anthony Wayne

text: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley (anonymously) publishes the pioneering work of science fiction, Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, in London.
name: Mary Wollstonecraft

text: Liberal forces supporting Benito Juárez enter Mexico City.
name: Benito Juárez

text: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom is proclaimed Empress of India.
name: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom

text: Twenty-five nations adopt Sandford Fleming's proposal for standard time (and also, time zones).
name: Sandford Fleming

text: The British colonies of New South Wales, Queensland, Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania, and Western Australia federate as the Commonwealth of Australia; Edmund Barton is appointed the first Prime Minister.
name: Edmund Barton

text: The Canadian Citizenship Act 1946 comes into effect, converting British subjects into Canadian citizens. Prime Minister William Lyon Mackenzie King becomes the first Canadian citizen.
name: William Lyon Mackenzie King

text: George Town, Penang, is made a city by a royal charter of Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Peruvian Javier Pérez de Cuéllar becomes the first Latin American to hold the title of Secretary-General of the United Nations.
name: Javier Pérez de Cuéllar

text: At least 60 people are killed and 200 injured in a stampede after celebrations at Félix Houphouët-Boigny Stadium in Abidjan, Ivory Coast.
name: Félix Houphouët-Boigny

text: The British Institution of Civil Engineers is founded by a group of six engineers; Thomas Telford would later become its first president.
name: Thomas Telford

text: Luis Muñoz Marín is inaugurated as the first democratically elected Governor of Puerto Rico.
name: Luis Muñoz Marín

text: Following the assassination of the Panamanian president José Antonio Remón Cantera, his deputy, José Ramón Guizado, takes power, but is quickly deposed after his involvement in Cantera's death is discovered.
name: José Ramón Guizado

text: One of the largest investigations by a British police force ends when serial killer Peter Sutcliffe, the "Yorkshire Ripper", is arrested in Sheffield, South Yorkshire.
name: Peter Sutcliffe

text: Joseph Jenkins Roberts is sworn in as the first president of Liberia.
name: Joseph Jenkins Roberts

text: World War II: US flying ace Major Greg "Pappy" Boyington is shot down in his Vought F4U Corsair by Captain Masajiro Kawato flying a Mitsubishi A6M Zero.
name: Pappy Boyington

text: United States invasion of Panama: Manuel Noriega, former leader of Panama, surrenders to American forces.
name: Manuel Noriega

text: Iranian General Qasem Soleimani is killed by an American airstrike near Baghdad International Airport, igniting global concerns of a potential armed conflict.
name: Qasem Soleimani

text: At least 91 people are killed in bombings in Kerman, Iran, during a ceremony commemorating the assassination of Iranian General Qasem Soleimani four years earlier.
name: Qasem Soleimani

text: Rose Heilbron becomes the first female judge to sit at the Old Bailey in London, UK.
name: Rose Heilbron

text: Mikheil Saakashvili is elected President of Georgia following the November 2003 Rose Revolution.
name: Mikheil Saakashvili

text: Ehud Olmert becomes acting Prime Minister of Israel after the incumbent, Ariel Sharon, suffers a second, apparently more serious stroke.
name: Ehud Olmert

text: Amy Johnson, a 37-year-old pilot and the first woman to fly solo from London to Australia, disappears after bailing out of her plane over the River Thames, and is presumed dead.
name: Amy Johnson

text: President of Georgia Zviad Gamsakhurdia flees the country as a result of the military coup.
name: Zviad Gamsakhurdia

text: Thomas Edison makes a kinetoscopic film of someone sneezing. On the same day, his employee, William Kennedy Dickson, receives a patent for motion picture film.
name: William Kennedy Dickson

text: Roger Lafontant, former leader of the Tonton Macoute in Haiti under François Duvalier, attempts a coup d'état, which ends in his arrest.
name: François Duvalier

text: The Fourth Republic of Ghana is inaugurated with Jerry Rawlings as president.
name: Jerry Rawlings

text: The longest U.S. House of Representatives speaker election since the December 1859 - February 1860 U.S. speaker election concludes and Kevin McCarthy is elected 55th Speaker of the United States House of Representatives.
name: Kevin McCarthy

text: Louis XII of France marries Anne of Brittany in accordance with a law set by his predecessor, Charles VIII.
name: Louis XII

text: Herman Hollerith is issued US patent #395,791 for the 'Art of Applying Statistics' — his punched card calculator.
name: Herman Hollerith

text: Kashf-e hijab decree is made and immediately enforced by Reza Shah, Iran's head of state, banning the wearing of Islamic veils in public.
name: Reza Shah

text: Andrei Zhdanov, Chairman of the Finnish Allied Commission, submitted to the Finnish War Criminal Court an interrogation report by General Erich Buschenhagen, a German prisoner of war, on the contacts between Finnish and German military personnel before the Continuation War and a copy of Hitler's Barbarossa plan.
name: Andrei Zhdanov

text: Bowing to international pressure, President of Pakistan Zulfikar Ali Bhutto releases Bengali leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman from prison, who had been arrested after declaring the independence of Bangladesh.
name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman

text: Ella T. Grasso becomes Governor of Connecticut, the first woman to serve as a Governor in the United States other than by succeeding her husband.
name: Ella T. Grasso

text: The RMS Queen Mary 2, then the largest ocean liner ever built, is christened by her namesake's granddaughter, Queen Elizabeth II.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Supporters of former Brazil president Jair Bolsonaro storm the Brazilian Congress.
name: Jair Bolsonaro

text: Jin-Song Wars: Invading Jurchen soldiers from the Jin dynasty besiege and sack Bianjing (Kaifeng), the capital of the Song dynasty of China, and abduct Emperor Qinzong of Song and others, ending the Northern Song period.
name: Emperor Qinzong of Song

text: The trial of Joan of Arc begins in Rouen.
name: Joan of Arc

text: British Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger introduces an income tax of two shillings to the pound to raise funds for Great Britain's war effort in the Napoleonic Wars.
name: William Pitt

text: The Portuguese prince Pedro I of Brazil decides to stay in Brazil against the orders of the Portuguese King João VI, beginning the Brazilian independence process.
name: Pedro I

text: Ernest Shackleton, leading the Nimrod Expedition to the South Pole, plants the British flag 97 nautical miles (180 km; 112 mi) from the South Pole, the farthest anyone had ever reached at that time.
name: Ernest Shackleton

text: Archbishop William Laud is beheaded for treason at the Tower of London.
name: William Laud

text: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman returns to the newly independent Bangladesh as president after spending over nine months in prison in Pakistan.
name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman

text: Taiping Rebellion: Hong Xiuquan proclaims the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, starting the Jintian Uprising.
name: Hong Xiuquan

text: Louis B. Mayer, head of film studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM), announces the creation of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, at a banquet in Los Angeles, California.
name: Louis B. Mayer

text: Amelia Earhart becomes the first person to fly solo from Hawaii to California.
name: Amelia Earhart

text: Violent protests occur in Bucharest, Romania, as two-day-old demonstrations continue against President Traian Băsescu's economic austerity measures. Clashes are reported in numerous Romanian cities between protesters and law enforcement officers.
name: Traian Băsescu

text: Japan Air Lines Cargo Flight 1045, a Douglas DC-8 jet, crashes onto the runway during takeoff from Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport, killing five.
name: Ted Stevens

text: Lee Teng-hui becomes the first native Taiwanese President of the Republic of China.
name: Lee Teng-hui

text: Douglas Wilder becomes the first elected African American governor as he takes office as Governor of Virginia in Richmond, Virginia.
name: Douglas Wilder

text: Treaty of Kiel: Frederick VI of Denmark cedes the Kingdom of Norway to Charles XIII of Sweden in return for Pomerania.
name: Charles XIII of Sweden

text: NBC's long-running morning news program Today debuts, with host Dave Garroway.
name: Dave Garroway

text: Queen Margrethe II of Denmark ascends the throne, the first Queen of Denmark since 1412 and the first Danish monarch not named Frederik or Christian since 1513.
name: Queen Margrethe II of Denmark

text: President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali of Tunisia seeks refuge in Saudi Arabia after a series of demonstrations against his regime, considered to be the birth of the Arab Spring.
name: Zine El Abidine Ben Ali

text: Queen Margrethe II abdicates as Queen of Denmark and is succeeded by her son, Frederik X.
name: Frederik X

text: War of 1812: American frigate USS President, commanded by Commodore Stephen Decatur, is captured by a squadron of four British frigates.
name: Stephen Decatur

text: Thomas Nast publishes a political cartoon  symbolizing the Democratic Party with a donkey ("A Live Jackass Kicking a Dead Lion") for Harper's Weekly.
name: Thomas Nast

text: James Naismith publishes the rules of basketball.
name: James Naismith

text: Elizabeth II, in her capacity as Queen of Australia, signs letters patent allowing Australia to become the first Commonwealth realm to institute its own Victoria Cross in its honours system.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Emir Abd-ar-Rahman III establishes the Caliphate of Córdoba.
name: Abd-ar-Rahman III

text: Edward I permits his mother Eleanor of Provence to expel the Jews from the towns Worcester, Marlborough, Cambridge and Gloucester.
name: Edward I

text: Ernest Shackleton's expedition finds the magnetic South Pole.
name: Ernest Shackleton

text: Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 205 crashes into the Atlantic Ocean near Astor Piazzolla International Airport in Mar del Plata, Argentina, killing 51.
name: Astor Piazzolla

text: War in Afghanistan: The UN Security Council unanimously establishes an arms embargo and the freezing of assets of Osama bin Laden, al-Qaeda, and the remaining members of the Taliban.
name: Osama bin Laden

text: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is sworn in as Liberia's new president. She becomes Africa's first female elected head of state.
name: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf

text: Swedish diplomat Raoul Wallenberg is taken into Soviet custody while in Hungary; he is never publicly seen again.
name: Raoul Wallenberg

text: Former Congolese Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba is murdered in circumstances suggesting the support and complicity of the governments of Belgium and the United States.
name: Patrice Lumumba

text: Capital punishment in the United States resumes after a ten-year hiatus, as convicted murderer Gary Gilmore is executed by firing squad in Utah.
name: Gary Gilmore

text: Ignacy Jan Paderewski becomes Prime Minister of the newly independent Poland.
name: Ignacy Jan Paderewski

text: Albert DeSalvo, the "Boston Strangler", is convicted of numerous crimes and is sentenced to life imprisonment.
name: Albert DeSalvo

text: The International Olympic Committee restores Jim Thorpe's Olympic medals to his family.
name: Jim Thorpe

text: Martin Luther King, Jr. Day is officially observed for the first time in all 50 US states.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: John Wilkes is expelled from the British House of Commons for seditious libel.
name: John Wilkes

text: Georges Claude patents the neon discharge tube for use in advertising.
name: Georges Claude

text: President Gerald Ford pardons Iva Toguri D'Aquino (a.k.a. "Tokyo Rose").
name: Iva Toguri D'Aquino

text: Turkish-Armenian journalist Hrant Dink is assassinated in front of his newspaper's Istanbul office by 17-year-old Turkish ultra-nationalist Ogün Samast.
name: Hrant Dink

text: Amílcar Cabral, leader of the independence movement in Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde, is assassinated in Conakry, Guinea.
name: Amílcar Cabral

text: In the United States, Martin Luther King Jr. Day is celebrated as a federal holiday for the first time.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Leabua Jonathan, Prime Minister of Lesotho, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by General Justin Lekhanya.
name: Leabua Jonathan

text: President of the Philippines Joseph Estrada is ousted in a nonviolent four-day revolution, and is succeeded by Gloria Macapagal Arroyo.
name: Gloria Macapagal Arroyo

text: Abdul Hamid I becomes Sultan of the Ottoman Empire and Caliph of Islam.
name: Abdul Hamid I

text: American lawyer and government official Alger Hiss is convicted of perjury.
name: Alger Hiss

text: Ramsay MacDonald becomes the first Labour Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
name: Ramsay MacDonald

text: Teddy Wakelam gives the first live radio commentary of a football match, between Arsenal F.C. and Sheffield United at Highbury.
name: Teddy Wakelam

text: In a bout for the world heavyweight boxing championship in Kingston, Jamaica, challenger George Foreman knocks down champion Joe Frazier six times in the first two rounds before the fight is stopped by referee Arthur Mercante.
name: Joe Frazier

text: Space Shuttle program: The space shuttle Discovery launches on STS-42 carrying Dr. Roberta Bondar, who becomes the first Canadian woman and the first neurologist in space.
name: Roberta Bondar

text: Evo Morales is inaugurated as President of Bolivia, becoming the country's first indigenous president.
name: Evo Morales

text: Georgetown College, the first Catholic university in the United States, is founded in Georgetown, Maryland (now a part of Washington, D.C.) when Bishop John Carroll, Rev. Robert Molyneux, and Rev. John Ashton purchase land for the proposed academy for the education of youth.
name: John Carroll

text: Elizabeth Blackwell is awarded her M.D. by the Geneva Medical College of Geneva, New York, becoming the United States' first female doctor.
name: Elizabeth Blackwell

text: Madeleine Albright becomes the first woman to serve as United States Secretary of State.
name: Madeleine Albright

text: U.S. journalist Daniel Pearl is kidnapped in Karachi, Pakistan and subsequently murdered.
name: Daniel Pearl

text: Walter Raleigh is knighted, shortly after renaming North America region "Virginia", in honor of Elizabeth I, Queen of England, sometimes referred to as the "Virgin Queen".
name: Walter Raleigh

text: The Wedding March by Felix Mendelssohn is played at the marriage of Queen Victoria's daughter, Victoria, and Friedrich of Prussia, and becomes a popular wedding processional.
name: Felix Mendelssohn

text: Nellie Bly completes her round-the-world journey in 72 days.
name: Nellie Bly

text: Brazilian Army captain Carlos Lamarca deserts in order to fight against the military dictatorship, taking with him ten machine guns and 63 rifles.
name: Carlos Lamarca

text: Idi Amin leads a coup deposing Milton Obote and becomes Uganda's president.
name: Milton Obote

text: American Civil War: General Ambrose Burnside is relieved of command of the Army of the Potomac after the disastrous Fredericksburg campaign. He is replaced by Joseph Hooker.
name: Joseph Hooker

text: Troops loyal to The Mahdi conquer Khartoum, killing the Governor-General Charles George Gordon.
name: Charles George Gordon

text: The first demonstration of the television by John Logie Baird.
name: John Logie Baird

text: World War II: Audie Murphy displays valor and bravery in action for which he will later be awarded the Medal of Honor.
name: Audie Murphy

text: JAT Flight 367 is destroyed by a terrorist bomb, killing 27 of the 28 people on board the DC-9. Flight attendant Vesna Vulović survives with critical injuries.
name: Vesna Vulović

text: Lewinsky scandal: On American television, U.S. President Bill Clinton denies having had "sexual relations" with former White House intern Monica Lewinsky.
name: Monica Lewinsky

text: Rioting breaks out in Antananarivo, Madagascar, sparking a political crisis that will result in the replacement of President Marc Ravalomanana with Andry Rajoelina.
name: Marc Ravalomanana

text: A Sikorsky S-76B flying from John Wayne Airport to Camarillo Airport crashes in Calabasas, 30 miles west of Los Angeles, killing all nine people on board, including five-time NBA champion Kobe Bryant and his daughter Gianna Bryant.
name: Kobe Bryant

text: A Russian expedition led by Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen and Mikhail Petrovich Lazarev discovers the Antarctic continent, approaching the Antarctic coast.
name: Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen

text: Modest Mussorgsky's opera Boris Godunov premieres in Mariinsky Theatre in St.Petersburg.
name: Modest Mussorgsky

text: Apollo program: Astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee are killed in a fire during a test of their Apollo 1 spacecraft at the Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
name: Ed White

text: In a military coup, Colonel Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara deposes the first democratically elected president of Niger, Mahamane Ousmane.
name: Mahamane Ousmane

text: Edward VI, the nine-year-old son of Henry VIII, becomes King of England on his father's death.
name: Edward VI

text: The Edict of Torda prohibits the persecution of individuals on religious grounds in John Sigismund Zápolya's Eastern Hungarian Kingdom.
name: John Sigismund Zápolya

text: The Russian Academy of Sciences is founded in St. Petersburg, Russia, by Peter the Great, and implemented by Senate decree. It is called the St. Petersburg Academy of Sciences until 1917.
name: Peter the Great

text: Sir Horace Walpole coins the word serendipity in a letter to a friend.
name: Horace Walpole

text: The Carnegie Institution of Washington is founded in Washington, D.C., with a $10 million gift from Andrew Carnegie.
name: Andrew Carnegie

text: The name Pakistan is coined by Choudhry Rahmat Ali Khan and is accepted by Indian Muslims who then thereby adopted it further for the Pakistan Movement seeking independence.
name: Choudhry Rahmat Ali

text: The World Land Speed Record on a public road is broken by Rudolf Caracciola in the Mercedes-Benz W125 Rekordwagen at a speed of 432.7 kilometres per hour (268.9 mph).
name: Rudolf Caracciola

text: Archduke Crown Prince Rudolf of Austria, heir to the Austro-Hungarian crown, is found dead with his mistress Baroness Mary Vetsera in the Mayerling.
name: Rudolf of Austria

text: In the United States, Civil Rights Movement leader Martin Luther King Jr.'s home is bombed in retaliation for the Montgomery bus boycott.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Eighty Years' War and Anglo-Spanish War: The Battle of Gembloux is a victory for Spanish forces led by Don John of Austria over a rebel army of Dutch, Flemish, English, Scottish, German, French and Walloons.
name: John of Austria

text: Gervasio Antonio de Posadas becomes Supreme Director of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata (present-day Argentina).
name: Gervasio Antonio de Posadas

text: Alvan Graham Clark discovers the white dwarf star Sirius B, a companion of Sirius, through an 18.5-inch (47 cm) telescope now located at Northwestern University.
name: Alvan Graham Clark

text: American Civil War: Confederate General Robert E. Lee becomes general-in-chief of all Confederate armies.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: Apollo program: Apollo 14: Astronauts Alan Shepard, Stuart Roosa, and Edgar Mitchell, aboard a Saturn V, lift off for a mission to the Fra Mauro Highlands on the Moon.
name: Alan Shepard

text: Fountains Valley, Pretoria, the oldest nature reserve in Africa, is proclaimed by President Paul Kruger.
name: Paul Kruger

text: La bohème premieres in Turin at the Teatro Regio (Turin), conducted by the young Arturo Toscanini.
name: Arturo Toscanini

text: Trygve Lie of Norway is picked to be the first United Nations Secretary-General.
name: Trygve Lie

text: Daniel Pearl, American journalist and South Asia Bureau Chief of The Wall Street Journal, kidnapped on January 23, is beheaded and mutilated by his captors.
name: Daniel Pearl

text: A coup d'état in Myanmar removes Aung San Suu Kyi from power and restores military rule.
name: Aung San

text: Translatio imperii: Pope John XII crowns Otto I, Holy Roman Emperor, the first Holy Roman Emperor in nearly 40 years.
name: Otto I

text: The Battle of Lincoln, at which Stephen, King of England is defeated and captured by the allies of Empress Matilda.
name: Empress Matilda

text: Brigham Young declares war on Timpanogos in the Battle at Fort Utah.
name: Brigham Young

text: The Seven Brothers (Seitsemän veljestä), a novel by Finnish author Aleksis Kivi, is published first time in several thin booklets.
name: Aleksis Kivi

text: Idi Amin replaces President Milton Obote as leader of Uganda.
name: Milton Obote

text: Rock and roll musicians Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and J. P. "The Big Bopper" Richardson are killed in a plane crash along with the pilot near Clear Lake, Iowa, an event later known as The Day the Music Died.
name: The Big Bopper

text: British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan speaks of "a wind of change", signalling that his Government was likely to support decolonisation.
name: Harold Macmillan

text: New York Police Officer Frank Serpico is shot during a drug bust in Brooklyn and survives to later testify against police corruption.
name: Frank Serpico

text: A military coup overthrows Alfredo Stroessner, dictator of Paraguay since 1954.
name: Alfredo Stroessner

text: Zhao Kuangyin declares himself Emperor Taizu of Song, ending the Later Zhou and beginning the Song dynasty.
name: Emperor Taizu of Song

text: John Marshall is sworn in as Chief Justice of the United States.
name: John Marshall

text: A coup d'état is led by Hugo Chávez against Venezuelan President Carlos Andrés Pérez.
name: Hugo Chávez

text: Facebook, a mainstream online social networking site, is founded by Mark Zuckerberg and Eduardo Saverin.
name: Eduardo Saverin

text: King Leopold II of Belgium establishes the Congo as a personal possession.
name: Leopold II of Belgium

text: Belgian chemist Leo Baekeland announces the creation of Bakelite, the world's first synthetic plastic.
name: Leo Baekeland

text: Charlie Chaplin, Mary Pickford, Douglas Fairbanks, and D. W. Griffith launch United Artists.
name: Mary Pickford

text: Manuel Noriega is indicted on drug smuggling and money laundering charges.
name: Manuel Noriega

text: Pope Francis becomes the first Pope in history to visit and perform papal mass in the Arabian Peninsula during his visit to Abu Dhabi.
name: Pope Francis

text: Elizabeth II becomes Queen of the United Kingdom and her other Realms and Territories and Head of the Commonwealth upon the death of her father, George VI. At the exact moment of succession, she was in a tree house at the Treetops Hotel in Kenya.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Haiti's first democratically elected president, Jean-Bertrand Aristide, is sworn in.
name: Jean-Bertrand Aristide

text: President Mohamed Nasheed of the Republic of Maldives resigns, after 23 days of anti-governmental protests calling for the release of the Chief Judge unlawfully arrested by the military.
name: Mohamed Nasheed

text: The Byzantine civil war of 1341-47 ends with a power-sharing agreement between John VI Kantakouzenos and John V Palaiologos.
name: John V Palaiologos

text: Sandford Fleming first proposes the adoption of Universal Standard Time at a meeting of the Royal Canadian Institute.
name: Sandford Fleming

text: Queen Elizabeth II issues an Order-in-Council, proclaiming the House of Windsor and declaring that her descendants will take the name Mountbatten-Windsor.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Nine protestors are killed at Charonne station, Paris, by French police under the command of ex-Vichy official and Parisian Prefect of Police Maurice Papon.
name: Maurice Papon

text: The Beatles make their first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show, performing before a record-setting audience of 73 million viewers across the United States.
name: Ed Sullivan

text: Satchel Paige becomes the first Negro league player to be voted into the USA's Baseball Hall of Fame.
name: Satchel Paige

text: In front of the high altar of Greyfriars Church in Dumfries, Robert the Bruce murders John Comyn, sparking the revolution in the Wars of Scottish Independence.
name: Robert the Bruce

text: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom marries Prince Albert of Saxe-Coburg-Gotha.
name: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom

text: In round 13 of a boxing match at New York City's Madison Square Garden, Primo Carnera knocks out Ernie Schaaf. Schaaf dies four days later.
name: Primo Carnera

text: Cold War: Captured American U2 spy-plane pilot Gary Powers is exchanged for captured Soviet spy Rudolf Abel.
name: Rudolf Abel

text: Ron Brown is elected chairman of the Democratic National Committee, becoming the first African American to lead a major American political party.
name: Ron Brown

text: IBM supercomputer Deep Blue defeats Garry Kasparov in chess for the first time.
name: Garry Kasparov

text: Guo Wei, a court official, leads a military coup and declares himself emperor of the new Later Zhou.
name: Guo Wei

text: Bernadette Soubirous's first vision of the Blessed Virgin Mary occurs in Lourdes, France.
name: Bernadette Soubirous

text: King Amadeo I of Spain abdicates, triggering the proclamation of the First Spanish Republic.
name: Amadeo I

text: LAPD Red Squad raid on John Reed Club art show in the U.S. results in the destruction of a dozen political artworks.
name: John Reed

text: Cold War: U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower denies all appeals for clemency for Julius and Ethel Rosenberg.
name: Ethel Rosenberg

text: Rebel East Timorese soldiers seriously wound President José Ramos-Horta. Rebel leader Alfredo Reinado is killed in the attack.
name: José Ramos-Horta

text: Arab Spring: The first wave of the Egyptian revolution culminates in the resignation of Hosni Mubarak and the transfer of power to the Supreme Military Council after 17 days of protests.
name: Hosni Mubarak

text: Santiago, Chile is founded by Pedro de Valdivia.
name: Pedro de Valdivia

text: Bernardo O'Higgins formally approves the Chilean Declaration of Independence near Concepción, Chile.
name: Bernardo O'Higgins

text: Pope Francis and Patriarch Kirill sign an Ecumenical Declaration in the first such meeting between leaders of the Catholic and Russian Orthodox Churches since their split in 1054.
name: Pope Francis

text: Emperor Otto I and Pope John XII co-sign the Diploma Ottonianum, recognizing John as ruler of Rome.
name: Otto I

text: The Treaty of Westminster is finalised between Edward IV of England and the Scottish Lord of the Isles.
name: Edward IV

text: With the accession of young Charles XI of Sweden, his regents begin negotiations to end the Second Northern War.
name: Charles XI of Sweden

text: The 13th Dalai Lama proclaims Tibetan independence following a period of domination by Manchu Qing dynasty and initiated a period of almost four decades of independence.
name: 13th Dalai Lama

text: Taiwan opposition leader Ma Ying-jeou resigns as the chairman of the Kuomintang party after being indicted on charges of embezzlement during his tenure as the mayor of Taipei; Ma also announces his candidacy for the 2008 presidential election.
name: Ma Ying-jeou

text: Wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Frederick V of the Palatinate at Whitehall Palace, London.
name: Frederick V

text: President Franklin D. Roosevelt meets King Ibn Saud of Saudi Arabia aboard the USS Quincy, officially beginning U.S.-Saudi diplomatic relations.
name: Saud of Saudi Arabia

text: Iranian leader Ruhollah Khomeini issues a fatwa encouraging Muslims to kill Salman Rushdie, author of The Satanic Verses.
name: Salman Rushdie

text: Iraq disarmament crisis: UNMOVIC Executive Chairman Hans Blix reports to the United Nations Security Council that disarmament inspectors have found no weapons of mass destruction in Ba'athist Iraq.
name: Hans Blix

text: In Beirut, 23 people, including former Prime Minister Rafic Hariri, are killed when the equivalent of around 1,000 kg of TNT is detonated while Hariri's motorcade drives through the city.
name: Rafic Hariri

text: The Roman Republic is proclaimed after Louis-Alexandre Berthier, a general of Napoleon, had invaded the city of Rome five days earlier.
name: Louis-Alexandre Berthier

text: In Miami, Giuseppe Zangara attempts to assassinate US President-elect Franklin D. Roosevelt, but instead shoots Chicago mayor Anton J. Cermak, who dies of his wounds on March 6.
name: Giuseppe Zangara

text: Paul Creston's Saxophone Sonata was officially premiered at the Carnegie Chamber Hall by saxophonist Cecil Leeson, who had commissioned it, and the composer.
name: Paul Creston

text: World War II: Fall of Singapore. Following an assault by Japanese forces, the British General Arthur Percival surrenders. About 80,000 Indian, United Kingdom and Australian soldiers become prisoners of war, the largest surrender of British-led military personnel in history.
name: Arthur Percival

text: Serial killer Jeffrey Dahmer is sentenced in Milwaukee to 15 terms of life in prison.
name: Jeffrey Dahmer

text: First Barbary War: Stephen Decatur leads a raid to burn the pirate-held frigate USS Philadelphia.
name: Stephen Decatur

text: Howard Carter unseals the burial chamber of Pharaoh Tutankhamun.
name: Howard Carter

text: Nicaraguan Contras leader Enrique Bermúdez is assassinated in Managua.
name: Enrique Bermúdez

text: Chaim Weizmann begins his term as the first President of Israel.
name: Chaim Weizmann

text: In Philadelphia, world champion Garry Kasparov beats the Deep Blue supercomputer in a chess match.
name: Garry Kasparov

text: George, Duke of Clarence, convicted of treason against his older brother Edward IV of England, is executed in private at the Tower of London.
name: Edward IV

text: Bulgarian revolutionary leader Vasil Levski is executed by hanging in Sofia by the Ottoman authorities.
name: Vasil Levski

text: While studying photographs taken in January, Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto.
name: Clyde Tombaugh

text: A thousand armed soldiers raid Kalakuta Republic, the commune of Nigerian singer Fela Kuti, leading to the death of Funmilayo Anikulapo Kuti.
name: Fela Kuti

text: Richard Petty wins a then-record sixth Daytona 500 after leaders Donnie Allison and Cale Yarborough crash on the final lap of the first NASCAR race televised live flag-to-flag.
name: Cale Yarborough

text: WikiLeaks publishes the first of hundreds of thousands of classified documents disclosed by the soldier now known as Chelsea Manning.
name: Chelsea Manning

text: British explorer William Smith discovers the South Shetland Islands.
name: William Smith

text: Pedro Lascuráin becomes President of Mexico for 45 minutes; this is the shortest term to date of any person as president of any country.
name: Pedro Lascuráin

text: The publication of Betty Friedan's The Feminine Mystique reawakens the feminist movement in the United States as women's organizations and consciousness raising groups spread.
name: Betty Friedan

text: Orkney and Shetland are pawned by Norway to Scotland in lieu of a dowry for Margaret of Denmark.
name: Margaret of Denmark

text: Edward VI of England is crowned King of England at Westminster Abbey.
name: Edward VI

text: Manuel Belgrano defeats the royalist army of Pío de Tristán during the Battle of Salta.
name: Manuel Belgrano

text: William Buckland formally announces the name Megalosaurus, the first scientifically validly named non-avian dinosaur species.
name: William Buckland

text: The Saturday Evening Post publishes the first of Norman Rockwell's Four Freedoms in support of United States President Franklin Roosevelt's 1941 State of the Union address theme of Four Freedoms.
name: Norman Rockwell

text: Mercury program: While aboard Friendship 7, John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit the Earth, making three orbits in four hours, 55 minutes.
name: John Glenn

text: An Englishman raised in Australia, Bob Fitzsimmons, fought an Irishman, Peter Maher, in an American promoted event which technically took place in Mexico, winning the 1896 World Heavyweight Championship in boxing.
name: Bob Fitzsimmons

text: Rezā Shāh takes control of Tehran during a successful coup.
name: Reza Shah

text: Aldrich Ames is arrested by the Federal Bureau of Investigation for selling national secrets to the Soviet Union in Arlington County, Virginia.
name: Aldrich Ames

text: Ferdinando II de' Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany, the dedicatee, receives the first printed copy of Galileo's Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems.
name: Ferdinando II de' Medici

text: Filipino forces led by General Antonio Luna launch counterattacks for the first time against the American forces during the Philippine-American War. The Filipinos fail to regain Manila from the Americans.
name: Antonio Luna

text: World War II: Members of the White Rose resistance, Sophie Scholl, Hans Scholl, and Christoph Probst are executed in Nazi Germany.
name: Hans Scholl

text: Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam survives a communist shooting assassination attempt in Buôn Ma Thuột.
name: Ngô Đình Diệm

text: The notorious Broadway flop Moose Murders opens and closes on the same night at the Eugene O'Neill Theatre.
name: Eugene O'Neill

text: Aldrich Ames and his wife are charged by the United States Department of Justice with spying for the Soviet Union.
name: Aldrich Ames

text: Angolan political and rebel leader Jonas Savimbi is killed in a military ambush.
name: Jonas Savimbi

text: Charles Martin Hall produced the first samples of aluminium from the electrolysis of aluminium oxide, after several years of intensive work. He was assisted in this project by his older sister, Julia Brainerd Hall.
name: Charles Martin Hall

text: Kurdish rebel leader Abdullah Öcalan is charged with treason in Ankara, Turkey.
name: Abdullah Öcalan

text: Battle of Karnal: The army of Iranian ruler Nader Shah defeats the forces of the Mughal emperor of India, Muhammad Shah.
name: Muhammad Shah

text: London's Drury Lane Theatre burns to the ground, leaving its owner, Irish writer and politician Richard Brinsley Sheridan, destitute.
name: Richard Brinsley Sheridan

text: Nancy Astor becomes the first woman to speak in the House of Commons of the United Kingdom following her election as a Member of Parliament (MP) three months earlier.
name: Nancy Astor

text: Ghanaian coup d'état by National Liberation Council overthrows Kwame Nkrumah's Government
name: Kwame Nkrumah

text: Philippine President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo declares Proclamation 1017 placing the country in a state of emergency in attempt to subdue a possible military coup.
name: Gloria Macapagal Arroyo

text: Mahathir Mohamad resigns as Prime Minister of Malaysia following an attempt to replace the Pakatan Harapan government, which triggered the 2020-2022 Malaysian political crisis.
name: Mahathir Mohamad

text: Marie-Adélaïde, the eldest of six daughters of Guillaume IV, becomes the first reigning Grand Duchess of Luxembourg.
name: Marie-Adélaïde

text: In a coup d'état led by Klement Gottwald, the Communist Party of Czechoslovakia takes control of government in Prague to end the Third Czechoslovak Republic.
name: Klement Gottwald

text: The government of Suriname is overthrown by a military coup led by Dési Bouterse.
name: Dési Bouterse

text: Battle of Benevento: An army led by Charles, Count of Anjou, defeats a combined German and Sicilian force led by Manfred, King of Sicily. Manfred is killed in the battle and Pope Clement IV invests Charles as king of Sicily and Naples.
name: Pope Clement IV

text: Argentine War of Independence: Manuel Belgrano raises the Flag of Argentina in the city of Rosario for the first time.
name: Manuel Belgrano

text: Poet Lord Byron gives his first address as a member of the House of Lords, in defense of Luddite violence against Industrialism in his home county of Nottinghamshire.
name: Lord Byron

text: King George I of Greece survives an assassination attempt.
name: George I of Greece

text: Vietnam War: Two dissident Republic of Vietnam Air Force pilots bomb the Independence Palace in Saigon in a failed attempt to assassinate South Vietnam President Ngô Đình Diệm.
name: Ngô Đình Diệm

text: Russian politician Boris Nemtsov is assassinated in Moscow while out walking with his girlfriend.
name: Boris Nemtsov

text: Elias Lönnrot signed and dated the first version of the Kalevala, the so-called foreword to the Old Kalevala.
name: Elias Lönnrot

text: The British election ended in a hung parliament after the Jeremy Thorpe-led Liberal Party achieved their biggest vote share since 1929.
name: Jeremy Thorpe

text: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF) agents raid the Branch Davidian church in Waco, Texas with a warrant to arrest the group's leader David Koresh, starting a 51-day standoff.
name: David Koresh

text: For her performance as Mammy in Gone with the Wind, Hattie McDaniel becomes the first African American to win an Academy Award.
name: Hattie McDaniel

text: Gordie Howe of the Hartford Whalers makes NHL history as he scores his 800th goal.
name: Gordie Howe

text: South African archbishop Desmond Tutu is arrested along with 100 other clergymen during a five-day anti-apartheid demonstration in Cape Town.
name: Desmond Tutu

text: Svend Robinson becomes the first member of the House of Commons of Canada to come out as gay.
name: Svend Robinson

text: Jean-Bertrand Aristide is removed as president of Haiti following a coup.
name: Jean-Bertrand Aristide

text: The United Kingdom's Ministry of Defence withdraws Prince Harry from a tour of Afghanistan after news of his deployment is leaked to foreign media.
name: Prince Harry

text: Sarah Good, Sarah Osborne, and Tituba are brought before local magistrates in Salem Village, Massachusetts, beginning what would become known as the Salem witch trials.
name: Sarah Good

text: Justice Samuel Chase is acquitted at the end of his impeachment trial before the U.S. Senate.
name: Samuel Chase

text: Henri Becquerel discovers radioactive decay.
name: Henri Becquerel

text: The Australian cricket team captained by Warwick Armstrong becomes the first team to complete a whitewash of The Ashes, something that would not be repeated for 86 years.
name: Warwick Armstrong

text: Cold War: Klaus Fuchs is convicted of spying for the Soviet Union by disclosing top secret atomic bomb data.
name: Klaus Fuchs

text: President of Pakistan Yahya Khan indefinitely postpones the pending national assembly session, precipitating massive civil disobedience in East Pakistan.
name: Yahya Khan

text: Provisional Irish Republican Army member Bobby Sands begins his hunger strike in HM Prison Maze.
name: Bobby Sands

text: George of Poděbrady is chosen as the king of Bohemia.
name: George of Poděbrady

text: Burgundian Wars: The Old Swiss Confederacy hands Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, a major defeat in the Battle of Grandson in Canton of Neuchâtel.
name: Charles the Bold

text: The College of Arms is formally incorporated by Royal Charter signed by King Richard III of England.
name: Richard III of England

text: Norodom Sihanouk, king of Cambodia, abdicates the throne in favor of his father, Norodom Suramarit.
name: Norodom Sihanouk

text: In Burma, the army led by General Ne Win seizes power in a coup d'état.
name: Ne Win

text: Wilt Chamberlain sets the single-game scoring record in the National Basketball Association by scoring 100 points.
name: Wilt Chamberlain

text: An amateur video captures the beating of Rodney King by Los Angeles police officers.
name: Rodney King

text: Yang Jian declares himself Emperor Wen of Sui, ending the Northern Zhou and beginning the Sui dynasty.
name: Emperor Wen of Sui

text: Wars of the Roses in England: Lancastrian King Henry VI is deposed by his House of York cousin, who then becomes King Edward IV.
name: Edward IV

text: John Flamsteed is appointed the first Astronomer Royal of England.
name: John Flamsteed

text: Jeannette Rankin of Montana becomes the first female member of the United States House of Representatives.
name: Jeannette Rankin

text: Nationalist leader Robert Mugabe wins a sweeping election victory to become Zimbabwe's first black prime minister.
name: Robert Mugabe

text: Nik Wallenda becomes the first person to walk over the Masaya Volcano in Nicaragua.
name: Nik Wallenda

text: King Henry VII of England issues letters patent to John Cabot and his sons, authorising them to explore unknown lands.
name: Henry VII

text: Mefistofele, an opera by Arrigo Boito, receives its premiere performance at La Scala.
name: Arrigo Boito

text: Pope Francis begins a historical visit to Iraq amidst the COVID-19 pandemic.
name: Pope Francis

text: Texas Revolution: Battle of the Alamo: After a thirteen-day siege by an army of 3,000 Mexican troops, the 187 Texas volunteers, including frontiersman Davy Crockett and colonel Jim Bowie, defending the Alamo are killed and the fort is captured.
name: Davy Crockett

text: Norman Rockwell published Freedom from Want in The Saturday Evening Post with a matching essay by Carlos Bulosan as part of the Four Freedoms series.
name: Norman Rockwell

text: Nation of Islam leader Elijah Muhammad officially gives boxing champion Cassius Clay the name Muhammad Ali.
name: Elijah Muhammad

text: Forbes names Jeff Bezos as the world's richest person, for the first time, at $112 billion net worth.
name: Jeff Bezos

text: Shrigley abduction: 15-year old Ellen Turner is abducted by Edward Gibbon Wakefield, a future figure in the establishment of colonies in South Australia and New Zealand.
name: Edward Gibbon Wakefield

text: Second Boer War: Boers, led by Koos de la Rey, defeat the British at the Battle of Tweebosch.
name: Koos de la Rey

text: Korean War: Operation Ripper: United Nations troops led by General Matthew Ridgway begin an assault against Chinese forces.
name: Matthew Ridgway

text: Iran and the United Kingdom break diplomatic relations after a fight over Salman Rushdie and his controversial novel, The Satanic Verses.
name: Salman Rushdie

text: Following the death of his mother, queen Urraca of León, Alfonso VII is proclaimed king of León.
name: Alfonso VII

text: French aviator Raymonde de Laroche becomes the first woman to receive a pilot's license.
name: Raymonde de Laroche

text: A supposed failed assassination attempt on Islamic cleric Sayyed Mohammad Hussein Fadlallah in Beirut, Lebanon kills 80 and injures 200 others.
name: Mohammad Hussein Fadlallah

text: Headlined by Hulk Hogan and Ric Flair, TNA Wrestling moved its flagship program, TNA Impact!, to Monday night. This effort to go "big time live" failed but is notable in the history of professional wrestling television.
name: Ric Flair

text: Paraguayan forces defeat Manuel Belgrano at the Battle of Tacuarí.
name: Manuel Belgrano

text: Francis Ronalds describes the first battery-operated clock in the Philosophical Magazine.
name: Francis Ronalds

text: Two Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil helicopters collide in mid-air over Villa Castelli, Argentina, killing all 10 people on board both aircraft, including French athletes Florence Arthaud, Camille Muffat and Alexis Vastine, as well as producers and guests for the French TV show Dropped.
name: Camille Muffat

text: Giuseppe Conte, Prime Minister of Italy, announces in a televised address and signs the decree imposing the first nationwide COVID-19 lockdown in the world.
name: Giuseppe Conte

text: The Later Han is founded by Liu Zhiyuan. He declares himself emperor.
name: Liu Zhiyuan

text: French "Sun King" Louis XIV begins his personal rule of France after the death of his premier, the Cardinal Mazarin.
name: Louis XIV

text: Mildred Gillars ("Axis Sally") is convicted of treason.
name: Mildred Gillars

text: John Gorton resigns as Prime Minister of Australia and the leader of the Liberal Party of Australia after a secret ballot vote of confidence, being replaced in both positions by William McMahon.
name: John Gorton

text: Arnošt of Pardubice becomes the last Bishop of Prague (3 March 1343 O.S.), and, a year later, the first Archbishop of Prague.
name: Arnošt of Pardubice

text: Louis-Hippolyte Lafontaine and Robert Baldwin become the first Prime Ministers of the Province of Canada to be democratically elected under a system of responsible government.
name: Robert Baldwin

text: World War I: Mesopotamian campaign: Baghdad falls to Anglo-Indian forces commanded by General Frederick Stanley Maude.
name: Frederick Stanley

text: Rudolf Höss, the first commandant of Auschwitz concentration camp, is captured by British troops.
name: Rudolf Höss

text: Bob Hawke is appointed Prime Minister of Australia.
name: Bob Hawke

text: Economist and businessman Sebastián Piñera is sworn in as President of Chile. Aftershocks of the 2010 Pichilemu earthquakes hit central Chile during the ceremony.
name: Sebastián Piñera

text: The 1971 Turkish military memorandum is sent to the Süleyman Demirel government of Turkey and the government resigns.
name: Süleyman Demirel

text: Zoran Đinđić, Prime Minister of Serbia, is assassinated in Belgrade.
name: Zoran Đinđić

text: Harvard College is named after clergyman John Harvard.
name: John Harvard

text: Gustav IV Adolf of Sweden is deposed in the Coup of 1809.
name: Gustav IV Adolf of Sweden

text: Pope Leo XII publishes the apostolic constitution Quo Graviora in which he renewed the prohibition on Catholics joining freemasonry.
name: Pope Leo XII

text: Felix Mendelssohn's Violin Concerto receives its première performance in Leipzig with Ferdinand David as soloist.
name: Felix Mendelssohn

text: The Battle of Điện Biên Phủ begins with an artillery barrage by Viet Minh forces under Võ Nguyên Giáp; Viet Minh victory led to the end of the First Indochina War and French withdrawal from Vietnam.
name: Võ Nguyên Giáp

text: The New Jewel Movement, headed by Maurice Bishop, ousts the Prime Minister of Grenada, Eric Gairy, in a coup d'état.
name: Eric Gairy
