text: The 2013 papal conclave elects Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio taking the name Pope Francis as the 266th Pope of the Catholic Church.
name: Pope Francis

text: According to his own account, Otto von Guericke completes his book Experimenta Nova (ut vocantur) Magdeburgica de Vacuo Spatio, detailing his experiments on vacuum and his discovery of electrostatic repulsion.
name: Otto von Guericke

text: Admiral Sir John Byng is executed by firing squad aboard HMS Monarch for breach of the Articles of War.
name: John Byng

text: The Mikado, a light opera by W. S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan, receives its first public performance at the Savoy Theatre in London.
name: Arthur Sullivan

text: King Gustav III of Sweden is shot; he dies on March 29.
name: Gustav III of Sweden

text: The 7th and 10th US cavalry regiments under John J. Pershing cross the US-Mexico border to join the hunt for Pancho Villa.
name: John J. Pershing

text: Assassination of Kamal Jumblatt, the main leader of the anti-government forces in the Lebanese Civil War.
name: Kamal Jumblatt

text: Former Italian Prime Minister Aldo Moro is kidnapped; he is later murdered by his captors.
name: Aldo Moro

text: The Troubles: Ulster loyalist militant Michael Stone attacks a Provisional IRA funeral in Belfast with pistols and grenades. Three persons, one of them a member of PIRA are killed, and more than 60 others are wounded.
name: Michael Stone

text: American activist Rachel Corrie is killed in Rafah by being run over by an Israel Defense Forces bulldozer while trying to obstruct the demolition of a home.
name: Rachel Corrie

text: The Female Relief Society of Nauvoo is formally organized with Emma Smith as president.
name: Emma Smith

text: A plane crash in Cebu, Philippines kills Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay and 24 others.
name: Ramon Magsaysay

text: Serial killer Richard Ramirez, aka the "Night Stalker", commits the first two murders in his Los Angeles murder spree.
name: Richard Ramirez

text: Leader of the House of Commons and Lord President of the Council, Robin Cook, resigns from the British Cabinet in disagreement with government plans for the 2003 invasion of Iraq.
name: Robin Cook

text: King George I of Greece is assassinated in the recently liberated city of Thessaloniki.
name: George I of Greece

text: Frederick III of Habsburg is the last Holy Roman Emperor crowned by medieval tradition in Rome by Pope Nicholas V.
name: Nicholas V

text: Louis Riel declares a provisional government in Saskatchewan, beginning the North-West Rebellion.
name: Louis Riel

text: The first President of Kazakhstan, Nursultan Nazarbayev, resigns from office after nearly three decades, leaving Senate Chairman Kassym-Jomart Tokayev as the acting President and successor.
name: Nursultan Nazarbayev

text: Sir Walter Raleigh is freed from the Tower of London after 13 years of imprisonment.
name: Walter Raleigh

text: German revolutions of 1848-49: King Ludwig I of Bavaria abdicates.
name: Ludwig I of Bavaria

text: Harriet Beecher Stowe's Uncle Tom's Cabin is published.
name: Harriet Beecher Stowe

text: Ferdinand Marcos's widow, Imelda Marcos, goes on trial for bribery, embezzlement, and racketeering.
name: Imelda Marcos

text: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev is sworn in as acting president of Kazakhstan, following the resignation of long-time president Nursultan Nazarbayev.
name: Nursultan Nazarbayev

text: On the day of his execution in Oxford, former archbishop of Canterbury Thomas Cranmer deviates from the scripted sermon by renouncing the recantations he has made and adds, "And as for the pope, I refuse him, as Christ's enemy, and Antichrist with all his false doctrine."
name: Thomas Cranmer

text: Syngman Rhee is removed from office after being impeached as the President of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea.
name: Syngman Rhee

text: Shah of Iran Reza Shah Pahlavi formally asks the international community to call Persia by its native name, Iran.
name: Reza Shah

text: Alan Freed presents the Moondog Coronation Ball, the first rock and roll concert, in Cleveland, Ohio.
name: Alan Freed

text: Martin Luther King Jr. leads 3,200 people on the start of the third and finally successful civil rights march from Selma to Montgomery, Alabama.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Debi Thomas became the first African American to win the World Figure Skating Championships.
name: Debi Thomas

text: Anne Hutchinson is expelled from Massachusetts Bay Colony for religious dissent.
name: Anne Hutchinson

text: Before the Société pour L'Encouragement à l'Industrie, brothers Auguste and Louis Lumière demonstrate movie film technology publicly for the first time.
name: Louis Lumière

text: Karl Wallenda of The Flying Wallendas dies after falling off a tight-rope suspended between two hotels in San Juan, Puerto Rico.
name: Karl Wallenda

text: The Special Counsel investigation on the 2016 United States presidential election concludes when Robert Mueller submits his report to the United States Attorney General.
name: Robert Mueller

text: The Ahmadiyya Muslim Community is established by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in Qadian, British India.
name: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad

text: Bhagat Singh, Shivaram Rajguru and Sukhdev Thapar are hanged for the killing of a deputy superintendent of police during the Indian independence movement.
name: Bhagat Singh

text: The first of The Nixon Interviews (12 will be recorded over four weeks) is videotaped with British journalist David Frost interviewing former United States President Richard Nixon about the Watergate scandal and the Nixon tapes.
name: David Frost

text: Archbishop Óscar Romero of El Salvador gives his famous speech appealing to men of the El Salvadoran armed forces to stop killing the Salvadorans.
name: Óscar Romero

text: Guatemala's government, headed by Fernando Romeo Lucas García is overthrown in a military coup by right-wing General Efraín Ríos Montt.
name: Efraín Ríos Montt

text: The Revolutionary United Front, with support from the special forces of Charles Taylor's National Patriotic Front of Liberia, invades Sierra Leone in an attempt to overthrow Joseph Saidu Momoh, sparking the 11-year Sierra Leone Civil War.
name: Joseph Saidu Momoh

text: Taiwan holds its first direct elections and chooses Lee Teng-hui as President.
name: Lee Teng-hui

text: President of Peru Pedro Pablo Kuczynski resigns from the presidency amid a mass corruption scandal before certain impeachment by the opposition-majority Congress of Peru.
name: Pedro Pablo Kuczynski

text: Prime Minister Boris Johnson put the United Kingdom into its first national lockdown in response to COVID-19.
name: Boris Johnson

text: Direct rule is imposed on Northern Ireland by the Government of the United Kingdom under Edward Heath.
name: Edward Heath

text: In Argentina, the armed forces overthrow the constitutional government of President Isabel Perón and start a seven-year dictatorial period self-styled the National Reorganization Process.
name: Isabel Perón

text: Morarji Desai became the Prime Minister of India, the first Prime Minister not to belong to Indian National Congress.
name: Morarji Desai

text: El Salvadorian Archbishop Óscar Romero is assassinated while celebrating Mass in San Salvador.
name: Óscar Romero

text: Bangladeshi President Abdus Sattar is deposed in a bloodless coup led by Army Chief Lieutenant general Hussain Muhammad Ershad, who suspends the Constitution and imposes martial law.
name: Hussain Muhammad Ershad

text: Fatimid caliph al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah assassinates the eunuch chief minister Barjawan and assumes control of the government.
name: Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah

text: Robert the Bruce becomes King of Scots (Scotland).
name: Robert the Bruce

text: Sir Walter Raleigh is granted a patent to colonize Virginia.
name: Walter Raleigh

text: On the anniversary of Greek Independence, Alexandros Papanastasiou proclaims the Second Hellenic Republic.
name: Alexandros Papanastasiou

text: Civil rights activists led by Martin Luther King Jr. successfully complete their 4-day 50-mile (80 km) march from Selma to the capitol in Montgomery, Alabama.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Faisal of Saudi Arabia is shot and killed by his nephew.
name: Faisal of Saudi Arabia

text: WikiWikiWeb, the world's first wiki, and part of the Portland Pattern Repository, is made public by Ward Cunningham.
name: Ward Cunningham

text: The death of the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah, kept secret for six weeks, is announced, along with the succession of his son, al-Zahir li-i'zaz Din Allah.
name: Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah

text: Guru Amar Das becomes the Third Sikh guru.
name: Guru Amar Das

text: William Dampier is the first European to circumnavigate New Britain, discovering it is an island (which he names Nova Britannia) rather than part of New Guinea.
name: William Dampier

text: The Métis people of the District of Saskatchewan under Louis Riel begin the North-West Rebellion against Canada.
name: Louis Riel

text: Jiang Zemin is appointed President of the People's Republic of China.
name: Jiang Zemin

text: The foundation stone of Valletta, Malta's capital city, is laid by Jean Parisot de Valette, Grand Master of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta.
name: Jean Parisot de Valette

text: First concert of the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra, conducted by Otto Nicolai.
name: Otto Nicolai

text: Henri Fabre becomes the first person to fly a seaplane, the Fabre Hydravion, after taking off from water runway Étang le Barre, near Marseille.
name: Henri Fabre

text: General John J. Pershing, during World War I, cancels 42nd 'Rainbow' Division's orders to Rolampont for further training and diverted it to the occupy the Baccarat sector. Rainbow Division becomes "the first American division to take over an entire sector on its own, which it held longer than any other American division-occupied sector alone for a period of three months".
name: John J. Pershing

text: Greek poet and Nobel Prize laureate Giorgos Seferis makes a famous statement on the BBC World Service opposing the junta in Greece.
name: Giorgos Seferis

text: United States President George H. W. Bush posthumously awards Jesse Owens the Congressional Gold Medal.
name: Jesse Owens

text: Battle of Towton: Edward of York defeats Queen Margaret to become King Edward IV of England, bringing a temporary stop to the Wars of the Roses.
name: Edward IV

text: King Gustav III of Sweden dies after being shot in the back at a midnight masquerade ball at Stockholm's Royal Opera 13 days earlier.
name: Gustav III of Sweden

text: King Gustav IV Adolf of Sweden abdicates after a coup d'état.
name: Gustav IV Adolf of Sweden

text: Sepoy Mangal Pandey of the 34th Regiment, Bengal Native Infantry mutinies against the East India Company's rule in India and inspires the protracted Indian Rebellion of 1857, also known as the Sepoy Mutiny.
name: Mangal Pandey

text: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg are convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage.
name: Ethel Rosenberg

text: The Canada Act 1982 receives the Royal Assent from Queen Elizabeth II, setting the stage for the Queen of Canada to proclaim the Constitution Act, 1982.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Edward I sacks Berwick-upon-Tweed, during armed conflict between Scotland and England.
name: Edward I

text: Guru Gobind Singh establishes the Khalsa in Anandpur Sahib, Punjab.
name: Guru Gobind Singh

text: Discovery of the chemical elements: Sir William Crookes announces his discovery of thallium.
name: William Crookes

text: Second Sino-Japanese War: Japan declares Nanking capital of a new Chinese puppet government, nominally controlled by Wang Jingwei.
name: Wang Jingwei

text: Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, flees Tibet for India.
name: Tenzin Gyatso

text: Pope Francis visits Morocco.
name: Pope Francis

text: A Transcontinental & Western Air airliner crashes near Bazaar, Kansas, killing eight, including University of Notre Dame head football coach Knute Rockne.
name: Knute Rockne

text: Selena is murdered by her fan club president Yolanda Saldívar at a Days Inn in Corpus Christi, Texas.
name: Yolanda Saldívar

text: The dwarf planet Makemake is discovered by a team led by astronomer Michael E. Brown at the Palomar Observatory.
name: Michael E. Brown

text: American Civil War: Union troops led by Philip Sheridan decisively defeat Confederate troops led by George Pickett, cutting the Army of Northern Virginia's last supply line during the Siege of Petersburg.
name: Philip Sheridan

text: Project Tiger, a tiger conservation project, is launched in the Jim Corbett National Park, India.
name: Jim Corbett

text: After the mysterious death of Empress Zewditu, Haile Selassie is proclaimed emperor of Ethiopia.
name: Haile Selassie

text: Prince Norodom Sihanouk resigns as leader of Cambodia and is placed under house arrest.
name: Norodom Sihanouk

text: In New York, Mafia boss John Gotti is convicted of murder and racketeering and is later sentenced to life in prison.
name: John Gotti

text: Japanese Lt. General Masaharu Homma is executed in the Philippines for leading the Bataan Death March.
name: Masaharu Homma

text: Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his "I've Been to the Mountaintop" speech; he was assassinated the next day.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: A United States Air Force Boeing T-43 crashes near Dubrovnik Airport in Croatia, killing 35, including Secretary of Commerce Ron Brown.
name: Ron Brown

text: Napoleon abdicates (conditionally) for the first time and names his son Napoleon II as Emperor of the French, followed by unconditional abdication two days later.
name: Napoleon II

text: Argonia, Kansas elects Susanna M. Salter as the first female mayor in the United States.
name: Susanna M. Salter

text: Bye Bye Birdie, a musical romantic comedy film directed by George Sidney, was released.
name: George Sidney

text: Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his "Beyond Vietnam: A Time to Break Silence" speech in New York City's Riverside Church.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Dr. Denton Cooley implants the first temporary artificial heart.
name: Denton Cooley

text: In the Battle of Maipú, Chile's independence movement, led by Bernardo O'Higgins and José de San Martín, win a decisive victory over Spain, leaving 2,000 Spaniards and 1,000 Chilean patriots dead.
name: Bernardo O'Higgins

text: In Sri Lanka, Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna launches a revolt against the United Front government of Sirimavo Bandaranaike.
name: Sirimavo Bandaranaike

text: Alberto Fujimori, president of Peru, dissolves the Peruvian congress by military force.
name: Alberto Fujimori

text: At the Cape of Good Hope, Dutch sailor Jan van Riebeeck establishes a resupply camp that eventually becomes Cape Town.
name: Jan van Riebeeck

text: King Buddha Yodfa Chulaloke (Rama I) of Siam (modern day Thailand) establishes the Chakri dynasty.
name: Rama I

text: John Jacob Astor incorporates the American Fur Company, that would eventually make him America's first millionaire.
name: John Jacob Astor

text: American Civil War: The Battle of Shiloh begins: In Tennessee, forces under Union General Ulysses S. Grant meet Confederate troops led by General Albert Sidney Johnston.
name: Albert Sidney Johnston

text: American Civil War: The Battle of Sailor's Creek: Confederate General Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia fights and loses its last major battle while in retreat from Richmond, Virginia, during the Appomattox Campaign.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: Members of Cameroon's Republican Guard unsuccessfully attempt to overthrow the government headed by Paul Biya.
name: Paul Biya

text: Empress Matilda becomes the first female ruler of England, adopting the title "Lady of the English".
name: Empress Matilda

text: Felix V abdicates his claim to the papacy, ending the reign of the final Antipope.
name: Felix V

text: Thomas D'Arcy McGee, one of the Canadian Fathers of Confederation, is assassinated by a Fenian activist.
name: Thomas D'Arcy McGee

text: Two-time Formula One British World Champion Jim Clark dies in an accident during a Formula Two race in Hockenheim.
name: Jim Clark

text: Soviet Defense Minister Dmitry Yazov orders the Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan.
name: Dmitry Yazov

text: Haitian president Jean-Bertrand Aristide demands reparations of $21 billion from France for the Haiti Independence Debt.
name: Jean-Bertrand Aristide

text: Former Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori is sentenced to 25 years in prison for ordering killings and kidnappings by security forces.
name: Alberto Fujimori

text: The city of Oulu, Finland, is founded by Charles IX of Sweden.
name: Charles IX of Sweden

text: A team of computer manufacturers, users, and university people led by Grace Hopper meets to discuss the creation of a new programming language that would be called COBOL.
name: Grace Hopper

text: Hank Aaron passes Babe Ruth as the all-time leader in career home runs by hitting his 715th home run off of Al Downing at Atlanta-Fulton County Stadium.
name: Babe Ruth

text: American Civil War: Robert E. Lee surrenders the Army of Northern Virginia (26,765 troops) to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House, Virginia, effectively ending the war.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: African-American singer Marian Anderson gives a concert at the Lincoln Memorial after being denied the use of Constitution Hall by the Daughters of the American Revolution.
name: Marian Anderson

text: Dr. Hendrik Verwoerd, Prime Minister of South Africa and architect of apartheid, narrowly survives an assassination attempt by a white farmer, David Pratt in Johannesburg.
name: Hendrik Verwoerd

text: A U.S. Federal Court finds former Panamanian dictator Manuel Noriega guilty of drug and racketeering charges. He is sentenced to 30 years in prison.
name: Manuel Noriega

text: In Tbilisi, Georgia, up to 60,000 people protest against the government of Mikheil Saakashvili.
name: Mikheil Saakashvili

text: Ludovico Sforza is captured by Swiss troops at Novara and is handed over to the French.
name: Ludovico Sforza

text: American Civil War: A day after his surrender to Union forces, Confederate General Robert E. Lee addresses his troops for the last time.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: India: Arya Samaj is founded in Mumbai by Swami Dayananda Saraswati to propagate his goal of social reform.
name: Dayananda Saraswati

text: 1896 Summer Olympics: The Olympic marathon is run ending with the victory of Greek athlete Spyridon Louis.
name: Spyridon Louis

text: Rudolf Vrba and Alfréd Wetzler escape from Birkenau death camp.
name: Rudolf Vrba

text: Imprisoned IRA hunger striker Bobby Sands was elected to Westminster as the MP for Fermanagh and South Tyrone, Northern Ireland. He died twenty-six days later.
name: Bobby Sands

text: War of the League of Cambrai: Franco-Ferrarese forces led by Gaston de Foix and Alfonso I d'Este win the Battle of Ravenna against the Papal-Spanish forces.
name: Alfonso I d'Este

text: Former shōgun Tokugawa Yoshinobu surrenders Edo Castle to Imperial forces, marking the end of the Tokugawa shogunate.
name: Tokugawa Yoshinobu

text: Over two hundred thousand people march in Caracas towards the presidential palace to demand the resignation of President Hugo Chávez. Nineteen protesters are killed.
name: Hugo Chávez

text: Sir Frank Whittle ground-tests the first jet engine designed to power an aircraft, at Rugby, England.
name: Frank Whittle

text: The polio vaccine, developed by Dr. Jonas Salk, is declared safe and effective.
name: Jonas Salk

text: Canadian runner and athlete, Terry Fox begins his Marathon of Hope Run in St. John's, NF
name: Terry Fox

text: Jim Gary's "Twentieth Century Dinosaurs" exhibition opens at the Smithsonian Institution National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C. He is the only sculptor ever invited to present a solo exhibition there.
name: Jim Gary

text: Samuel Argall, having captured Pocahontas in Passapatanzy, Virginia, sets off with her to Jamestown with the intention of exchanging her for English prisoners held by her father.
name: Samuel Argall

text: The Sikh religion is formalised as the Khalsa - the brotherhood of Warrior-Saints - by Guru Gobind Singh in northern India, in accordance with the Nanakshahi calendar.
name: Guru Gobind Singh

text: Lajos Kossuth presents the Hungarian Declaration of Independence in a closed session of the National Assembly.
name: Lajos Kossuth

text: The 31 March Incident leads to the overthrow of Sultan Abdul Hamid II.
name: Abdul Hamid II

text: Jallianwala Bagh massacre: British Indian Army troops led by Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer kill approximately 379-1,000 unarmed demonstrators including men and women in Amritsar, India; and approximately 1,500 injured.
name: Reginald Dyer

text: At the Academy Awards, Sidney Poitier becomes the first African-American man to win the Best Actor award for the 1963 film Lilies of the Field.
name: Sidney Poitier

text: In England, the Yorkists under Edward IV defeat the Lancastrians under the Earl of Warwick at the Battle of Barnet; the Earl is killed and Edward resumes the throne.
name: Edward IV

text: Hungary declares itself independent of Austria with Lajos Kossuth as its leader.
name: Lajos Kossuth

text: The inaugural Monaco Grand Prix takes place in the Principality of Monaco. William Grover-Williams wins driving a Bugatti Type 35.
name: William Grover-Williams

text: The Second Spanish Republic is proclaimed and King Alfonso XIII goes to exile. Meanwhile, in Barcelona, Francesc Macià proclaims the Catalan Republic.
name: Francesc Macià

text: Gnassingbé Eyadéma overthrows Nicolas Grunitzky and installs himself as the new President of Togo, a title he will hold for the next 38 years.
name: Nicolas Grunitzky

text: Venezuelan president Hugo Chávez returns to office two days after being ousted and arrested by the country's military.
name: Hugo Chávez

text: Thomas Hopkins Gallaudet and Laurent Clerc found the American School for the Deaf (then called the Connecticut Asylum for the Education and Instruction of Deaf and Dumb Persons), the first American school for deaf students, in Hartford, Connecticut.
name: Thomas Hopkins Gallaudet

text: Jackie Robinson debuts for the Brooklyn Dodgers, breaking baseball's color line.
name: Jackie Robinson

text: McDonald's restaurant dates its founding to the opening of a franchised restaurant by Ray Kroc, in Des Plaines, Illinois.
name: Ray Kroc

text: At Shaw University in Raleigh, North Carolina, Ella Baker leads a conference that results in the creation of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee, one of the principal organizations of the civil rights movement in the 1960s.
name: Ella Baker

text: Upon Hu Yaobang's death, the Tiananmen Square protests of 1989 begin in China.
name: Hu Yaobang

text: In Dodge City, Kansas, Bat Masterson fights his last gun battle.
name: Bat Masterson

text: Harriet Quimby becomes the first woman to fly an airplane across the English Channel.
name: Harriet Quimby

text: Bernard Baruch first applies the term "Cold War" to describe the relationship between the United States and the Soviet Union.
name: Bernard Baruch

text: U.S. civil rights campaigner Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. writes his open letter from Birmingham Jail, sometimes known as "The Negro Is Your Brother", while incarcerated in Birmingham, Alabama, for protesting against segregation.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Virginia Tech shooting: Seung-Hui Cho murders 32 people and injures 17 before committing suicide.
name: Seung-Hui Cho

text: The trial for Anders Behring Breivik, the perpetrator of the 2011 Norway attacks, begins in Oslo, Norway.
name: Anders Behring Breivik

text: The New York Times and the New Yorker win the Pulitzer Prize for Public Service for breaking news of the Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse scandal.
name: Harvey Weinstein

text: French prisoner of war General Henri Giraud escapes from his castle prison in Königstein Fortress.
name: Henri Giraud

text: Constitution Act, 1982 Patriation of the Canadian constitution in Ottawa by Proclamation of Elizabeth II, Queen of Canada.
name: Elizabeth II

text: The funeral of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, takes place at St George's Chapel, Windsor Castle.
name: Prince Philip

text: Bona Sforza is crowned as queen consort of Poland.
name: Bona Sforza

text: Bostonians rise up in rebellion against Sir Edmund Andros.
name: Edmund Andros

text: American Revolution: The British Army advances up the Charles River in Massachusetts to destroy supplies of American militias, while Paul Revere and other riders rapidly warn the countryside.
name: Paul Revere

text: World War I: French pilot Roland Garros is shot down and glides to a landing on the German side of the lines.
name: Roland Garros

text: Jackie Robinson makes his regular season debut for the Montreal Royals of the International League, to make them the first integrated modern professional baseball team.
name: Jackie Robinson

text: King Mswati III of Swaziland announces that his country's name will change to Eswatini.
name: Mswati III

text: Mae West is sentenced to ten days in jail for obscenity for her play Sex.
name: Mae West

text: Students in South Korea hold a nationwide pro-democracy protest against president Syngman Rhee, eventually forcing him to resign.
name: Syngman Rhee

text: Sierra Leone becomes a republic, and Siaka Stevens the president.
name: Siaka Stevens

text: English Admiral Robert Blake destroys a Spanish silver fleet, under heavy fire from the shore, at the Battle of Santa Cruz de Tenerife.
name: Robert Blake

text: American Civil War: Robert E. Lee resigns his commission in the United States Army in order to command the forces of the state of Virginia.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: Columbine High School massacre: Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold kill 14 people and injure 23 others before committing suicide at Columbine High School in Columbine, Colorado.
name: Eric Harris

text: Henry VIII ascends the throne of England on the death of his father, Henry VII.
name: Henry VII

text: Rastafari movement: Haile Selassie of Ethiopia visits Jamaica, an event now celebrated as Grounation Day.
name: Haile Selassie

text: Tiananmen Square protests of 1989: In Beijing, around 100,000 students gather in Tiananmen Square to commemorate Chinese reform leader Hu Yaobang.
name: Hu Yaobang

text: The Supreme Court in La Paz, Bolivia, sentences former dictator Luis García Meza to 30 years in jail without parole for murder, theft, fraud and violating the constitution.
name: Luis García

text: British yachtsman Sir Robin Knox-Johnston wins the Sunday Times Golden Globe Race and completes the first solo non-stop circumnavigation of the world.
name: Robin Knox-Johnston

text: The Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM) is founded in Ankara. The assembly denounces the government of Sultan Mehmed VI and announces the preparation of a temporary constitution.
name: Mehmed VI

text: Joshua Slocum, the first person to sail single-handedly around the world, sets sail from Boston, Massachusetts aboard the sloop Spray.
name: Joshua Slocum

text: Ernest Shackleton and five men of the Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition launch a lifeboat from uninhabited Elephant Island in the Southern Ocean to organise a rescue for the crew of the sunken Endurance.
name: Ernest Shackleton

text: Thorvald Stauning becomes premier of Denmark (first term).
name: Thorvald Stauning

text: Civil war breaks out in the Dominican Republic when Colonel Francisco Caamaño overthrows the triumvirate that had been in power since the coup d'état against Juan Bosch.
name: Juan Bosch

text: Vietnam War: American General William Westmoreland says in a news conference that the enemy had "gained support in the United States that gives him hope that he can win politically that which he cannot win militarily".
name: William Westmoreland

text: The Gambia becomes a republic within the Commonwealth of Nations, with Dawda Jawara as its first President.
name: Dawda Jawara

text: Transition from Ming to Qing: The Chongzhen Emperor, the last Emperor of Ming China, commits suicide during a peasant rebellion led by Li Zicheng.
name: Li Zicheng

text: "La Marseillaise" (the French national anthem) is composed by Claude Joseph Rouget de Lisle.
name: Claude Joseph Rouget de Lisle

text: American Civil War: Forces under U.S. Admiral David Farragut demand the surrender of the Confederate city of New Orleans, Louisiana.
name: David Farragut

text: Violeta Chamorro takes office as the President of Nicaragua, the first woman to hold the position.
name: Violeta Chamorro

text: Sybil Ludington, aged 16, allegedly rode 40 miles (64 km) to alert American colonial forces to the approach of British regular forces
name: Sybil Ludington

text: The first clinical trials of Jonas Salk's polio vaccine begin in Fairfax County, Virginia.
name: Jonas Salk

text: Forced out by the April Revolution, President of South Korea Syngman Rhee resigns after 12 years of dictatorial rule.
name: Syngman Rhee

text: Nursultan Nazarbayev is re-elected President of Kazakhstan with 97.7% of the vote, one of the biggest vote shares in Kazakhstan's history.
name: Nursultan Nazarbayev

text: First War of Scottish Independence: John Balliol's Scottish army is defeated by an English army commanded by John de Warenne, 6th Earl of Surrey at the Battle of Dunbar.
name: John de Warenne

text: The Saur Revolution begins in Afghanistan, ending the following morning with the murder of Afghan President Mohammed Daoud Khan and the establishment of the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan.
name: Mohammed Daoud Khan

text: South African medical researcher Max Theiler develops the yellow fever vaccine at the Rockefeller Foundation in New York City.
name: Max Theiler

text: Thor Heyerdahl and five crew mates set out from Peru on the Kon-Tiki to demonstrate that Peruvian natives could have settled Polynesia.
name: Thor Heyerdahl

text: Former Central Intelligence Agency counterintelligence officer and analyst Aldrich Ames pleads guilty to giving US secrets to the Soviet Union and later Russia.
name: Aldrich Ames

text: Port Arthur massacre, Tasmania: A gunman, Martin Bryant, opens fire at the Broad Arrow Cafe in Port Arthur, Tasmania, killing 35 people and wounding 23 others.
name: Martin Bryant

text: Joan of Arc arrives to relieve the Siege of Orléans.
name: Joan of Arc

text: American Civil War: The Capture of New Orleans by Union forces under David Farragut.
name: David Farragut

text: American Civil War: The Siege of Corinth begins as Union forces under General Henry Halleck moves to engage Confederate forces led by General P. G. T. Beauregard.
name: P. G. T. Beauregard

text: Riots in Los Angeles begin, following the acquittal of police officers charged with excessive force in the beating of Rodney King. Over the next three days 63 people are killed and hundreds of buildings are destroyed.
name: Rodney King

text: J. J. Thomson of the Cavendish Laboratory announces his discovery of the electron as a subatomic particle, over 1,800 times smaller than a proton (in the atomic nucleus), at a lecture at the Royal Institution in London.
name: J. J. Thomson

text: Formula One racing driver Roland Ratzenberger is killed in a crash during the qualifying session of the San Marino Grand Prix run at Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari outside Imola, Italy.
name: Roland Ratzenberger

text: Canonization of Faustina Kowalska in the presence of 200,000 people and the first Divine Mercy Sunday celebrated worldwide.
name: Faustina Kowalska

text: Willem-Alexander is inaugurated as King of the Netherlands following the abdication of Beatrix.
name: Willem-Alexander

text: Christopher Columbus presents his plans discovering a western route to the Indies to the Spanish Queen Isabella I of Castile.
name: Isabella I of Castile

text: The polio vaccine developed by Jonas Salk is made available to the public.
name: Jonas Salk

text: Cold War: U-2 incident: Francis Gary Powers, in a Lockheed U-2 spyplane, is shot down over the Sverdlovsk Oblast, Soviet Union, sparking a diplomatic crisis.
name: Francis Gary Powers

text: Japan's Naomi Uemura, travelling by dog sled, becomes the first person to reach the North Pole alone.
name: Naomi Uemura

text: Three-time Formula One champion Ayrton Senna is killed in an accident during the San Marino Grand Prix.
name: Ayrton Senna

text: The body of British climber George Mallory is found on Mount Everest, 75 years after his disappearance in 1924.
name: George Mallory

text: Afonso Mendes, appointed by Pope Gregory XV as Latin Patriarch of Ethiopia, arrives at Beilul from Goa.
name: Pope Gregory XV

text: Osama bin Laden, the suspected mastermind behind the September 11 attacks and the FBI's most wanted man, is killed by the United States Navy SEALs in Abbottabad, Pakistan.
name: Osama bin Laden

text: A total solar eclipse is visible across northern Europe and northern Asia, as predicted by Edmond Halley to within four minutes accuracy.
name: Edmond Halley

text: The All India Forward Bloc is formed by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
name: Subhas Chandra Bose

text: Walter O'Malley, the owner of the Brooklyn Dodgers, agrees to move the team from Brooklyn to Los Angeles.
name: Walter O'Malley

text: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War: The Battle of Seringapatam: The siege of Seringapatam ends when the city is invaded and Tipu Sultan killed by the besieging British army, under the command of General George Harris.
name: Tipu Sultan

text: Daimyō (Lord) Shimazu Tadatsune of the Satsuma Domain in southern Kyūshū, Japan, completes his successful invasion of the Ryūkyū Kingdom in Okinawa.
name: Shimazu Tadatsune

text: Cinco de Mayo: Troops led by Ignacio Zaragoza halt a French invasion in the Battle of Puebla in Mexico.
name: Ignacio Zaragoza

text: Pitching against the Philadelphia Athletics at the Huntington Avenue Grounds, Cy Young of the Boston Americans throws the first perfect game in the modern era of baseball.
name: Cy Young

text: Emperor Haile Selassie returns to Addis Ababa; the country commemorates the date as Liberation Day or Patriots' Victory Day.
name: Haile Selassie

text: Project Mercury: Alan Shepard becomes the first American to travel into outer space, on a sub-orbital flight.
name: Alan Shepard

text: Bobby Sands dies in the Long Kesh prison hospital after 66 days of hunger-striking, aged 27.
name: Bobby Sands

text: Louis XIV of France moves his court to the Palace of Versailles.
name: Louis XIV

text: Captain Thomas Cochrane in the 14-gun HMS Speedy captures the 32-gun Spanish frigate El Gamo.
name: Thomas Cochrane

text: The East India Company disbands the 34th Regiment of Bengal Native Infantry whose sepoy Mangal Pandey had earlier revolted against the British in the lead up to the War of Indian Independence.
name: Mangal Pandey

text: Thomas Henry Burke and Lord Frederick Cavendish are stabbed to death by Fenian assassins in Phoenix Park, Dublin.
name: Lord Frederick Cavendish

text: Babe Ruth, then a pitcher for the Boston Red Sox, hits his first major league home run.
name: Babe Ruth

text: Twenty-one Lebanese nationalists are executed in Martyrs' Square, Beirut by Djemal Pasha.
name: Djemal Pasha

text: The Deutsche Studentenschaft attacked Magnus Hirschfeld's Institut für Sexualwissenschaft, later burning many of its books.
name: Magnus Hirschfeld

text: At California's March Field, Bob Hope performs his first USO show.
name: Bob Hope

text: Roger Bannister becomes the first person to run the mile in under four minutes.
name: Roger Bannister

text: Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom and French President François Mitterrand officiate at the opening of the Channel Tunnel.
name: Elizabeth II

text: The body of former CIA director William Colby is found washed up on a riverbank in southern Maryland, eight days after he disappeared.
name: William Colby

text: Kerry Wood strikes out 20 Houston Astros to tie the major league record held by Roger Clemens. He threw a one-hitter and did not walk a batter in his fifth career start.
name: Roger Clemens

text: Dutch politician Pim Fortuyn is assassinated following a radio-interview at the Mediapark in Hilversum.
name: Pim Fortuyn

text: Inaugural celebrations begin at Louis XIV of France's new Palace of Versailles.
name: Louis XIV

text: The city of New Orleans is founded by Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne, Sieur de Bienville.
name: Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne

text: In Saint Petersburg, Russian scientist Alexander Stepanovich Popov demonstrates to the Russian Physical and Chemical Society his invention, the Popov lightning detector—a primitive radio receiver. In some parts of the former Soviet Union the anniversary of this day is celebrated as Radio Day.
name: Alexander Stepanovich Popov

text: Canadian Patrick Morrow becomes the first person to climb each of the Seven Summits.
name: Patrick Morrow

text: Joan of Arc lifts the Siege of Orléans, turning the tide of the Hundred Years' War.
name: Joan of Arc

text: Pharmacist John Pemberton first sells a carbonated beverage named "Coca-Cola" as a patent medicine.
name: John Pemberton

text: The first ascent of Mount Everest without supplemental oxygen, by Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler.
name: Peter Habeler

text: The 2025 papal conclave elects Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost taking the name Pope Leo XIV as the 267th Pope of the Catholic Church.
name: Pope Leo XIV

text: American Civil War: Nathan Bedford Forrest surrenders his forces at Gainesville, Alabama.
name: Nathan Bedford Forrest

text: Carlos Lamarca leads the first urban guerrilla action against the military dictatorship of Brazil in São Paulo, by robbing two banks.
name: Carlos Lamarca

text: Iranian Jewish businessman Habib Elghanian is executed by firing squad in Tehran, prompting the mass exodus of the once 100,000-strong Jewish community of Iran.
name: Habib Elghanian

text: Scottish nobles recognize the authority of Edward I of England pending the selection of a king.
name: Edward I

text: Great Northern War: The Russian Navy led by Admiral Fyodor Apraksin land both at Katajanokka and Hietalahti during the Battle of Helsinki.
name: Fyodor Apraksin

text: American Revolutionary War: A small Colonial militia led by Ethan Allen and Colonel Benedict Arnold captures Fort Ticonderoga.
name: Ethan Allen

text: A revolt broke out in southern Vietnam against Emperor Minh Mang, who had desecrated the deceased mandarin Le Van Duyet.
name: Minh Mạng

text: Astor Place Riot: A riot breaks out at the Astor Opera House in Manhattan, New York City over a dispute between actors Edwin Forrest and William Charles Macready, killing at least 22 and injuring over 120.
name: Edwin Forrest

text: American Civil War: In Kentucky, Union soldiers ambush and mortally wound Confederate raider William Quantrill, who lingers until his death on June 6.
name: William Quantrill

text: Victoria Woodhull becomes the first woman nominated for President of the United States.
name: Victoria Woodhull

text: Sailing in the lifeboat James Caird, Ernest Shackleton arrives at South Georgia after a journey of 800 nautical miles from Elephant Island.
name: Ernest Shackleton

text: J. Edgar Hoover is appointed first Director of the United States' Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and remains so until his death in 1972.
name: J. Edgar Hoover

text: Queen Elizabeth II misses the State Opening of Parliament for the first time in 59 years. It was the first time that a new session of Parliament was opened by the Prince of Wales and the Duke of Cambridge acting as Counsellors of State.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Constantine the Great dedicates the much-expanded and rebuilt city of Byzantium, changing its name to New Rome and declaring it the new capital of the Eastern Roman Empire.
name: Constantine the Great

text: Citing government misconduct, Daniel Ellsberg's charges for his involvement in releasing the Pentagon Papers to The New York Times are dismissed.
name: Daniel Ellsberg

text: Klaus Barbie goes on trial in Lyon for war crimes committed during World War II.
name: Klaus Barbie

text: Deep Blue, a chess-playing supercomputer, defeats Garry Kasparov in the last game of the rematch, becoming the first computer to beat a world-champion chess player in a classic match format.
name: Garry Kasparov

text: Heinrich XI, count of the Principality of Reuss-Greiz, is elevated to Prince by Joseph II, Holy Roman Emperor.
name: Joseph II

text: American Civil War: Battle of Raymond: Two divisions of James B. McPherson's XVII Corps turn the left wing of Confederate General John C. Pemberton's defensive line on Fourteen Mile Creek, opening up the interior of Mississippi to the Union Army during the Vicksburg Campaign.
name: John C. Pemberton

text: Konrad Zuse presents the Z3, the world's first working programmable, fully automatic computer, in Berlin.
name: Konrad Zuse

text: Dutch statesman Johan van Oldenbarnevelt is executed in The Hague after being convicted of treason.
name: Johan van Oldenbarnevelt

text: American Civil War: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom issues a "proclamation of neutrality" which recognizes the Confederacy as having belligerent rights.
name: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom

text: The USS Planter, a steamer and gunship, steals through Confederate lines and is passed to the Union, by a southern slave, Robert Smalls, who later was officially appointed as captain, becoming the first black man to command a United States ship.
name: Robert Smalls

text: The inaugural Formula One World Championship race takes place at Silverstone Circuit. The race was won by Giuseppe Farina, who would go on to become the inaugural champion that year.
name: Giuseppe Farina

text: Alison Hargreaves, a 33-year-old British mother, becomes the first woman to conquer Everest without oxygen or the help of sherpas.
name: Alison Hargreaves

text: American physician Kermit Gosnell is found guilty in Pennsylvania of murdering three infants born alive during attempted abortions, involuntary manslaughter of a woman during an abortion procedure, and other charges.
name: Kermit Gosnell

text: Four-year-old Louis XIV becomes King of France upon the death of his father, Louis XIII.
name: Louis XIV

text: Paraguay: Pedro Juan Caballero, Fulgencio Yegros and José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia start actions to depose the Spanish governor.
name: José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia

text: American Civil War: During the Vicksburg campaign, Union forces drive Confederates under Joseph E. Johnston out of Jackson, Mississippi in the Battle of Jackson.
name: Joseph E. Johnston

text: Fijian Prime Minister Timoci Bavadra is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Lieutenant colonel Sitiveni Rabuka.
name: Sitiveni Rabuka

text: A self coup by prime minister Kārlis Ulmanis succeeded in Latvia, suspending its constitution and dissolving its Saeima.
name: Kārlis Ulmanis

text: Édith Cresson becomes France's first female Prime Minister.
name: Édith Cresson

text: Continental Army officer Lachlan McIntosh fatally wounds Button Gwinnett, a signer of the United States Declaration of Independence, in a duel in Savannah, Georgia.
name: Lachlan McIntosh

text: American Civil War: During the Vicksburg campaign, the decisive Union victory by Ulysses S. Grant at the Battle of Champion Hill drives the Confederate army under John C. Pemberton back towards Vicksburg, Mississippi.
name: John C. Pemberton

text: Theodore Maiman operates the first optical laser (a ruby laser), at Hughes Research Laboratories in Malibu, California.
name: Theodore Maiman

text: Park Chung Hee leads a coup d'état to overthrow the Second Republic of South Korea.
name: Park Chung Hee

text: Junko Tabei from Japan becomes the first woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest.
name: Junko Tabei

text: A report by the Surgeon General of the United States C. Everett Koop states that the addictive properties of nicotine are similar to those of heroin and cocaine.
name: C. Everett Koop

text: Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom addresses a joint session of the United States Congress. She is the first British monarch to address the U.S. Congress.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Paul de Chomedey, Sieur de Maisonneuve founds the Ville Marie de Montréal.
name: Paul de Chomedey

text: Rosalía de Castro publishes Cantares Gallegos, the first book in the Galician language.
name: Rosalía de Castro

text: The children's novel The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, by L. Frank Baum, is first published in the United States. The first copy is given to the author's sister.
name: L. Frank Baum

text: Spanish Civil War: The Largo Caballero government resigns in the wake of the Barcelona May Days, leading Juan Negrín to form a government, without the anarcho-syndicalist CNT, in its stead.
name: Juan Negrín

text: Prince Charles calls a proposed addition to the National Gallery, London, a "monstrous carbuncle on the face of a much-loved and elegant friend", sparking controversies on the proper role of the Royal Family and the course of modern architecture.
name: Prince Charles

text: Emperor Constantine the Great announces free distributions of food to the citizens in Constantinople.
name: Constantine the Great

text: The first Indian film, Shree Pundalik by Dadasaheb Torne, is released in Mumbai.
name: Dadasaheb Torne

text: Evangelist Aimee Semple McPherson disappears in Venice, California.
name: Aimee Semple McPherson

text: John II of Castile defeats the Infantes of Aragon at the First Battle of Olmedo.
name: John II of Castile

text: King George II of Great Britain grants the Ohio Company a charter of land around the forks of the Ohio River.
name: George II of Great Britain

text: The New York Post Sunday Magazine publishes Martin Luther King Jr.'s Letter from Birmingham Jail.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: President of Romania Traian Băsescu survives an impeachment referendum and returns to office from suspension.
name: Traian Băsescu

text: The wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle is held at St George's Chapel, Windsor, with an estimated global audience of 1.9 billion.
name: Prince Harry

text: Cartographer Abraham Ortelius issues Theatrum Orbis Terrarum, the first modern atlas.
name: Abraham Ortelius

text: Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis receive a U.S. patent for blue jeans with copper rivets.
name: Levi Strauss

text: Amelia Earhart takes off from Newfoundland to begin the world's first solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic Ocean by a female pilot, landing in Ireland the next day.
name: Amelia Earhart

text: Discovery of the cosmic microwave background radiation by Robert Woodrow Wilson and Arno Penzias.
name: Robert Woodrow Wilson

text: Henry III of Castile sends Ruy González de Clavijo as ambassador to Timur to discuss the possibility of an alliance between Timur and Castile against the Ottoman Empire.
name: Henry III of Castile

text: The first day of the Battle of Aspern-Essling between the Austrian army led by Archduke Charles and the French army led by Napoleon I of France sees the French attack across the Danube held.
name: Archduke Charles

text: The American Red Cross is established by Clara Barton in Washington, D.C.
name: Clara Barton

text: Bad weather forces Amelia Earhart to land in a pasture in Derry, Northern Ireland, and she thereby becomes the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean.
name: Amelia Earhart

text: Start of the Wars of the Roses: At the First Battle of St Albans, Richard, Duke of York, defeats and captures King Henry VI of England.
name: Henry VI of England

text: The Sultan of the Ottoman Empire Abdul Hamid II establishes the Ullah millet for the Aromanians of the empire. For this reason, the Aromanian National Day is sometimes celebrated on this day, although most do so on May 23 instead, which is when this event was publicly announced.
name: Abdul Hamid II

text: Greek left-wing politician Grigoris Lambrakis is clubbed over the head, causing his death five days later.
name: Grigoris Lambrakis

text: A worldwide trade embargo against Haiti goes into effect to punish its military rulers for not reinstating the country's ousted elected leader, Jean-Bertrand Aristide.
name: Jean-Bertrand Aristide

text: The Burmese military regime jails 71 supporters of Aung San Suu Kyi in a bid to block a pro-democracy meeting.
name: Aung San

text: Joan of Arc is captured at the Siege of Compiègne by troops from the Burgundian faction.
name: Joan of Arc

text: Dutch rebels led by Louis of Nassau, defeat Jean de Ligne, Duke of Arenberg, and his loyalist troops in the Battle of Heiligerlee, opening the Eighty Years' War.
name: Louis of Nassau

text: Mexican-American War: President Mariano Paredes of Mexico unofficially declares war on the United States.
name: Mariano Paredes

text: Sultan Abdul Hamid II publicly announces the creation of the Ullah millet for the Aromanians of the empire, which had been established one day earlier. For this reason, the Aromanian National Day is usually celebrated on May 23, although some do so on May 22 instead.
name: Abdul Hamid II

text: Italy's most prominent anti-mafia judge Giovanni Falcone, his wife and three body guards are killed by the Corleonesi clan with a half-ton bomb near Capaci, Sicily. His friend and colleague Paolo Borsellino will be assassinated less than two months later, making 1992 a turning point in the history of Italian Mafia prosecutions.
name: Giovanni Falcone

text: John Wesley is converted, essentially launching the Methodist movement; the day is celebrated annually by Methodists as Aldersgate Day and a church service is generally held on the preceding Sunday.
name: John Wesley

text: Samuel Morse sends the message "What hath God wrought" (a biblical quotation, Numbers 23:23) from a committee room in the United States Capitol to his assistant, Alfred Vail, in Baltimore, Maryland, to inaugurate a commercial telegraph line between Baltimore and Washington D.C.
name: Samuel Morse

text: American Civil War: Union troops occupy Alexandria, Virginia, with Colonel Elmer E. Ellsworth becoming the first Union officer to be killed during the war.
name: Elmer E. Ellsworth

text: Amy Johnson lands in Darwin, Northern Territory, becoming the first woman to fly solo from England to Australia (she left on May 5 for the 11,000 mile flight).
name: Amy Johnson

text: Igor Sikorsky performs the first successful single-rotor helicopter flight.
name: Igor Sikorsky

text: Scopes Trial: John T. Scopes is indicted for teaching human evolution in Tennessee.
name: John T. Scopes

text: Jesse Owens of Ohio State University breaks three world records and ties a fourth at the Big Ten Conference Track and Field Championships in Ann Arbor, Michigan.
name: Jesse Owens

text: John Spenkelink, a convicted murderer, is executed in Florida; he is the first person to be executed in the state after the reintroduction of capital punishment in 1976.
name: John Spenkelink

text: A military coup in Sierra Leone replaces President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah with Major Johnny Paul Koroma.
name: Ahmad Tejan Kabbah

text: Alfonso VII of León and Castile is crowned in León Cathedral as Imperator totius Hispaniae (Emperor of all of Spain).
name: Alfonso VII

text: Charles Dow publishes the first edition of the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
name: Charles Dow

text: Walter Reuther and members of the United Auto Workers (UAW) clash with Ford Motor Company security guards at the River Rouge Complex complex in Dearborn, Michigan, during the Battle of the Overpass.
name: Walter Reuther

text: Zviad Gamsakhurdia becomes the first elected President of the Republic of Georgia in the post-Soviet era.
name: Zviad Gamsakhurdia

text: Protests triggered by the murder of George Floyd erupt in Minneapolis-Saint Paul, later becoming widespread across the United States and around the world.
name: George Floyd

text: Manchu regent Dorgon defeats rebel leader Li Zicheng of the Shun dynasty at the Battle of Shanhai Pass, allowing the Manchus to enter and conquer the capital city of Beijing.
name: Li Zicheng

text: Tsar Peter the Great founds the city of Saint Petersburg.
name: Peter the Great

text: The Pitt-Tierney duel takes place on Putney Heath outside London. A bloodless duel between the Prime Minister of Great Britain William Pitt the Younger and his political opponent George Tierney.
name: William Pitt

text: In Turkey, a military coup removes President Celâl Bayar and the rest of the democratic government from office.
name: Celâl Bayar

text: English Civil War: Bolton Massacre by Royalist troops under the command of James Stanley, 7th Earl of Derby.
name: James Stanley

text: In San Francisco, John Muir organizes the Sierra Club.
name: John Muir

text: Russo-Japanese War: The Battle of Tsushima ends with the destruction of the Russian Baltic Fleet by Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō and the Imperial Japanese Navy.
name: Tōgō Heihachirō

text: Daniel François Malan is elected as Prime Minister of South Africa. He later goes on to implement Apartheid.
name: Daniel François Malan

text: Peter Benenson's article The Forgotten Prisoners is published in several internationally read newspapers. This will later be thought of as the founding of the human rights organization Amnesty International.
name: Peter Benenson

text: An 18-year-old West German pilot, Mathias Rust, evades Soviet Union air defences and lands a private plane in Red Square in Moscow, Russia.
name: Mathias Rust

text: Peter Hollingworth resigns as Governor-General of Australia following criticism of his handling of child sexual abuse allegations during his tenure as Anglican Archbishop of Brisbane.
name: Peter Hollingworth

text: Former Formula One driver Takuma Sato wins his first Indianapolis 500, the first Japanese and Asian driver to do so. Double world champion Fernando Alonso retires from an engine issue in his first entry of the event.
name: Fernando Alonso

text: Jenny Lind leaves New York after her two-year American tour.
name: Jenny Lind

text: The pharmacist John Pemberton places his first advertisement for Coca-Cola, which appeared in The Atlanta Journal.
name: John Pemberton

text: Hundred Years' War: In Rouen, France, the 19-year-old Joan of Arc is burned at the stake by an English-dominated tribunal.
name: Joan of Arc

text: American Civil War: The Siege of Corinth ends in a Union victory, with General Henry Halleck capturing the critical rail junction of Corinth, Mississippi from retreating Confederate forces under General P. G. T. Beauregard.
name: P. G. T. Beauregard

text: Ottoman sultan Abdülaziz is deposed and succeeded by his nephew Murad V.
name: Murad V

text: At the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, the first Indianapolis 500 ends with Ray Harroun in his Marmon Wasp becoming the first winner of the 500-mile auto race.
name: Ray Harroun

text: World War II: Manolis Glezos and Apostolos Santas climb the Athenian Acropolis and tear down the German flag.
name: Manolis Glezos

text: The Auckland Harbour Bridge, crossing the Waitemata Harbour in Auckland, New Zealand, is officially opened by Governor-General Charles Lyttelton, 10th Viscount Cobham.
name: Charles Lyttelton

text: The long-time Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo is assassinated in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.
name: Rafael Trujillo

text: Depayin massacre: At least 70 people associated with the National League for Democracy are killed by government-sponsored mob in Burma. Aung San Suu Kyi flees the scene, but is arrested soon afterwards.
name: Aung San

text: Citing poor eyesight as a reason, Samuel Pepys records the last event in his diary.
name: Samuel Pepys

text: American Civil War: Peninsula Campaign: Confederate forces under Joseph E. Johnston and G.W. Smith engage Union forces under George B. McClellan outside the Confederate capital of Richmond, Virginia.
name: Joseph E. Johnston

text: Gilmore's Garden in New York City is renamed Madison Square Garden by William Henry Vanderbilt and is opened to the public at 26th Street and Madison Avenue.
name: William Henry Vanderbilt

text: Vanity Fair reveals that Mark Felt was "Deep Throat".
name: Mark Felt

text: James Clark Ross becomes the first European at the North Magnetic Pole.
name: James Clark Ross

text: The United States Census Bureau begins using Herman Hollerith's tabulating machine to count census returns.
name: Herman Hollerith

text: The United States Senate confirms the appointment of Louis Brandeis to the United States Supreme Court, making him the first Jew to be an Associate Justice.
name: Louis Brandeis

text: World War I: Western Front: Battle of Belleau Wood: Allied Forces under John J. Pershing and James Harbord engage Imperial German Forces under Wilhelm, German Crown Prince.
name: John J. Pershing

text: The Declaration of Conscience speech, by U.S. Senator from Maine, Margaret Chase Smith, is delivered in response to Joseph R. McCarthy's speech at Wheeling, West Virginia.
name: Margaret Chase Smith

text: Alfred Deakin becomes Prime Minister of Australia for the third time.
name: Alfred Deakin

text: Birth of the Italian Republic: In a referendum, Italians vote to turn Italy from a monarchy into a Republic. After the referendum, King Umberto II of Italy is exiled.
name: Umberto II of Italy

text: The coronation of Queen Elizabeth II at Westminster Abbey becomes the first British coronation and one of the first major international events to be televised.
name: Elizabeth II

text: In Denver, Timothy McVeigh is convicted on 15 counts of murder and conspiracy for his role in the 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City, in which 168 people died. He was executed four years later.
name: Timothy McVeigh

text: Former Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak is sentenced to life imprisonment for his role in the killing of demonstrators during the 2011 Egyptian revolution.
name: Hosni Mubarak

text: Samuel de Champlain lands at Tadoussac, Quebec, in the course of his third voyage to New France, and begins erecting fortifications.
name: Samuel de Champlain

text: American Civil War: Robert E. Lee and his Army of Northern Virginia begin marching to invade the North for a second time, starting the Gettysburg campaign.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: American Civil War: Union forces under Ulysses S. Grant sustain heavy casualties attacking Confederate troops under Robert E. Lee at the Battle of Cold Harbor in Hanover County, Virginia.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: The Duke of Windsor marries Wallis Simpson.
name: Wallis Simpson

text: The launch of Gemini 4, the first multi-day space mission by a NASA crew. Ed White, a crew member, performs the first American spacewalk.
name: Ed White

text: Australian Aboriginal land rights are recognised in Mabo v Queensland (No 2), a case brought by Torres Strait Islander Eddie Mabo which led to the Native Title Act 1993  overturning the long-held colonial assumption of terra nullius.
name: Eddie Mabo

text: The pageant for the Diamond Jubilee of Elizabeth II takes place on the River Thames.
name: Elizabeth II

text: The trial of United States Army private Chelsea Manning for leaking classified material to WikiLeaks begins in Fort Meade, Maryland.
name: Chelsea Manning

text: Captain George Vancouver claims Puget Sound for the Kingdom of Great Britain.
name: George Vancouver

text: Emily Davison, a suffragette, runs out in front of King George V's horse at The Derby. She is trampled, never regains consciousness, and dies four days later.
name: Emily Davison

text: The first Pulitzer Prizes are awarded: Laura E. Richards, Maude H. Elliott, and Florence Hall receive the first Pulitzer for biography (for Julia Ward Howe). Jean Jules Jusserand receives the first Pulitzer for history for his work With Americans of Past and Present Days. Herbert B. Swope receives the first Pulitzer for journalism for his work for the New York World.
name: Julia Ward Howe

text: The President of the Republic of China, Zhang Zuolin, is assassinated by Japanese agents.
name: Zhang Zuolin

text: A military coup in Argentina ousts Ramón Castillo.
name: Ramón Castillo

text: Flight Lieutenant Jerry Rawlings takes power in Ghana after a military coup in which General Fred Akuffo is overthrown.
name: Jerry Rawlings

text: Jonathan Pollard pleads guilty to espionage for selling top secret United States military intelligence to Israel.
name: Jonathan Pollard

text: In the 1989 Iranian Supreme Leader election, Ali Khamenei is elected as the new Supreme Leader of Iran after the death and funeral of Ruhollah Khomeini.
name: Ali Khamenei

text: The masque Tethys' Festival is performed at Whitehall Palace to celebrate the investiture of Henry Frederick, Prince of Wales.
name: Henry Frederick

text: Harriet Beecher Stowe's anti-slavery serial, Uncle Tom's Cabin, or Life Among the Lowly, starts a ten-month run in the National Era abolitionist newspaper.
name: Harriet Beecher Stowe

text: As the Treaty of Saigon is signed, ceding parts of southern Vietnam to France, the guerrilla leader Trương Định decides to defy Emperor Tự Đức of Vietnam and fight on against the Europeans.
name: Tự Đức

text: The trial of Lizzie Borden for the murder of her father and step-mother begins in New Bedford, Massachusetts.
name: Lizzie Borden

text: Louis Brandeis is sworn in as a Justice of the United States Supreme Court; he is the first American Jew to hold such a position.
name: Louis Brandeis

text: Elvis Presley introduces his new single, "Hound Dog", on The Milton Berle Show, scandalizing the audience with his suggestive hip movements.
name: Milton Berle

text: Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on STS-111, carrying the Expedition 5 crew to the International Space Station to replace the Expedition 4 crew. Astronaut Franklin Chang-Díaz becomes the second person to have flown on seven spaceflights.
name: Franklin Chang Díaz

text: Constantine VII, the eight-year-old illegitimate son of Leo VI the Wise, becomes nominal ruler of the Byzantine Empire under the regency of a seven-man council headed by Patriarch Nicholas Mystikos, appointed by Constantine's uncle Alexander on his deathbed.
name: Leo VI the Wise

text: Alexis St Martin is accidentally shot in the stomach, leading to William Beaumont's studies on digestion.
name: William Beaumont

text: Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat wins the first presidential election in Mongolia.
name: Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat

text: Louis XIV is crowned King of France.
name: Louis XIV

text: David Thompson reaches the mouth of the Saskatchewan River in Manitoba.
name: David Thompson

text: American Temperance crusader Carrie Nation begins her campaign of vandalizing alcohol-serving establishments by destroying the inventory in a saloon in Kiowa, Kansas.
name: Carrie Nation

text: King Haakon VII of Norway returns from exactly five years in exile during World War II.
name: Haakon VII of Norway

text: Edvard Beneš resigns as President of Czechoslovakia rather than signing the Ninth-of-May Constitution, making his nation a Communist state.
name: Edvard Beneš

text: The United States Supreme Court overturns the conviction of Paul Cohen for disturbing the peace, setting the precedent that vulgar writing is protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution.
name: Paul Cohen

text: Five hundred million people watch the high day of the Silver Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II begin on television.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Herman Hollerith applies for US patent #395,781 for the 'Art of Compiling Statistics', which was his punched card calculator.
name: Herman Hollerith

text: Vietnam War: Nine-year-old Phan Thị Kim Phúc is burned by napalm, an event captured by Associated Press photographer Nick Ut moments later while the young girl is seen running naked down a road, in what would become an iconic, Pulitzer Prize-winning photo.
name: Nick Ut

text: Charles Kingsford Smith completes the first trans-Pacific flight in a Fokker Trimotor monoplane, the Southern Cross.
name: Charles Kingsford Smith

text: King Buddha Yodfa Chulaloke (Rama I) of Siam (modern day Thailand) is crowned.
name: Rama I

text: American Civil War: Battle of Brice's Crossroads: Confederate troops under Nathan Bedford Forrest defeat a much larger Union force led by General Samuel D. Sturgis in Mississippi.
name: Nathan Bedford Forrest

text: Fascists kidnap and kill Italian Socialist leader Giacomo Matteotti in Rome.
name: Giacomo Matteotti

text: James Earl Ray escapes from Brushy Mountain State Penitentiary in Petros, Tennessee. He is recaptured three days later.
name: James Earl Ray

text: The first direct electronic communication experiment between the nervous systems of two humans is carried out by Kevin Warwick in the United Kingdom.
name: Kevin Warwick

text: Battle of Sauchieburn: Fought between rebel Lords and James III of Scotland, resulting in the death of the king.
name: James III of Scotland

text: A group of Serbian officers storms the royal palace and assassinates King Alexander I of Serbia and his wife, Queen Draga.
name: Alexander I of Serbia

text: American Civil Rights Movement: Governor of Alabama George Wallace defiantly stands at the door of Foster Auditorium at the University of Alabama in an attempt to block two black students, Vivian Malone and James Hood, from attending that school. Later in the day, accompanied by federalized National Guard troops, they are able to register.
name: James Hood

text: Lloyd J. Old identified the first cell surface antigens that could differentiate among different cell types.
name: Lloyd J. Old

text: Timothy McVeigh is executed for his role in the Oklahoma City bombing.
name: Timothy McVeigh

text: American Civil War, Overland Campaign: Battle of Cold Harbor: Ulysses S. Grant gives the Confederate forces under Robert E. Lee a victory when he pulls his Union troops from their position at Cold Harbor, Virginia and moves south.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: The Central African Republic's former emperor Jean-Bédel Bokassa is sentenced to death for crimes he had committed during his 13-year rule.
name: Jean-Bédel Bokassa

text: Forty-nine civilians are killed and 58 others injured in an attack on a gay nightclub in Orlando, Florida, United States; the gunman, Omar Mateen, is killed in a gunfight with police.
name: Omar Mateen

text: The decisions of the Edict of Milan, signed by Constantine the Great and co-emperor Valerius Licinius, granting religious freedom throughout the Roman Empire, are published in Nicomedia.
name: Constantine the Great

text: American Revolutionary War: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette lands near Charleston, South Carolina, in order to help the Continental Congress to train its army.
name: Gilbert du Motier

text: Émile Levassor wins the world's first real automobile race. Levassor completed the 732-mile course, from Paris to Bordeaux and back, in just under 49 hours, at a then-impressive speed of about fifteen miles per hour (24 km/h).
name: Émile Levassor

text: At the Trooping the Colour ceremony in London, a teenager, Marcus Sarjeant, fires six blank shots at Queen Elizabeth II.
name: Elizabeth II

text: A jury sentences Timothy McVeigh to death for his part in the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing.
name: Timothy McVeigh

text: Richard II of England meets leaders of Peasants' Revolt at Mile End. The Tower of London is stormed by rebels who enter without resistance.
name: Richard II of England

text: Arlington National Cemetery is established when 200 acres (0.81 km2) of the Arlington estate (formerly owned by the family of Confederate General Robert E. Lee) are officially set aside as a military cemetery by U.S. Secretary of War Edwin M. Stanton.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: Eadweard Muybridge takes a series of photographs to prove that all four feet of a horse leave the ground when it runs; the study becomes the basis of motion pictures.
name: Eadweard Muybridge

text: Bessie Coleman earns her pilot's license, becoming the first female pilot of African-American descent.
name: Bessie Coleman

text: A German expedition led by Karl Wien loses sixteen members in an avalanche on Nanga Parbat. It is the worst single disaster to occur on an 8000m peak.
name: Karl Wien

text: In the Saskatchewan general election, the CCF, led by Tommy Douglas, is elected and forms the first socialist government in North America.
name: Tommy Douglas

text: Red Army Faction co-founder Ulrike Meinhof is captured by police in Langenhagen.
name: Ulrike Meinhof

text: King Hussein of Jordan marries Jordanian-American Lisa Halaby, who takes the name Queen Noor.
name: Hussein of Jordan

text: Nik Wallenda becomes the first person to successfully tightrope walk directly over Niagara Falls.
name: Nik Wallenda

text: Battle of Stoke Field: King Henry VII of England defeats the leaders of a Yorkist rebellion in the final engagement of the Wars of the Roses.
name: Henry VII

text: War of the Austrian Succession: New England colonial troops under the command of William Pepperrell capture the Fortress of Louisbourg in Louisbourg, New France (Old Style date).
name: William Pepperrell

text: French Revolutionary Wars: In what became known as Cornwallis's Retreat, a British Royal Navy squadron led by Vice Admiral William Cornwallis strongly resists a much larger French Navy force and withdraws largely intact, setting up the French Navy defeat at the Battle of Groix six days later.
name: William Cornwallis

text: While on tour with the Kirov Ballet in Paris, Rudolf Nureyev defects from the Soviet Union.
name: Rudolf Nureyev

text: Padre Pio is canonized by the Roman Catholic Church.
name: Padre Pio

text: China successfully launches its Shenzhou 9 spacecraft, carrying three astronauts, including the first female Chinese astronaut Liu Yang, to the Tiangong-1 orbital module.
name: Liu Yang

text: Battle of Deptford Bridge: Forces under King Henry VII defeat troops led by Michael An Gof.
name: Henry VII

text: Matsunaga Hisahide assassinates the 13th Ashikaga shōgun, Ashikaga Yoshiteru.
name: Ashikaga Yoshiteru

text: Last public guillotining in France: Eugen Weidmann, a convicted murderer, is executed in Versailles outside the Saint-Pierre prison.
name: Eugen Weidmann

text: A day after South Vietnamese President Ngô Đình Diệm announced the Joint Communiqué to end the Buddhist crisis, a riot involving around 2,000 people breaks out. One person is killed.
name: Ngô Đình Diệm

text: Following a televised low-speed highway chase, O. J. Simpson is arrested for the murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend Ronald Goldman.
name: O. J. Simpson

text: Juneteenth National Independence Day, was signed into law by President Joe Biden, to become the first federal holiday established since Martin Luther King Jr. Day in 1983.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Susan B. Anthony is fined $100 for attempting to vote in the 1872 presidential election.
name: Susan B. Anthony

text: Empress Dowager Cixi of China orders all foreigners killed, including foreign diplomats and their families.
name: Empress Dowager Cixi of China

text: Aviator Amelia Earhart becomes the first woman to fly in an aircraft across the Atlantic Ocean (she is a passenger; Wilmer Stultz is the pilot and Lou Gordon the mechanic).
name: Amelia Earhart

text: William Joyce ("Lord Haw-Haw") is charged with treason for his pro-German propaganda broadcasting during World War II.
name: William Joyce

text: Carlos Castillo Armas leads an invasion force across the Guatemalan border, setting in motion the 1954 Guatemalan coup d'état.
name: Carlos Castillo Armas

text: Italian banker Roberto Calvi's body is discovered hanging beneath Blackfriars Bridge in London, England.
name: Roberto Calvi

text: The first officially recorded, organized baseball game is played under Alexander Cartwright's rules on Hoboken, New Jersey's Elysian Fields with the New York Base Ball Club defeating the Knickerbockers 23-1. Cartwright umpired.
name: Alexander Cartwright

text: Princess Louise of the Netherlands marries Crown Prince Karl of Sweden-Norway.
name: Louise of the Netherlands

text: Cold War: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg are executed at Sing Sing, in New York.
name: Ethel Rosenberg

text: Samuel Morse receives the patent for the telegraph.
name: Samuel Morse

text: Lizzie Borden is acquitted of the murders of her father and stepmother.
name: Lizzie Borden

text: Aeroméxico Flight 229 crashes on approach to Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport, killing all 27 people on board.
name: Gustavo Díaz Ordaz

text: Haitian president Leslie Manigat is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Lieutenant General Henri Namphy.
name: Leslie Manigat

text: Külüg Khan is enthroned as Khagan of the Mongols and Wuzong of the Yuan.
name: Külüg Khan

text: Edgar Ray Killen, who had previously been unsuccessfully tried for the murders of James Chaney, Andrew Goodman, and Mickey Schwerner, is convicted of manslaughter 41 years afterwards (the case had been reopened in 2004).
name: James Chaney

text: The Royal Navy battleship HMS Camperdown accidentally rams the British Mediterranean Fleet flagship HMS Victoria which sinks taking 358 crew with her, including the fleet's commander, Vice-Admiral Sir George Tryon.
name: George Tryon

text: George V and Mary of Teck are crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.
name: Mary of Teck

text: Former Liberal Party leader Jeremy Thorpe was acquitted of conspiracy to murder Norman Scott, who had accused Thorpe of having a relationship with him.
name: Jeremy Thorpe

text: Paraguayan President Fernando Lugo is removed from office by impeachment and succeeded by Federico Franco.
name: Fernando Lugo

text: John Jacob Astor forms the Pacific Fur Company.
name: John Jacob Astor

text: American Civil War: At Fort Towson in the Oklahoma Territory, Confederate Brigadier General Stand Watie surrenders the last significant Confederate army.
name: Stand Watie

text: In a game against the Washington Senators, Boston Red Sox pitcher Ernie Shore retires 26 batters in a row after replacing Babe Ruth, who had been ejected for punching the umpire.
name: Babe Ruth

text: Wiley Post and Harold Gatty take off from Roosevelt Field, Long Island in an attempt to circumnavigate the world in a single-engine plane.
name: Harold Gatty

text: Convicted Manhattan Project spy Klaus Fuchs is released after only nine years in prison and allowed to emigrate to Dresden, East Germany where he resumes a scientific career.
name: Klaus Fuchs

text: Nik Wallenda becomes the first man to successfully walk across the Grand Canyon on a tight rope.
name: Nik Wallenda

text: First War of Scottish Independence: The Battle of Bannockburn concludes with a decisive victory by Scottish forces led by Robert the Bruce.
name: Robert the Bruce

text: Samuel de Champlain encounters the mouth of the Saint John River, site of Reversing Falls and the present-day city of Saint John, New Brunswick, Canada.
name: Samuel de Champlain

text: Mary Pickford becomes the first female film star to sign a million-dollar contract.
name: Mary Pickford

text: Siam is renamed Thailand by Plaek Phibunsongkhram, the country's third prime minister.
name: Plaek Phibunsongkhram

text: Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt is injured in an assassination attempt.
name: Rómulo Betancourt

text: Julia Gillard assumes office as the first female Prime Minister of Australia.
name: Julia Gillard

text: The Wagner Group led by Yevgeny Prigozhin launches an insurrection against the Russian government.
name: Yevgeny Prigozhin

text: Venetian Elena Cornaro Piscopia is the first woman awarded a doctorate of philosophy when she graduates from the University of Padua.
name: Elena Cornaro Piscopia

text: Maria Theresa is crowned Queen of Hungary.
name: Maria Theresa

text: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania millionaire Harry Thaw shoots and kills prominent architect Stanford White.
name: Stanford White

text: Dr. Douglas Hyde is inaugurated as the first President of Ireland.
name: Douglas Hyde

text: The final page of the comic Krazy Kat is published, exactly two months after its author George Herriman died.
name: George Herriman

text: Alexei Petrovich, Tsarevich of Russia, Peter the Great's son, mysteriously dies after being sentenced to death by his father for plotting against him.
name: Peter the Great

text: Henri Moissan isolated elemental Fluorine for the first time.
name: Henri Moissan

text: World War I: Allied forces under John J. Pershing and James Harbord defeat Imperial German forces under Wilhelm, German Crown Prince in the Battle of Belleau Wood.
name: John J. Pershing

text: Shirley Jackson's short story The Lottery is published in The New Yorker magazine.
name: Shirley Jackson

text: Swedish boxer Ingemar Johansson becomes world champion of heavy weight boxing, by defeating American Floyd Patterson on technical knockout after two minutes and three seconds in the third round at Yankee Stadium.
name: Floyd Patterson

text: Two FBI agents and a member of the American Indian Movement are killed in a shootout on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation in South Dakota; Leonard Peltier is later convicted of the murders in a controversial trial.
name: Leonard Peltier

text: J. K. Rowling publishes the first of her Harry Potter novel series, Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone in United Kingdom.
name: J. K. Rowling

text: Mari Alkatiri, the first Prime Minister of East Timor, resigns after weeks of political unrest.
name: Mari Alkatiri

text: Joseph Smith, founder of the Latter Day Saint movement, and his brother Hyrum Smith, are killed by a mob at the Carthage, Illinois jail.
name: Hyrum Smith

text: The first solo circumnavigation of the globe is completed by Joshua Slocum from Briar Island, Nova Scotia.
name: Joshua Slocum

text: The President of Uruguay Juan María Bordaberry dissolves Parliament and establishes a dictatorship.
name: Juan María Bordaberry

text: Edward, Earl of March, is crowned King Edward IV of England.
name: Edward IV

text: Coronation of Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom.
name: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom

text: Greek politician Charilaos Trikoupis publishes a manifesto in the Athens daily Kairoi entitled "Who's to Blame?" leveling complaints against King George. Trikoupis is elected Prime Minister of Greece the next year.
name: Charilaos Trikoupis

text: Vice President Isabel Perón assumes powers and duties as Acting President of Argentina, while her husband President Juan Perón is terminally ill.
name: Isabel Perón

text: Mikhail Baryshnikov defects from the Soviet Union to Canada while on tour with the Kirov Ballet.
name: Mikhail Baryshnikov

text: The Spanish-held Castillo San Felipe del Morro in San Juan, Puerto Rico having been besieged for fifteen days, surrenders to an English force under Sir George Clifford, Earl of Cumberland.
name: George Clifford

text: Seven Years' War: Habsburg Austrian forces destroy a Prussian reinforcement and supply convoy in the Battle of Domstadtl, helping to expel Prussian King Frederick the Great from Moravia.
name: Frederick the Great

text: Charles J. Guiteau is hanged in Washington, D.C. for the assassination of U.S. President James Garfield.
name: Charles J. Guiteau

text: In Washington D.C., U.S. Secretary of State Charles Evans Hughes and Dominican Ambassador Francisco J. Peynado sign the Hughes-Peynado agreement, which ends the United States occupation of the Dominican Republic.
name: Charles Evans

text: Emperor Haile Selassie of Abyssinia appeals for aid to the League of Nations against Italy's invasion of his country.
name: Haile Selassie

text: Protests begin around Egypt against President Mohamed Morsi and the ruling Freedom and Justice Party, leading to their overthrow during the 2013 Egyptian coup d'état.
name: Mohamed Morsi
