text: Johann Georg Tralles discovers the Great Comet of 1819, (C/1819 N1). It is the first comet analyzed using polarimetry, by François Arago.
name: François Arago

text: Thomas Lempriere and James Clark Ross carve a marker on the Isle of the Dead in Van Diemen's Land to measure tidal variations, one of the earliest surviving benchmarks for sea level rise.
name: James Clark Ross

text: The British North America Act takes effect as the Province of Canada, New Brunswick, and Nova Scotia join into confederation to create the modern nation of Canada. John A. Macdonald is sworn in as the first Prime Minister of Canada. This date is commemorated annually in Canada as Canada Day, a national holiday.
name: John A. Macdonald

text: The Congo Free State is established by King Leopold II of Belgium.
name: Leopold II of Belgium

text: The National War Memorial for the Dominion of Newfoundland was inaugurated by Field Marshall Douglas Haig, 1st Earl Haig in St. John's, Newfoundland. The date commemorates the first day of the Battle of the Somme, where at Beaumont-Hamel, 86 percent of the Royal Newfoundland Regiment was wiped out.
name: Douglas Haig

text: Wiley Post and Harold Gatty become the first people to circumnavigate the globe in a single-engined monoplane aircraft.
name: Harold Gatty

text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Quaid-i-Azam) inaugurates Pakistan's central bank, the State Bank of Pakistan.
name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah

text: The British Government admits that former diplomat Kim Philby had worked as a Soviet agent.
name: Kim Philby

text: The Scottish Parliament is officially opened by Elizabeth II on the day that legislative powers are officially transferred from the old Scottish Office in London to the new devolved Scottish Executive in Edinburgh. In Wales, the powers of the Welsh Secretary are transferred to the National Assembly.
name: Elizabeth II

text: King Henry the Fowler dies in his royal palace in Memleben. He is succeeded by his son Otto I, who becomes the ruler of East Francia.
name: Otto I

text: The first English expedition (from Virginia) against Acadia led by Samuel Argall takes place.
name: Samuel Argall

text: Charles J. Guiteau shoots and fatally wounds U.S. President James A. Garfield (who will die of complications from his wounds on September 19).
name: Charles J. Guiteau

text: An airship designed and constructed by Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin of Germany made its first flight on Lake Constance near Friedrichshafen.
name: Ferdinand von Zeppelin

text: Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan are last heard from over the Pacific Ocean while attempting to make the first equatorial round-the-world flight.
name: Amelia Earhart

text: Indian independence leader Subhas Chandra Bose is arrested and detained in Calcutta.
name: Subhas Chandra Bose

text: Marcel Lefebvre and the four bishops he consecrated were excommunicated by the Holy See.
name: Marcel Lefebvre

text: Colombian conflict: Íngrid Betancourt, a member of the Chamber of Representatives of Colombia, is released from captivity after being held for six and a half years by FARC.
name: Íngrid Betancourt

text: Québec City is founded by Samuel de Champlain.
name: Samuel de Champlain

text: Pitcairn Island is discovered by Midshipman Robert Pitcairn on an expeditionary voyage commanded by Philip Carteret.
name: Philip Carteret

text: British Prime Minister John Major announced the Stone of Scone would be returned to Scotland.
name: John Major

text: Lewis Carroll tells Alice Liddell a story that would grow into Alice's Adventures in Wonderland and its sequels.
name: Alice Liddell

text: American Civil War: Retreat from Gettysburg: The Confederate Army of Northern Virginia under Robert E. Lee withdraws from the battlefield after losing the Battle of Gettysburg, signaling an end to his last invasion of the North.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: The Johnson-Jeffries riots occur after African-American boxer Jack Johnson knocks out white boxer Jim Jeffries in the 15th round. Between 11 and 26 people are killed and hundreds more injured.
name: Jack Johnson

text: Lê Văn Khôi along with 27 soldiers stage a mutiny taking over the Phiên An citadel, developing into the Lê Văn Khôi revolt against Emperor Minh Mạng.
name: Minh Mạng

text: Micheline Bernardini models the first modern bikini at a swimming pool in Paris.
name: Micheline Bernardini

text: Juvénal Habyarimana seizes power over Rwanda in a coup d'état.
name: Juvénal Habyarimana

text: Arthur Ashe becomes the first black man to win the Wimbledon singles title.
name: Arthur Ashe

text: Swedish tennis player Björn Borg wins his fifth Wimbledon final and becomes the first male tennis player to win the championships five times in a row (1976-1980).
name: Björn Borg

text: Jeff Bezos founds Amazon.
name: Jeff Bezos

text: Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lankan Tamil MP A. Thangathurai is shot dead at Sri Shanmuga Hindu Ladies College in Trincomalee.
name: A. Thangathurai

text: Richard III and Anne Neville are crowned King and Queen of England.
name: Anne Neville

text: American Revolutionary War: Siege of Fort Ticonderoga: After a bombardment by British artillery under General John Burgoyne, American forces retreat from Fort Ticonderoga, New York.
name: John Burgoyne

text: World War I: Arabian troops led by T. E. Lawrence ("Lawrence of Arabia") and Auda ibu Tayi capture Aqaba from the Ottoman Empire during the Arab Revolt.
name: T. E. Lawrence

text: Jackie Robinson refuses to move to the back of a bus, leading to a court-martial.
name: Jackie Robinson

text: Althea Gibson wins at the Wimbledon Championships, becoming the first black athlete to do so.
name: Althea Gibson

text: In the Bosnian War, under the command of General Ratko Mladić, Serbia begins its attack on the Bosnian town of Srebrenica.
name: Ratko Mladić

text: A retrial verdict acquits Joan of Arc of heresy 25 years after her execution.
name: Joan of Arc

text: Industrialist Henry J. Kaiser begins construction of Boulder Dam (now known as Hoover Dam).
name: Henry J. Kaiser

text: Ernesto "Che" Guevara sets out on a trip through Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, Panama, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, and El Salvador.
name: Ernesto "Che" Guevara

text: Boris Johnson announces his resignation as leader of the Conservative Party following days of pressure from the Members of Parliament (MPs) during the July 2022 United Kingdom government crisis.
name: Boris Johnson

text: Peter I of Russia defeats Charles XII of Sweden at the Battle of Poltava, thus effectively ending Sweden's status as a major power in Europe.
name: Charles XII

text: Francis Gary Powers is charged with espionage resulting from his flight over the Soviet Union.
name: Francis Gary Powers

text: Ne Win besieges and blows up the Rangoon University Student Union building to crush the Student Movement.
name: Ne Win

text: King Mwambutsa IV Bangiriceng of Burundi is deposed by his son Prince Charles Ndizi.
name: Prince Charles

text: Israeli Mossad assassinate Palestinian writer Ghassan Kanafani.
name: Ghassan Kanafani

text: The Fatimid general Jawhar leads the Friday prayer in Fustat in the name of Caliph al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah, thereby symbolically completing the Fatimid conquest of Egypt.
name: Al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah

text: Catherine the Great becomes Empress of Russia following the coup against her husband, Peter III.
name: Peter III

text: Explorer David Thompson posts a sign near what is now Sacajawea State Park in Washington state, claiming the Columbia District for the United Kingdom.
name: David Thompson

text: Daniel Hale Williams, American heart surgeon, performs the first successful open-heart surgery in United States without anesthesia.
name: Daniel Hale Williams

text: Johnny Weissmuller swims the 100 meters freestyle in 58.6 seconds breaking the world swimming record and the 'minute barrier'.
name: Johnny Weissmuller

text: The African Union is established in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, replacing the Organisation of African Unity (OAU). The organization's first chairman is Thabo Mbeki, President of South Africa.
name: Thabo Mbeki

text: William I of Orange is assassinated in his home in Delft, Holland, by Balthasar Gérard.
name: William I of Orange

text: War of the Pacific: Chileans led by Alejandro Gorostiaga defeat Andrés Avelino Cáceres's Peruvian army at the Battle of Huamachuco, hastening the end of the war.
name: Alejandro Gorostiaga

text: Scopes trial: In Dayton, Tennessee, the so-called "Monkey Trial" begins of John T. Scopes, a young high school science teacher accused of teaching evolution in violation of the Butler Act.
name: John T. Scopes

text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah is recommended as the first Governor-General of Pakistan by the British Prime Minister, Clement Attlee.
name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah

text: The Chicago Freedom Movement, co-founded by Martin Luther King Jr., holds a rally at Soldier Field in Chicago; as many as 60,000 people attend.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: In Miami, former Panamanian leader Manuel Noriega is sentenced to 40 years in prison for drug and racketeering violations.
name: Manuel Noriega

text: Burmese politician Aung San Suu Kyi is released from house arrest.
name: Aung San

text: Samuel de Champlain returns to Quebec.
name: Samuel de Champlain

text: Jacques Necker is dismissed as France's Finance Minister sparking the Storming of the Bastille.
name: Jacques Necker

text: French astronomer Jean-Louis Pons makes his first comet discovery. In the next 27 years he discovers another 36 comets, more than any other person in history.
name: Jean-Louis Pons

text: A duel occurs in which the Vice President of the United States Aaron Burr mortally wounds former Secretary of the Treasury Alexander Hamilton.
name: Alexander Hamilton

text: The Fly-fisher's Entomology is published by Alfred Ronalds. The book transformed the sport and went to many editions.
name: Alfred Ronalds

text: Fiat founded by Giovanni Agnelli in Turin, Italy.
name: Giovanni Agnelli

text: Murder of Grace Brown by Chester Gillette in the United States, inspiration for Theodore Dreiser's An American Tragedy.
name: Theodore Dreiser

text: Babe Ruth makes his debut in Major League Baseball.
name: Babe Ruth

text: Eric Liddell won the gold medal in 400m at the 1924 Paris Olympics, after refusing to run in the heats for 100m, his favoured distance, on a Sunday.
name: Eric Liddell

text: Engelbert Zaschka of Germany flies his large human-powered aircraft, the Zaschka Human-Power Aircraft, about 20 meters at Berlin Tempelhof Airport without assisted take-off.
name: Engelbert Zaschka

text: Prince Karim Husseini Aga Khan IV inherits the office of Imamat as the 49th Imam of Shia Imami Ismai'li worldwide, after the death of Sir Sultan Mahommed Shah Aga Khan III.
name: Aga Khan III

text: To Kill a Mockingbird by Harper Lee is first published, in the United States.
name: Harper Lee

text: Martin Luther King Jr., assassinated in 1968, is awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Hartmann Schedel's Nuremberg Chronicle, one of the best-documented early printed books, is published.
name: Hartmann Schedel

text: Ranjit Singh conquers Lahore and becomes Maharaja of the Punjab (Sikh Empire).
name: Ranjit Singh

text: Coronation of Alexander III as King of Scots.
name: Alexander III

text: English Civil War: Battle of Roundway Down: In England, Henry Wilmot, 1st Earl of Rochester, commanding the Royalist forces, heavily defeats the Parliamentarian forces led by Sir William Waller.
name: Henry Wilmot

text: The General Assembly's Institution, now the Scottish Church College, one of the pioneering institutions that ushered the Bengali Renaissance, is founded by Alexander Duff and Raja Ram Mohan Roy, in Calcutta, India.
name: Ram Mohan Roy

text: In an unprecedented action, British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan dismisses seven members of his Cabinet, marking the effective end of the National Liberals as a distinct force within British politics.
name: Harold Macmillan

text: French DGSE personnel abort an operation to rescue Íngrid Betancourt from FARC rebels in Colombia, causing a political scandal when details are leaked to the press.
name: Íngrid Betancourt

text: After a five-day search, the body of American actress and singer Naya Rivera is recovered from Lake Piru, where she drowned in California.
name: Naya Rivera

text: Joan of Arc, taken by the Burgundians in May, is handed over to Pierre Cauchon, the bishop of Beauvais.
name: Joan of Arc

text: Foundation of the Mission San Antonio de Padua in modern California by the Franciscan friar Junípero Serra.
name: Junípero Serra

text: The first ascent of the Matterhorn is completed by Edward Whymper and his party, four of whom die on the descent.
name: Edward Whymper

text: American outlaw Billy the Kid is shot and killed by Sheriff Pat Garrett in the Maxwell House at Fort Sumner, New Mexico.
name: Pat Garrett

text: Rawya Ateya takes her seat in the National Assembly of Egypt, thereby becoming the first female parliamentarian in the Arab world.
name: Rawya Ateya

text: Jane Goodall arrives at the Gombe Stream Reserve in present-day Tanzania to begin her study of chimpanzees in the wild.
name: Jane Goodall

text: An Lushan Rebellion: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang is ordered by his Imperial Guards to execute chancellor Yang Guozhong by forcing him to commit suicide or face a mutiny. General An Lushan has other members of the emperor's family killed.
name: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang

text: John Ball, a leader in the Peasants' Revolt, is hanged, drawn and quartered in the presence of King Richard II of England.
name: Richard II of England

text: French Revolution: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette, is named by acclamation Colonel General of the new National Guard of Paris.
name: Gilbert du Motier

text: Pike Expedition: United States Army Lieutenant Zebulon Pike begins an expedition from Fort Bellefontaine near St. Louis, Missouri,  to explore the west.
name: Zebulon Pike

text: American Civil War: The CSS Arkansas, the most effective ironclad on the Mississippi River, battles with Union Navy ships commanded by Admiral David Farragut, severely damaging three ships and sustaining heavy damage herself.
name: David Farragut

text: In Seattle, Washington, William Boeing and George Conrad Westervelt incorporate Pacific Aero Products (later renamed Boeing).
name: William Boeing

text: Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lankan Tamil MP S. Shanmuganathan is killed by a claymore mine.
name: S. Shanmuganathan

text: "American Taliban" John Walker Lindh pleads guilty to supplying aid to the enemy and possession of explosives during the commission of a felony.
name: John Walker Lindh

text: The Anti-Terrorism Court of Pakistan sentences British born Ahmed Omar Saeed Sheikh to death, and three others suspected of murdering The Wall Street Journal reporter Daniel Pearl to life.
name: Daniel Pearl

text: King Richard II of England is crowned.
name: Richard II of England

text: Father Junípero Serra founds California's first mission, Mission San Diego de Alcalá. Over the following decades, it evolves into the city of San Diego, California.
name: Junípero Serra

text: The last apparition of the Blessed Virgin Mary to Bernadette Soubirous in Lourdes, France.
name: Bernadette Soubirous

text: American Civil War: David Farragut is promoted to rear admiral, becoming the first officer in United States Navy to hold an admiral rank.
name: David Farragut

text: Persian Constitutional Revolution: Mohammad Ali Shah Qajar is forced out as Shah of Persia and is replaced by his son Ahmad Shah Qajar.
name: Ahmad Shah Qajar

text: Augusto César Sandino leads a raid on U.S. Marines and Nicaraguan Guardia Nacional that had been sent to apprehend him in the village of Ocotal, but is repulsed by one of the first dive-bombing attacks in history.
name: Augusto César Sandino

text: Emperor Haile Selassie signs the first constitution of Ethiopia.
name: Haile Selassie

text: Joe DiMaggio hits safely for the 56th consecutive game, a streak that still stands as an MLB record.
name: Joe DiMaggio

text: J. D. Salinger publishes his popular yet controversial novel, The Catcher in the Rye.
name: J. D. Salinger

text: Douglas Corrigan takes off from Brooklyn to fly the "wrong way" to Ireland and becomes known as "Wrong Way" Corrigan.
name: Douglas Corrigan

text: King Edward I of England issues the Edict of Expulsion, banishing all Jews (numbering about 16,000) from England.
name: Edward I

text: Coronation of Emperor Pedro II of Brazil.
name: Pedro II of Brazil

text: Coronation of George IV of the United Kingdom.
name: George IV of the United Kingdom

text: American Civil War: Morgan's Raid: At Buffington Island in Ohio, Confederate General John Hunt Morgan's raid into the north is mostly thwarted when a large group of his men are captured while trying to escape across the Ohio River.
name: John Hunt Morgan

text: Maurice Garin wins the first Tour de France.
name: Maurice Garin

text: Prime Minister of the shadow Burmese government, Bogyoke Aung San and eight others are assassinated.
name: Aung San

text: Chappaquiddick incident: U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy crashes his car into a tidal pond at Chappaquiddick Island, Massachusetts, killing his passenger Mary Jo Kopechne.
name: Ted Kennedy

text: Canadian explorer Pierre Gaultier de Varennes et de La Vérendrye reaches the western shore of Lake Michigan.
name: Pierre Gaultier de Varennes

text: Cold War: In Philadelphia, Harry Gold pleads guilty to spying for the Soviet Union by passing secrets from atomic scientist Klaus Fuchs.
name: Klaus Fuchs

text: Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) elects Sirimavo Bandaranaike Prime Minister, the world's first elected female head of government.
name: Sirimavo Bandaranaike

text: Burma's ruling junta puts opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi under house arrest.
name: Aung San

text: O. J. Simpson is granted parole to be released from prison after serving nine years of a 33-year sentence after being convicted of armed robbery in Las Vegas.
name: O. J. Simpson

text: American businessman Jeff Bezos flies to space aboard New Shepard  NS-16 operated by his private spaceflight company Blue Origin.
name: Jeff Bezos

text: In the market square of Springfield, Missouri, Wild Bill Hickok shoots and kills Davis Tutt in what is regarded as the first western showdown.
name: Wild Bill Hickok

text: Scopes Trial: In Dayton, Tennessee, high school biology teacher John T. Scopes is found guilty of teaching human evolution in class and fined $100.
name: John T. Scopes

text: Malcolm Campbell becomes the first man to exceed 150 mph (241 km/h) on land. At Pendine Sands in Wales, he drives Sunbeam 350HP built by Sunbeam at a two-way average speed of 150.33 mph (242 km/h).
name: Malcolm Campbell

text: Sirimavo Bandaranaike is elected Prime Minister of Sri Lanka, becoming the world's first female head of government
name: Sirimavo Bandaranaike

text: Jay Silverheels, a Mohawk actor, becomes the first Native American to have a star commemorated in the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
name: Jay Silverheels

text: The Barbenheimer phenomenon begins as two major motion pictures, Greta Gerwig's fantasy comedy Barbie and Christopher Nolan's epic biographical thriller Oppenheimer, are released in theaters on the same day and audiences, instead of creating a rivalry between the extremely dissimilar films, instead attend and praise both as an informal, surreal double feature.
name: Christopher Nolan

text: Wars of Scottish Independence: Battle of Falkirk: King Edward I of England and his longbowmen defeat William Wallace and his Scottish schiltrons outside the town of Falkirk.
name: Edward I

text: Surveyors of the Connecticut Land Company name an area in Ohio "Cleveland" after Gen. Moses Cleaveland, the superintendent of the surveying party.
name: Moses Cleaveland

text: Emperor Gia Long conquers Hanoi and unified Viet Nam, which had experienced centuries of feudal warfare.
name: Gia Long

text: Napoleonic Wars: Peninsular War: Battle of Salamanca: British forces led by Arthur Wellesley (later the Duke of Wellington) defeat French troops near Salamanca, Spain.
name: Arthur Wellesley

text: Katharine Lee Bates writes "America the Beautiful" after admiring the view from the top of Pikes Peak near Colorado Springs, Colorado.
name: Katharine Lee Bates

text: Aviator Wiley Post returns to Floyd Bennett Field in New York City, completing the first solo flight around the world in seven days, 18 hours and 49 minutes.
name: Floyd Bennett

text: Greg LeMond, an American road racing cyclist, wins his third Tour de France after leading the majority of the race. It was LeMond's second consecutive Tour de France victory.
name: Greg LeMond

text: Near Medellín, Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar escapes from his luxury prison fearing extradition to the United States.
name: Pablo Escobar

text: Chandrayaan-2, the second lunar exploration mission developed by Indian Space Research Organisation after Chandrayaan-1 is launched from Satish Dhawan Space Centre in a GSLV Mark III M1. It consists of a lunar orbiter, and also included the Vikram lander, and the Pragyan lunar rover.
name: Satish Dhawan

text: Aires de Ornelas e Vasconcelos is appointed the Archbishop of the Portuguese colonial enclave of Goa, India.
name: Aires de Ornelas e Vasconcelos

text: Bulgarian poet and Communist leader Nikola Vaptsarov is executed by firing squad.
name: Nikola Vaptsarov

text: Jackie Robinson becomes the first African American to be inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame.
name: Jackie Robinson

text: Phạm Tuân becomes the first Vietnamese citizen and the first Asian in space when he flies aboard the Soyuz 37 mission as an Intercosmos Research Cosmonaut.
name: Phạm Tuân

text: General Ne Win, effective ruler of Burma since 1962, resigns after pro-democracy protests.
name: Ne Win

text: Wars of Scottish Independence: Fall of Stirling Castle: King Edward I of England takes the stronghold using the War Wolf.
name: Edward I

text: Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac founds the trading post at Fort Pontchartrain, which later becomes the city of Detroit.
name: Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac

text: After 17 months of travel, Brigham Young leads 148 Mormon pioneers into Salt Lake Valley, resulting in the establishment of Salt Lake City.
name: Brigham Young

text: Richard March Hoe,  American inventor, patented the rotary-type printing press.
name: Richard March Hoe

text: American Civil War: Battle of Kernstown: Confederate General Jubal Early defeats Union troops led by General George Crook in an effort to keep them out of the Shenandoah Valley.
name: Jubal Early

text: O. Henry is released from prison in Columbus, Ohio, after serving three years for embezzlement from a bank.
name: O. Henry

text: Boris Johnson becomes Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after defeating Jeremy Hunt in a leadership contest, succeeding Theresa May.
name: Boris Johnson

text: At the behest of Tsar Peter the Great, the construction of Kadriorg Palace, dedicated to his wife Catherine, begins in Tallinn.
name: Peter the Great

text: Horatio Nelson loses more than 300 men and his right arm during the failed conquest attempt of Tenerife (Spain).
name: Horatio Nelson

text: The first commercial use of an electrical telegraph is successfully demonstrated in London by William Cooke and Charles Wheatstone.
name: Charles Wheatstone

text: Spanish-American War: The American invasion of Spanish-held Puerto Rico begins, as United States Army troops under General Nelson A. Miles land and secure the port at Guánica.
name: Nelson A. Miles

text: Louis Blériot makes the first flight across the English Channel in a heavier-than-air machine from Calais to Dover, England, United Kingdom in 37 minutes.
name: Louis Blériot

text: The Tunisian King Muhammad VIII al-Amin is replaced by President Habib Bourguiba.
name: Habib Bourguiba

text: During the Bavarian Rummel the rural population of Tyrol drove the Bavarian Prince-Elector Maximilian II Emanuel out of North Tyrol with a victory at the Pontlatzer Bridge and thus prevented the Bavarian Army, which was allied with France, from marching as planned on Vienna during the War of the Spanish Succession.
name: Maximilian II Emanuel

text: First day of the three-day Battle of Dervenakia, between the Ottoman Empire force led by Mahmud Dramali Pasha and the Greek Revolutionary force led by Theodoros Kolokotronis.
name: Theodoros Kolokotronis

text: American Civil War: Morgan's Raid ends; At Salineville, Ohio, Confederate cavalry leader John Hunt Morgan and 360 of his volunteers are captured by Union forces.
name: John Hunt Morgan

text: In Buenos Aires, Argentina the Revolución del Parque takes place, forcing President Miguel Ángel Juárez Celman's resignation.
name: Miguel Ángel Juárez Celman

text: Dadabhai Naoroji is elected as the first Indian Member of Parliament in Britain.
name: Dadabhai Naoroji

text: Emmy Noether's paper, which became known as Noether's theorem was presented at Göttingen, Germany, from which  conservation laws are deduced for symmetries of angular momentum, linear momentum, and energy.
name: Emmy Noether

text: King Edward VIII, in one of his few official duties before he abdicates the throne, officially unveils the Canadian National Vimy Memorial.
name: Edward VIII

text: King Farouk of Egypt abdicates in favor of his son Fuad.
name: Farouk of Egypt

text: Carlos Castillo Armas, dictator of Guatemala, is assassinated.
name: Carlos Castillo Armas

text: Researchers at the University of Toronto, led by biochemist Frederick Banting, prove that the hormone insulin regulates blood sugar.
name: Frederick Banting

text: Cessation of hostilities is achieved in the Korean War when the United States, China, and North Korea sign an armistice agreement. Syngman Rhee, President of South Korea, refuses to sign but pledges to observe the armistice.
name: Syngman Rhee

text: Mayor of Jaffna and former MP Alfred Duraiappah is shot dead.
name: Alfred Duraiappah

text: Mahmud II became Sultan of the Ottoman Empire and Caliph of Islam.
name: Mahmud II

text: The widowed Mary, Queen of Scots marries Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley, Duke of Albany, at Holyrood Palace, Edinburgh, Scotland, in a Catholic ceremony.
name: Henry Stuart

text: Driver Roger Williamson is killed during the Dutch Grand Prix, after a suspected tire failure causes his car to pitch into the barriers at high speed.
name: Roger Williamson

text: In New York City, David Berkowitz (a.k.a. the "Son of Sam") kills one person and seriously wounds another in the first of a series of attacks.
name: David Berkowitz

text: After impeachment on June 21, Abolhassan Banisadr flees with Massoud Rajavi to Paris, in an Iranian Air Force Boeing 707, piloted by Colonel Behzad Moezzi, to form the National Council of Resistance of Iran.
name: Abolhassan Banisadr

text: Beaver Wars: At Ticonderoga (now Crown Point, New York), Samuel de Champlain shoots and kills two Iroquois chiefs on behalf of his native allies.
name: Samuel de Champlain

text: Eighty Years' War: The Siege of Schenkenschans begins; Frederick Henry, Prince of Orange, begins the recapture of the strategically important fortress from the Spanish Army.
name: Frederick Henry

text: Nathaniel Bacon issues the "Declaration of the People of Virginia", beginning Bacon's Rebellion against the rule of Governor William Berkeley.
name: Nathaniel Bacon

text: Father Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, leader of the Mexican insurgency, is executed by the Spanish in Chihuahua City, Mexico.
name: Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla

text: Jimmy Hoffa disappears from the parking lot of the Machus Red Fox restaurant in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan, a suburb of Detroit, at about 2:30 p.m. He is never seen or heard from again.
name: Jimmy Hoffa

text: Ian Gow, Conservative Member of Parliament, is assassinated at his home by the IRA in a car bombing after he assured the group that the British government would never surrender to them.
name: Ian Gow

text: Marriage of Queen Elizabeth II's eldest granddaughter Zara Phillips to former rugby union footballer Mike Tindall.
name: Elizabeth II

text: The U.S. Second Continental Congress passes a resolution that the services of Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette "be accepted, and that, in consideration of his zeal, illustrious family and connexions, he have the rank and commission of major-general of the United States."
name: Gilbert du Motier

text: Michael Phelps breaks the record set in 1964 by Larisa Latynina for the most medals won at the Olympics.
name: Larisa Latynina

text: Ottoman forces are defeated in the battle of Saint Gotthard by an Austrian army led by Raimondo Montecuccoli, resulting in the Peace of Vasvár.
name: Raimondo Montecuccoli

text: Harriet Quimby takes her pilot's test and becomes the first U.S. woman to earn an Aero Club of America aviator's certificate.
name: Harriet Quimby

text: Patrick Pearse gives his famous speech "Ireland unfree shall never be at peace" at O'Donovan Rossa's funeral in Dublin.
name: Patrick Pearse

text: Anti-Fascist activists Bruno Tesch, Walter Möller, Karl Wolff and August Lütgens are executed by the Nazi regime in Altona.
name: Bruno Tesch

text: The coronation of Hassanal Bolkiah, the 29th Sultan of Brunei, is held.
name: Hassanal Bolkiah

text: Niki Lauda has a severe accident that almost claims his life at the German Grand Prix at Nürburgring.
name: Niki Lauda

text: Edward I of England returns from the Ninth Crusade and is crowned King seventeen days later.
name: Edward I

text: Judge Kenesaw Mountain Landis fines Standard Oil of Indiana a record $29.4 million for illegal rebating to freight carriers; the conviction and fine are later reversed on appeal.
name: Kenesaw Mountain Landis

text: Major League Baseball Commissioner Kenesaw Mountain Landis confirms the ban of the eight Chicago Black Sox, the day after they were acquitted by a Chicago court.
name: Kenesaw Mountain Landis

text: Senegalese opposition parties, under the leadership of Mamadou Dia, launch the Antiimperialist Action Front - Suxxali Reew Mi.
name: Mamadou Dia

text: Second Barons' War: Battle of Evesham: The army of Prince Edward (the future king Edward I of England) defeats the forces of rebellious barons led by Simon de Montfort, 6th Earl of Leicester, killing de Montfort and many of his allies.
name: Edward I

text: The father and stepmother of Lizzie Borden are found murdered in their Fall River, Massachusetts home. She will be tried and acquitted for the crimes a year later.
name: Lizzie Borden

text: Bolshevik-Makhnovist conflict: Mikhail Frunze declares victory over the Makhnovshchina.
name: Mikhail Frunze

text: Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo, president of the military government of Upper Volta, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Captain Thomas Sankara.
name: Thomas Sankara

text: Crisis in Venezuela: Seven people are injured when two drones detonate explosives on Avenida Bolívar, Caracas while president Nicolás Maduro is giving a speech to the Venezuelan National Guard.
name: Nicolás Maduro

text: The Battle of Alhandic is fought between Ramiro II of León and Abd-ar-Rahman III at Zamora in the context of the Spanish Reconquista. The battle resulted in a victory for the Emirate of Córdoba.
name: Abd-ar-Rahman III

text: The British Admiralty dismisses Francis Ronalds's new invention of the first working electric telegraph as "wholly unnecessary", preferring to continue using the semaphore.
name: Francis Ronalds

text: Charles XV of Sweden-Norway is crowned king of Norway in Trondheim.
name: Charles XV of Sweden

text: American Civil War: The Battle of Mobile Bay begins at Mobile Bay near Mobile, Alabama, Admiral David Farragut leads a Union flotilla through Confederate defenses and seals one of the last major Southern ports.
name: David Farragut

text: Peter O'Connor sets the first World Athletics recognised long jump world record of 24 ft 11.75 in (7.6137 m), a record that would stand for 20 years.
name: Peter O'Connor

text: Harry Houdini performs his greatest feat, spending 91 minutes underwater in a sealed tank before escaping.
name: Harry Houdini

text: Gertrude Ederle becomes the first woman to swim across the English Channel.
name: Gertrude Ederle

text: Takako Doi, chair of the Social Democratic Party, becomes Japan's first female speaker of the House of Representatives.
name: Takako Doi

text: A military junta led by Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz stages a coup d'état in Mauritania, overthrowing president Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi.
name: Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz

text: Coronation of King Otto I of Germany.
name: Otto I

text: Thor Heyerdahl's balsa wood raft, the Kon-Tiki, smashes into the reef at Raroia in the Tuamotu Islands after a 101-day, 7,000 kilometres (4,300 mi) journey across the Pacific Ocean in an attempt to prove that pre-historic peoples could have traveled from South America.
name: Thor Heyerdahl

text: Canadian-born American pharmacologist Frances Oldham Kelsey is awarded the U.S. President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service for her refusal to authorize thalidomide.
name: Frances Oldham Kelsey

text: California judge Harold Haley is taken hostage in his courtroom and killed during an effort to free George Jackson from police custody.
name: Harold Haley

text: Philippe Petit performs a high wire act between the twin towers of the World Trade Center 1,368 feet (417 m) in the air.
name: Philippe Petit

text: U.S. Congressman Mickey Leland (D-TX) and 15 others die in a plane crash in Ethiopia.
name: Mickey Leland

text: The Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, headed by Brigham Young, is reaffirmed as the leading body of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS Church).
name: Brigham Young

text: American Civil War: Following his defeat in the Battle of Gettysburg, General Robert E. Lee sends a letter of resignation to Confederate President Jefferson Davis (which is refused upon receipt).
name: Robert E. Lee

text: Wilbur Wright makes his first flight at a racecourse at Le Mans, France. It is the Wright Brothers' first public flight.
name: Wilbur Wright

text: At a zebra crossing in London, photographer Iain Macmillan takes the iconic photo that becomes the cover image of the Beatles' album Abbey Road.
name: Iain Macmillan

text: Kim Dae-jung, a South Korean politician and later president of South Korea, is kidnapped.
name: Kim Dae-jung

text: American Civil War: Battle of Cedar Mountain: At Cedar Mountain, Virginia, Confederate General Stonewall Jackson narrowly defeats Union forces under General John Pope.
name: John Pope

text: Edward VII and Alexandra of Denmark are crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.
name: Alexandra of Denmark

text: Summer Olympics: Jesse Owens wins his fourth gold medal at the games.
name: Jesse Owens

text: Battle of Lechfeld: Otto I, Holy Roman Emperor defeats the Magyars, ending 50 years of Magyar invasion of the West.
name: Otto I

text: World War I: Ottoman sultan Mehmed VI's representatives sign the Treaty of Sèvres that divides up the Ottoman Empire between the Allies.
name: Mehmed VI

text: In Yonkers, New York, 24-year-old postal employee David Berkowitz ("Son of Sam") is arrested for a series of killings in the New York City area over the period of one year.
name: David Berkowitz

text: Oklahoma City bombing: Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols are indicted for the bombing. Michael Fortier pleads guilty in a plea-bargain for his testimony.
name: Timothy McVeigh

text: The Battle of Otlukbeli: Mehmed the Conqueror of the Ottoman Empire decisively defeats Uzun Hassan of Aq Qoyunlu.
name: Mehmed the Conqueror

text: The 1920 Cork hunger strike begins which eventually results in the deaths of three Irish Republicans including the Lord Mayor of Cork Terence MacSwiney.
name: Terence MacSwiney

text: Babe Ruth becomes the first baseball player to hit 500 home runs in his career with a home run at League Park in Cleveland, Ohio.
name: Babe Ruth

text: Actress Hedy Lamarr and composer George Antheil receive a patent for a Frequency-hopping spread spectrum communication system that later became the basis for modern technologies in wireless telephones, two-way radio communications, and Wi-Fi.
name: Hedy Lamarr

text: A meeting between Sayyed Imam Al-Sharif, Osama bin Laden, Abdullah Yusuf Azzam, and leaders of Egyptian Islamic Jihad in Afghanistan culminates in the formation of Al-Qaeda.
name: Osama bin Laden

text: Santiago de Liniers, 1st Count of Buenos Aires re-takes the city of Buenos Aires, Argentina after the first British invasion.
name: Santiago de Liniers

text: French intervention forces William I of the Netherlands to abandon his attempt to suppress the Belgian Revolution.
name: William I of the Netherlands

text: Isaac Singer is granted a patent for his sewing machine.
name: Isaac Singer

text: Joseph Lister, British surgeon and scientist,  performs the first antiseptic surgery.
name: Joseph Lister

text: Colonel George Monck of the English Army forms Monck's Regiment of Foot, which will later become the Coldstream Guards.
name: George Monck

text: Carl Gustav Witt discovers 433 Eros, the first near-Earth asteroid to be found.
name: Carl Gustav Witt

text: First production in the UK of stainless steel by Harry Brearley.
name: Harry Brearley

text: Alexandros Panagoulis attempts to assassinate the Greek dictator Colonel Georgios Papadopoulos in Varkiza, Athens.
name: Alexandros Panagoulis

text: The first claimed powered flight, by Gustave Whitehead in his Number 21.
name: Gustave Whitehead

text: Ilich Ramírez Sánchez, also known as "Carlos the Jackal", is captured.
name: Carlos the Jackal

text: Egypt declares a state of emergency as security forces kill hundreds of demonstrators supporting former president Mohamed Morsi.
name: Mohamed Morsi

text: Will Rogers and Wiley Post are killed after their aircraft develops engine problems during takeoff in Barrow, Alaska.
name: Will Rogers

text: Founder of Pakistan, Muhammad Ali Jinnah is sworn in as first Governor-General of Pakistan in Karachi.
name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah

text: Alfredo Stroessner begins his dictatorship in Paraguay.
name: Alfredo Stroessner

text: Yuk Young-soo, First Lady of South Korea, is killed during an apparent assassination attempt upon President Park Chung Hee.
name: Park Chung Hee

text: Bangladeshi leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman is killed along with most members of his family during a military coup.
name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman

text: Battle of Plymouth: Inconclusive naval action between the fleets of Michiel de Ruyter and George Ayscue in the First Anglo-Dutch War.
name: Michiel de Ruyter

text: American Revolutionary War: The Americans led by General John Stark rout British and Brunswick troops under Friedrich Baum at the Battle of Bennington in Walloomsac, New York.
name: John Stark

text: U.S. President James Buchanan inaugurates the new transatlantic telegraph cable by exchanging greetings with Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom. However, a weak signal forces a shutdown of the service in a few weeks.
name: Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom

text: Joseph Kittinger parachutes from a balloon over New Mexico, United States, at 102,800 feet (31,300 m), setting three records that held until 2012: High-altitude jump, free fall, and highest speed by a human without an aircraft.
name: Joseph Kittinger

text: In an unsuccessful coup d'état attempt, the Royal Moroccan Air Force fires upon Hassan II of Morocco's plane while he is traveling back to Rabat.
name: Hassan II of Morocco

text: Australian Prime Minister Gough Whitlam symbolically hands over land to the Gurindji people after the eight-year Wave Hill walk-off, a landmark event in the history of Indigenous land rights in Australia, commemorated in a 1991 song by Paul Kelly and an annual celebration.
name: Gough Whitlam

text: AIRES Flight 8250 crashes at Gustavo Rojas Pinilla International Airport in San Andrés, San Andrés y Providencia, Colombia, killing two people.
name: Gustavo Rojas Pinilla

text: Hundred Years' War: Battle of Verneuil: An English force under John, Duke of Bedford defeats a larger French army under Jean II, Duke of Alençon, John Stewart, and Earl Archibald of Douglas.
name: Jean II

text: Eighty Years' War: Siege of Antwerp: Antwerp is captured by Spanish forces under Alexander Farnese, Duke of Parma, who orders Protestants to leave the city and as a result over half of the 100,000 inhabitants flee to the northern provinces.
name: Alexander Farnese

text: A first group of colonists sent by Sir Walter Raleigh under the charge of Ralph Lane lands in the New World to create Roanoke Colony on Roanoke Island, off the coast of present-day North Carolina.
name: Walter Raleigh

text: Islands Voyage: Robert Devereux, 2nd Earl of Essex, and Sir Walter Raleigh set sail on an expedition to the Azores.
name: Walter Raleigh

text: Ioan Giurgiu Patachi becomes Bishop of Făgăraș and is festively installed in his position at the St. Nicolas Cathedral in Făgăraș, after being formally confirmed earlier by Pope Clement XI.
name: Pope Clement XI

text: Robert Fulton's North River Steamboat leaves New York City for Albany, New York, on the Hudson River, inaugurating the first commercial steamboat service in the world.
name: Robert Fulton

text: Dutch King William I and Pope Leo XII sign concord.
name: Pope Leo XII

text: Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta proclaim the independence of Indonesia, igniting the Indonesian National Revolution against the Dutch Empire.
name: Mohammad Hatta

text: Lewinsky scandal: US President Bill Clinton admits in taped testimony that he had an "improper physical relationship" with White House intern Monica Lewinsky; later that same day he admits before the nation that he "misled people" about the relationship.
name: Monica Lewinsky

text: The Huguenot King Henry III of Navarre marries the Catholic Margaret of Valois, ostensibly to reconcile the feuding Protestants and Catholics of France.
name: Margaret of Valois

text: Camila O'Gorman and Ladislao Gutierrez are executed on the orders of Argentine dictator Juan Manuel de Rosas.
name: Juan Manuel de Rosas

text: French astronomer Pierre Janssen discovers helium.
name: Pierre Janssen

text: American astronomer Asaph Hall discovers Phobos, one of Mars’s moons.
name: Asaph Hall

text: Vladimir Nabokov's controversial novel Lolita is published in the United States.
name: Vladimir Nabokov

text: Steve Biko is arrested at a police roadblock under Terrorism Act No. 83 of 1967 in King William's Town, South Africa. He later dies from injuries sustained during this arrest, bringing attention to South Africa's apartheid policies.
name: Steve Biko

text: Gustav III of Sweden stages a coup d'état, in which he assumes power and enacts a new constitution that divides power between the Riksdag and the King.
name: Gustav III of Sweden

text: Gervasio Antonio de Posadas joins Argentina's Second Triumvirate.
name: Gervasio Antonio de Posadas

text: The French government announces that Louis Daguerre's photographic process is a gift "free to the world".
name: Louis Daguerre

text: Cold War: In Moscow, Russia, Soviet Union, downed American U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers is sentenced to ten years imprisonment by the Soviet Union for espionage.
name: Francis Gary Powers

text: A truck-bomb attack on United Nations headquarters in Iraq kills the agency's top envoy Sérgio Vieira de Mello and 21 other employees.
name: Sérgio Vieira de Mello

text: Philosopher and general Wang Yangming defeats Zhu Chenhao, ending the Prince of Ning rebellion against the reign of the Ming dynasty's Zhengde Emperor.
name: Wang Yangming

text: Former Grand Pensionary Johan de Witt and his brother Cornelis are lynched by a mob in The Hague.
name: Johan de Witt

text: World War II: One hundred sixty-eight captured allied airmen, including Phil Lamason, accused by the Gestapo of being "terror fliers", arrive at Buchenwald concentration camp.
name: Phil Lamason

text: Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lankan Tamil politician and former MP S. Sivamaharajah is shot dead at his home in Tellippalai.
name: S. Sivamaharajah

text: Song dynasty general Yue Fei defeats an army led by Jin dynasty general Wuzhu at the Battle of Yancheng during the Jin-Song Wars.
name: Yue Fei

text: Minamoto no Yoritomo becomes Sei-i Taishōgun and the de facto ruler of Japan. (Traditional Japanese date: the 12th day of the seventh month in the third year of the Kenkyū (建久) era).
name: Minamoto no Yoritomo

text: Battle of Vimeiro: British and Portuguese forces led by General Arthur Wellesley defeat French force under Major-General Jean-Andoche Junot near the village of Vimeiro, Portugal, the first Anglo-Portuguese victory of the Peninsular War.
name: Arthur Wellesley

text: Nat Turner leads black slaves and free blacks in a rebellion in Southampton County, Virginia, which will claim the lives of 55 to 65 whites and about twice that number of blacks.
name: Nat Turner

text: Philippine opposition leader Benigno Aquino Jr. is assassinated at Manila International Airport (now renamed Ninoy Aquino International Airport in his honor).
name: Benigno Aquino Jr.

text: American golfer Tiger Woods wins the 82nd PGA Championship and becomes the first golfer since Ben Hogan in 1953 to win three majors in a calendar year.
name: Ben Hogan

text: José de La Mar becomes President of Peru.
name: José de La Mar

text: Michael Collins, Commander-in-chief of the Irish Free State Army, is shot dead in an ambush during the Irish Civil War.
name: Michael Collins

text: Bill Woodfull of Australia becomes the only test cricket captain to twice regain The Ashes.
name: Bill Woodfull

text: Juan Marichal, pitcher for the San Francisco Giants, strikes John Roseboro, catcher for the Los Angeles Dodgers, on the head with a bat, sparking a 14-minute brawl, one of the most violent on-field incidents in sports history.
name: Juan Marichal

text: J. Edgar Hoover and John Mitchell announce the arrest of 20 of the Camden 28.
name: J. Edgar Hoover

text: Christian II of Denmark is deposed as king of Sweden and Gustav Vasa is elected regent.
name: Christian II of Denmark

text: George Villiers, the first Duke of Buckingham, is assassinated by John Felton.
name: George Villiers

text: Edirne event: Sultan Mustafa II of the Ottoman Empire is dethroned.
name: Mustafa II

text: Nat Turner's rebellion of enslaved Virginians is suppressed.
name: Nat Turner

text: Organized by Mexican American labor union leader César Chávez, the Salad Bowl strike, the largest farm worker strike in U.S. history, begins.
name: Cesar Chavez

text: Eugene Bullard, the only African American pilot in World War I, is posthumously commissioned as Second Lieutenant in the United States Air Force.
name: Eugene Bullard

text: The skeletal remains of Russia's last royal family members Alexei Nikolaevich, Tsarevich of Russia, and his sister Grand Duchess Anastasia are discovered near Yekaterinburg, Russia.
name: Alexei Nikolaevich

text: Willem of Orange marries duchess Anna of Saxony.
name: Anna of Saxony

text: American Revolutionary War: A small force of Pennsylvania militia is ambushed and overwhelmed by an American Indian group, which forces George Rogers Clark to abandon his attempt to attack Detroit.
name: George Rogers Clark

text: Amelia Earhart becomes the first woman to fly across the United States non-stop (from Los Angeles to Newark, New Jersey).
name: Amelia Earhart

text: Vice president João Café Filho takes office as president of Brazil, following the suicide of Getúlio Vargas.
name: Café Filho

text: Buddhist crisis: As a result of the Xá Lợi Pagoda raids, the US State Department cables the United States Embassy, Saigon to encourage Army of the Republic of Vietnam generals to launch a coup against President Ngô Đình Diệm if he did not remove his brother Ngô Đình Nhu.
name: Ngô Đình Diệm

text: Led by Abbie Hoffman, the Youth International Party temporarily disrupts trading at the New York Stock Exchange by throwing dollar bills from the viewing gallery, causing trading to cease as brokers scramble to grab them.
name: Abbie Hoffman

text: Mark David Chapman is sentenced to 20 years to life in prison for murdering John Lennon.
name: Mark David Chapman

text: Anders Behring Breivik, perpetrator of the 2011 Norway attacks, is sentenced to 21 years of preventive detention.
name: Anders Behring Breivik

text: Captain Matthew Webb becomes the first person to swim across the English Channel, traveling from Dover, England, to Calais, France, in 21 hours and 45 minutes.
name: Matthew Webb

text: The August Revolution ends as Emperor Bảo Đại abdicates, ending the Nguyễn dynasty.
name: Bảo Đại

text: The world's first publicly marketed instant noodles, Chikin Ramen, are introduced by Taiwanese-Japanese businessman Momofuku Ando.
name: Momofuku Ando

text: George Lincoln Rockwell, founder of the American Nazi Party, is assassinated by a former member of his group.
name: George Lincoln Rockwell

text: Linus Torvalds announces the first version of what will become Linux.
name: Linus Torvalds

text: The former viceroy Santiago de Liniers of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata is executed after the defeat of his counter-revolution.
name: Santiago de Liniers

text: The Battle of St. Quentin results in Emmanuel Philibert becoming Duke of Savoy.
name: Emmanuel Philibert

text: Jeongyu War: Battle of Chilcheollyang: A Japanese fleet of 500 ships destroys Joseon commander Won Gyun's fleet of 200 ships at Chilcheollyang.
name: Won Gyun

text: French Revolution: Frederick William II of Prussia and Leopold II, Holy Roman Emperor, issue the Declaration of Pillnitz, declaring the joint support of the Holy Roman Empire and Prussia for the French monarchy, agitating the French revolutionaries and contributing to the outbreak of the War of the First Coalition.
name: Frederick William II of Prussia

text: Wolfe Tone's United Irish and French forces clash with the British Army in the Battle of Castlebar, part of the Irish Rebellion of 1798, resulting in the creation of the French puppet Republic of Connacht.
name: Wolfe Tone

text: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés sights land near St. Augustine, Florida and founds the oldest continuously occupied European-established city in the continental United States.
name: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés

text: Black teenager Emmett Till is lynched in Mississippi for whistling at a white woman, galvanizing the nascent civil rights movement.
name: Emmett Till

text: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom: Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. gives his I Have a Dream speech.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Singaporean presidential election: Former Deputy Prime Minister Ong Teng Cheong is elected President of Singapore. Although it is the first presidential election to be determined by popular vote, the allowed candidates consist only of Ong and a reluctant whom the government had asked to run to confer upon the election the semblance of an opposition.
name: Ong Teng Cheong

text: Chicago Seven defendant David Dellinger, antiwar activist Bradford Lyttle, Civil Rights Movement historian Randy Kryn, and eight others are arrested by the Federal Protective Service while protesting in a demonstration at the Kluczynski Federal Building in downtown Chicago during that year's Democratic National Convention.
name: David Dellinger

text: The first experimental mission of ISRO's Scramjet Engine towards the realisation of an Air Breathing Propulsion System is successfully conducted from Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR, Sriharikota.
name: Satish Dhawan

text: Frederick the Great attacks Saxony, beginning the Seven Years' War in Europe.
name: Frederick the Great

text: British troops under Sir Arthur Wellesley defeat a Danish militia outside Copenhagen in the Battle of Køge.
name: Arthur Wellesley

text: Guru Ram Das becomes the Fourth Sikh Guru/Master.
name: Guru Ram Das

text: Anne, eldest daughter of King George II of Great Britain, is given the title Princess Royal.
name: George II of Great Britain

text: Ernest Shackleton completes the rescue of all of his men stranded on Elephant Island in Antarctica.
name: Ernest Shackleton

text: Thurgood Marshall is confirmed as the first African American Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
name: Thurgood Marshall

text: President Mohammad-Ali Rajai and Prime Minister Mohammad-Javad Bahonar of Iran are assassinated in a bombing committed by the People's Mujahedin of Iran.
name: Mohammad-Ali Rajai

text: German Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin patents his navigable balloon.
name: Ferdinand von Zeppelin

text: Diana, Princess of Wales, her partner, Dodi Fayed, and driver Henri Paul die in a car crash in Paris.
name: Dodi Fayed

text: Brazil's President Dilma Rousseff is impeached and removed from office.
name: Dilma Rousseff

text: Battle of Tippermuir: James Graham, 1st Marquess of Montrose defeats the Earl of Wemyss's Covenanters, reviving the Royalist cause.
name: James Graham

text: At the age of five, Louis XV becomes king of France in succession to his great-grandfather, King Louis XIV.
name: Louis XIV

text: The Order of St. Gregory the Great is established by Pope Gregory XVI of the Vatican State to recognize high support for the Vatican or for the Pope, by a man or a woman, and not necessarily a Roman Catholic.
name: Pope Gregory XVI

text: American Civil War: The Confederate Army General John Bell Hood orders the evacuation of Atlanta, ending a four-month siege by General William Tecumseh Sherman.
name: William Tecumseh Sherman

text: J. Robert Oppenheimer and his student Hartland Snyder publish the Oppenheimer-Snyder model, proving for the first time in contemporary physics how black holes could develop.
name: J. Robert Oppenheimer

text: Central African President David Dacko is ousted from power in a bloodless military coup led by General André Kolingba.
name: David Dacko

text: The wreck of the Titanic is discovered by an American-French expedition led by Robert Ballard and Jean-Louis Michel.
name: Robert Ballard

text: The Italian city of Castro is completely destroyed by the forces of Pope Innocent X, ending the Wars of Castro.
name: Innocent X

text: Mutsuhito, Emperor Meiji of Japan, marries Masako Ichijō, thereafter known as Empress Shōken.
name: Emperor Meiji of Japan

text: Arthur Rose Eldred is awarded the first Eagle Scout award of the Boy Scouts of America.
name: Arthur Rose Eldred

text: President Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam becomes the first foreign head of state to make a state visit to Australia.
name: Ngô Đình Diệm

text: In Moscow, the trial begins for 19-year-old pilot Mathias Rust, who flew his Cessna airplane into Red Square in May.
name: Mathias Rust

text: India's first solar observation mission: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launches Aditya-L1 from Satish Dhawan space centre.
name: Satish Dhawan

text: At the congress of Visegrád Charles I of Hungary mediates a reconciliation between two neighboring monarchs, John of Bohemia and Casimir III of Poland.
name: John of Bohemia

text: King Otto of Greece is forced to grant a constitution following an uprising in Athens.
name: Otto of Greece

text: American Civil War: Confederate General Leonidas Polk invades neutral Kentucky, prompting the state legislature to ask for Union assistance.
name: Leonidas Polk

text: French composer Albéric Magnard is killed defending his estate against invading German soldiers.
name: Albéric Magnard

text: Sir Malcolm Campbell reaches a speed of 304.331 miles per hour on the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah, becoming the first person to drive an automobile over 300 mph.
name: Malcolm Campbell

text: American Civil War Maryland Campaign: General Robert E. Lee takes the Army of Northern Virginia, and the war, into the North.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: Google is founded by Larry Page and Sergey Brin, two PhD students at Stanford University.
name: Sergey Brin

text: Fall of Nicolas Fouquet: Louis XIV's Superintendent of Finances is arrested in Nantes by D'Artagnan, captain of the king's musketeers.
name: Louis XIV

text: War of the Grand Alliance : A French warship commanded by Captain Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville defeated an English squadron at the Battle of Hudson's Bay.
name: Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville

text: Olympe de Gouges writes the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen.
name: Olympe de Gouges

text: Louis XVIII has to dissolve the Chambre introuvable ("Unobtainable Chamber").
name: Louis XVIII

text: Iva Toguri D'Aquino, a Japanese American suspected of being wartime radio propagandist Tokyo Rose, is arrested in Yokohama.
name: Iva Toguri D'Aquino

text: Poet Léopold Sédar Senghor is the first elected President of Senegal.
name: Léopold Sédar Senghor

text: Liz Truss is declared the winner of the UK Conservative Party leadership election, beating Rishi Sunak
name: Liz Truss

text: Leon Czolgosz, an unemployed anarchist, shoots and fatally wounds US President William McKinley at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York.
name: Leon Czolgosz

text: King Carol II of Romania abdicates and is succeeded by his son Michael. General Ion Antonescu becomes the Conducător of Romania.
name: Carol II of Romania

text: United States Secretary of State James F. Byrnes announces that the U.S. will follow a policy of economic reconstruction in postwar Germany.
name: James F. Byrnes

text: Prime Minister Hendrik Verwoerd, the architect of apartheid, is stabbed to death in Cape Town, South Africa during a parliamentary meeting.
name: Hendrik Verwoerd

text: Henry Every perpetrates one of the most profitable pirate raids in history with the capture of the Grand Mughal ship Ganj-i-Sawai. In response, Emperor Aurangzeb threatens to end all English trading in India.
name: Henry Every

text: Election of Stanisław August Poniatowski as the last ruler of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
name: Stanisław August Poniatowski

text: Dom Pedro I declares Brazil independent from Portugal on the shores of the Ipiranga Brook in São Paulo.
name: Pedro I

text: American Civil War: Atlanta is evacuated on orders of Union General William Tecumseh Sherman.
name: William Tecumseh Sherman

text: Alberto Santos-Dumont flies his 14-bis aircraft at Bagatelle, France successfully for the first time.
name: Alberto Santos-Dumont

text: Desmond Tutu becomes the first black man to lead the Anglican Diocese of Cape Town.
name: Desmond Tutu

text: St. Augustine, Florida is founded by Spanish admiral and Florida's first governor, Pedro Menéndez de Avilés.
name: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés

text: The Tonquin sets sail from New York Harbor with 33 employees of John Jacob Astor's newly created Pacific Fur Company on board.
name: John Jacob Astor

text: Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom dies at Balmoral Castle in Scotland after reigning for 70 years. Her son Charles, Prince of Wales, ascends the throne upon her death as Charles III.
name: Elizabeth II

text: James IV of Scotland is defeated and dies in the Battle of Flodden, ending Scotland's involvement in the War of the League of Cambrai.
name: James IV of Scotland

text: Thomas Cavendish in his ship Desire enters Plymouth and completes the first deliberately planned voyage of circumnavigation.
name: Thomas Cavendish

text: John Herschel takes the first glass plate photograph.
name: John Herschel

text: Kim Il Sung declares the establishment of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea).
name: Kim Il Sung

text: Elvis Presley appears on The Ed Sullivan Show for the first time.
name: Ed Sullivan

text: Elizabeth II becomes the longest reigning monarch of the United Kingdom.
name: Elizabeth II

text: The Battle of Pinkie, the last full-scale military confrontation between England and Scotland, resulting in a decisive victory for the forces of Edward VI.
name: Edward VI

text: American Revolutionary War: Nathan Hale volunteers to spy for the Continental Army.
name: Nathan Hale

text: At the Summer Olympics in Rome, Abebe Bikila becomes the first sub-Saharan African to win a gold medal, winning the marathon in bare feet.
name: Abebe Bikila

text: Death of Queen Elizabeth II: King Charles III is formally proclaimed as monarch at a meeting of the Accession Council in St James's Palace.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Charles XII of Sweden stops his march to conquer Moscow outside Smolensk, marking the turning point in the Great Northern War. The army is defeated nine months later in the Battle of Poltava, and the Swedish Empire ceases to be a major power.
name: Charles XII

text: Alexander Hamilton is appointed the first United States Secretary of the Treasury.
name: Alexander Hamilton

text: Captain William Morgan, an ex-freemason is arrested in Batavia, New York for debt after declaring that he would publish The Mysteries of Free Masonry, a book against Freemasonry. This sets into motion the events that led to his mysterious disappearance.
name: William Morgan

text: John Eliot Gardiner conducts Monteverdi's Vespro della Beata Vergine with the Monteverdi Choir at the Proms.
name: John Eliot Gardiner

text: Leó Szilárd, waiting for a red light on Southampton Row in Bloomsbury, conceives the idea of the nuclear chain reaction.
name: Leo Szilard

text: Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia, 'Messiah' of the Rastafari movement, is deposed following a military coup by the Derg, ending a reign of 58 years.
name: Haile Selassie

text: South African anti-apartheid activist Steve Biko dies in police custody.
name: Steve Biko

text: Abimael Guzmán, leader of the Shining Path, is captured by Peruvian special forces; shortly thereafter the rest of Shining Path's leadership fell as well.
name: Abimael Guzmán

text: Finnish War: In the Battle of Jutas, Swedish forces under Lieutenant General Georg Carl von Döbeln beat the Russians, making von Döbeln a Swedish war hero.
name: Georg Carl von Döbeln

text: The Greek Army rebels (OS date: September 3) against the autocratic rule of king Otto of Greece, demanding the granting of a constitution.
name: Otto of Greece

text: American Civil War: Union soldiers find a copy of Robert E. Lee's battle plans in a field outside Frederick, Maryland. It is the prelude to the Battle of Antietam.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: Elizabeth McCombs becomes the first woman elected to the New Zealand Parliament.
name: Elizabeth McCombs

text: Margaret Chase Smith is elected United States senator, and becomes the first woman to serve in both the U.S. House of Representatives and the United States Senate.
name: Margaret Chase Smith

text: Martin Luther King Jr. addresses a crowd of 20,000 West Berliners on Sunday, in Waldbühne.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Largest anti-Apartheid march in South Africa, led by Desmond Tutu.
name: Desmond Tutu

text: Genpei War: In the Battle of Ishibashiyama in Japan, the new military commander of the Minamoto clan, Minamoto no Yoritomo, is routed by Ōba Kagechika of the Taira clan.
name: Minamoto no Yoritomo

text: Grand Master António Manoel de Vilhena lays down the first stone of Fort Manoel in Malta.
name: António Manoel de Vilhena

text: U.S. President William McKinley dies after being mortally wounded on September 6 by anarchist Leon Czolgosz and is succeeded by Vice President Theodore Roosevelt.
name: Leon Czolgosz

text: President-elect of Lebanon Bachir Gemayel is assassinated.
name: Bachir Gemayel

text: Death of Queen Elizabeth II: The Queen's coffin is taken from Buckingham Palace, placed on a gun carriage of The King's Troop Royal Horse Artillery and moved in a procession to Westminster Hall for her lying in state over the next four days with the queue of mourners stretching for miles along the River Thames.
name: Elizabeth II

text: French Revolutionary Wars: Arthur Wellesley (later Duke of Wellington) sees his first combat at the Battle of Boxtel during the Flanders Campaign.
name: Arthur Wellesley

text: At the Superdome in New Orleans, Muhammad Ali outpoints Leon Spinks in a rematch to become the first boxer to win the world heavyweight title three times.
name: Leon Spinks

text: The Senate Judiciary Committee unanimously approves Sandra Day O'Connor to become the first female justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
name: Sandra Day O'Connor

text: During a CART race at the Lausitzring in Germany, former Formula One driver Alex Zanardi suffers a heavy accident resulting in him losing both his legs.
name: Alex Zanardi

text: National Hockey League commissioner Gary Bettman announces lockout of the players' union and cessation of operations by the NHL head office.
name: Gary Bettman

text: James Francis Edward Stuart, sometimes called the "Old Pretender", becomes the Jacobite claimant to the thrones of England and Scotland.
name: James Francis Edward Stuart

text: The Wall Street bombing: A bomb in a horse wagon explodes in front of the J. P. Morgan building in New York City killing 38 and injuring 400.
name: J. P. Morgan

text: Pakistan establishes its Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission with Abdus Salam as its head.
name: Abdus Salam

text: King Hussein of Jordan declares war against the Palestine Liberation Organization, the conflict came to be known as Black September.
name: Hussein of Jordan

text: Armenian champion swimmer Shavarsh Karapetyan saves 20 people from a trolleybus that had fallen into a Yerevan reservoir.
name: Shavarsh Karapetyan

text: The trial of the deposed Panamanian dictator Manuel Noriega ends in the United States with a 40-year sentence for drug trafficking and money laundering.
name: Manuel Noriega

text: Highest Galician nobility led by Pedro Fróilaz de Traba and the bishop Diego Gelmírez crown Alfonso VII as "King of Galicia".
name: Alfonso VII

text: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek writes a letter to the Royal Society describing "animalcules", later known as protozoa.
name: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek

text: American Civil War: George B. McClellan's Army of the Potomac halts the first invasion of the North by Robert E. Lee and his Army of Northern Virginia in the single-day Battle of Antietam, the bloodiest day in American military history.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: Andrew Fisher becomes Prime Minister of Australia for the third time.
name: Andrew Fisher

text: The Lehi (also known as the Stern gang) assassinates Count Folke Bernadotte, who was appointed by the United Nations to mediate between the Arab nations and Israel.
name: Folke Bernadotte

text: An audio tape of a private speech by Hungarian Prime Minister Ferenc Gyurcsány is leaked to the public, in which he confessed that his Hungarian Socialist Party had lied to win the 2006 election, sparking widespread protests across the country.
name: Ferenc Gyurcsány

text: Constantine the Great decisively defeats Licinius in the Battle of Chrysopolis, establishing Constantine's sole control over the Roman Empire.
name: Constantine the Great

text: American Civil War: John Bell Hood begins the Franklin-Nashville Campaign in an unsuccessful attempt to draw William Tecumseh Sherman back out of Georgia.
name: William Tecumseh Sherman

text: The U.S. bank Jay Cooke & Company declares bankruptcy, contributing to the Panic of 1873.
name: Jay Cooke

text: Margaret Chase Smith of Maine becomes the first woman elected to the United States Senate without completing another senator's term.
name: Margaret Chase Smith

text: The wedding of Constantine II of Greece and Princess Anne-Marie of Denmark takes place in Athens.
name: Constantine II of Greece

text: United States media magnate Ted Turner donates US$1 billion to the United Nations.
name: Ted Turner

text: Jamestown is burned to the ground by the forces of Nathaniel Bacon during Bacon's Rebellion.
name: Nathaniel Bacon

text: Mariano Rivera of the New York Yankees surpasses Trevor Hoffman to become Major League Baseball's all-time career saves leader with 602.
name: Mariano Rivera

text: The state funeral of Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom is held at Westminster Abbey, London.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Six days after a referendum, King Christian X of Denmark annuls the declaration of independence of the Faroe Islands.
name: Christian X of Denmark

text: Billie Jean King beats Bobby Riggs in the Battle of the Sexes tennis match at the Houston Astrodome.
name: Bobby Riggs

text: Roughly four million people, mostly students, demonstrate across the world to address climate change. Sixteen-year-old Greta Thunberg from Sweden leads the demonstration in New York City.
name: Greta Thunberg

text: British Secretary of War Lord Castlereagh and Foreign Secretary George Canning meet in a duel on Putney Heath, with Castlereagh wounding Canning in the thigh.
name: George Canning

text: Salvador Lutteroth establishes Mexican professional wrestling.
name: Salvador Lutteroth

text: Orlando Letelier is assassinated in Washington, D.C., at the order of Augusto Pinochet.
name: Orlando Letelier

text: Sandra Day O'Connor is unanimously approved by the U.S. Senate as the first female Supreme Court justice.
name: Sandra Day O'Connor

text: Nathan Hale is hanged for spying during the American Revolution.
name: Nathan Hale

text: Gail Halvorsen officially starts parachuting candy to children as part of the Berlin Airlift.
name: Gail Halvorsen

text: In Haiti, François Duvalier is elected president.
name: François Duvalier

text: American Revolution: John Paul Jones, naval commander of the United States, on board the USS Bonhomme Richard, wins the Battle of Flamborough Head.
name: John Paul Jones

text: Saudi National Day: Crown Prince (later king) Faisal of Saudi Arabia, on behalf of Ibn Saud, proclaims the unification of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the current iteration of the Third Saudi State.
name: Faisal of Saudi Arabia

text: An all-white jury in Mississippi finds Roy Bryant and J. W. Milam not guilty in the torture-murder of 14-year-old African American boy Emmett Till.
name: Emmett Till

text: The 1864 play Heath Cobblers by Aleksis Kivi is premiered for the first time in Oulu, Finland.
name: Aleksis Kivi

text: Jimmy Doolittle performs the first flight without a window, proving that full instrument flying from take off to landing is possible.
name: Jimmy Doolittle

text: The Cambodian monarchy is restored, with Norodom Sihanouk as king.
name: Norodom Sihanouk

text: Thabo Mbeki resigns as president of South Africa.
name: Thabo Mbeki

text: American Revolution: Ethan Allen surrenders to British forces after attempting to capture Montreal during the Battle of Longue-Pointe.
name: Ethan Allen

text: World War I: The end of the Battle of Megiddo, the climax of the British Army's Sinai and Palestine campaign under General Edmund Allenby.
name: Edmund Allenby

text: Dr. Frank Jobe performs first ulnar collateral ligament replacement surgery (better known as Tommy John surgery) on baseball player Tommy John.
name: Frank Jobe

text: Fijian Governor-General Penaia Ganilau is overthrown in a coup d'état led by Lieutenant colonel Sitiveni Rabuka.
name: Sitiveni Rabuka

text: As gangster Machine Gun Kelly surrenders to the FBI, he shouts out, "Don't shoot, G-Men!", which becomes a nickname for FBI agents.
name: Machine Gun Kelly

text: Spanish Civil War: Lluis Companys reshuffles the Generalitat de Catalunya, with the marxist POUM and anarcho-syndicalist CNT joining the government.
name: Lluís Companys

text: The Army of the Three Guarantees triumphantly enters Mexico City, led by Agustín de Iturbide. The following day Mexico is declared independent.
name: Agustín de Iturbide

text: King Constantine I of Greece abdicates his throne in favor of his eldest son, George II.
name: Constantine I of Greece

text: Bobby Jones wins the (pre-Masters) Grand Slam of golf.
name: Bobby Jones

text: The National League for Democracy is formed by Aung San Suu Kyi and others to fight dictatorship in Myanmar.
name: Aung San

text: American Revolution: Samuel Huntington is elected President of the Continental Congress, succeeding John Jay.
name: Samuel Huntington

text: Oscar I of Sweden-Norway is crowned king of Sweden.
name: Oscar I of Sweden

text: Bob Denard and a group of mercenaries take the islands of the Comoros in a coup.
name: Bob Denard

text: Ukrainian War of Independence: Insurgent forces led by Nestor Makhno defeat the Central Powers at the battle of Dibrivka.
name: Nestor Makhno

text: The coronation of Shah Abbas I of Persia occurs.
name: Abbas I of Persia

text: Ahmed III is forced to abdicate as the Ottoman sultan.
name: Ahmed III

text: The city of Tampere, Finland (belonging to Sweden at this time) is founded by King Gustav III of Sweden.
name: Gustav III of Sweden

text: Georges Carpentier knocked out former British heavyweight champion Joe Beckett a mere twenty seconds into the first round of their boxing match at Olympia in London.
name: Georges Carpentier

text: Muhammad Ali defeats Joe Frazier in a boxing match in Manila, Philippines.
name: Joe Frazier

text: The leader of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party, Pedro Sánchez, resigns. He would return to the position a year later.
name: Pedro Sánchez

text: Sixty people are killed and 867 others injured in a mass shooting at a country music festival at the Las Vegas Strip in the United States; the gunman, Stephen Paddock, later commits suicide.
name: Stephen Paddock

text: Battle of Andernach: Otto I, Holy Roman Emperor, crushes a rebellion against his rule, by a coalition of Eberhard of Franconia and other Frankish dukes.
name: Otto I

text: The Earl of Warwick's rebellion forces King Edward IV of England to flee to the Netherlands, restoring Henry VI to the throne.
name: Edward IV

text: American Revolutionary War: John André, a British Army officer, is hanged as a spy by the Continental Army.
name: John André

text: Ukrainian War of Independence: Mikhail Frunze orders the Red Army to immediately cease hostilities with the Revolutionary Insurgent Army of Ukraine.
name: Mikhail Frunze

text: Rafael Trujillo orders the execution of Haitians living in the border region of the Dominican Republic.
name: Rafael Trujillo

text: Thurgood Marshall is sworn in as the first African-American justice of the United States Supreme Court.
name: Thurgood Marshall

text: Mexican President Gustavo Díaz Ordaz orders soldiers to suppress a demonstration of unarmed students, ten days before the start of the 1968 Summer Olympics.
name: Gustavo Díaz Ordaz

text: President Roh Moo-hyun of South Korea goes to North Korea for an Inter-Korean summit with North Korean leader Kim Jong-il.
name: Kim Jong Il

text: The Duke of Montrose issues a warrant for the arrest of Rob Roy MacGregor.
name: Rob Roy MacGregor

text: Nadine Gordimer is announced as the winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature.
name: Nadine Gordimer

text: O. J. Simpson murder case: O. J. Simpson is acquitted of the murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.
name: O. J. Simpson

text: Svante Pääbo is awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
name: Svante Pääbo

text: Horace Rawlins wins the first U.S. Open Men's Golf Championship.
name: Horace Rawlins

text: Norman Rockwell's Willie Gillis character debuts on the cover of The Saturday Evening Post.
name: Norman Rockwell

text: Richard Noble sets a new land speed record of 633.468 miles per hour (1,019.468 km/h) at the Black Rock Desert in Nevada.
name: Richard Noble

text: With the signing of the Treaty of Zamora, King Alfonso VII of León and Castile recognises Portugal as a Kingdom.
name: Alfonso VII

text: Louis IX, Duke of Bavaria expels Jews from his jurisdiction.
name: Louis IX

text: Assassins attempt to kill Venetian statesman and scientist Paolo Sarpi.
name: Paolo Sarpi

text: The British Trade Commissioner, James Cross, is kidnapped by members of the Front de libération du Québec, triggering the October Crisis in Canada.
name: James Cross

text: Marc Garneau becomes the first Canadian in space.
name: Marc Garneau

text: Mordechai Vanunu's story in The Sunday Times reveals Israel's secret nuclear weapons.
name: Mordechai Vanunu

text: World War I: Combined Austro-Hungarian and German Central Powers, reinforced by the recently joined Bulgaria launched a new offensive against Serbia under command of August von Mackensen .
name: August von Mackensen

text: Revolution of 1934: The President of the autonomous government of Catalonia, Lluís Companys, proclaims the Catalan State with the support of the Worker's Alliance.
name: Lluís Companys

text: American Revolutionary War: The Americans defeat British forces under general John Burgoyne in the Second Battle of Saratoga, also known as the Battle of Bemis Heights, compelling Burgoyne's eventual surrender.
name: John Burgoyne

text: American Revolutionary War: American militia defeat royalist irregulars led by British major Patrick Ferguson at the Battle of Kings Mountain in South Carolina, often regarded as the turning point in the war's Southern theater.
name: Patrick Ferguson

text: Matthew Shepard, a gay student at the University of Wyoming, is found tied to a fence after being savagely beaten by two young adults in Laramie, Wyoming. He dies five days later.
name: Matthew Shepard

text: Jeanne Mance opens the first lay hospital of North America in Montreal.
name: Jeanne Mance

text: The New York Yankees's Don Larsen pitches the only perfect game in a World Series.
name: Don Larsen

text: Carloman I and Charlemagne are crowned kings of the Franks.
name: Carloman I

text: Peter the Great defeats the Swedes at the Battle of Lesnaya.
name: Peter the Great

text: Ioannis Kapodistrias, the first head of state of independent Greece, is assassinated.
name: Ioannis Kapodistrias

text: An Ustashe assassin kills King Alexander I of Yugoslavia and Louis Barthou, Foreign Minister of France, in Marseille.
name: Alexander I of Yugoslavia

text: A day after his capture, Ernesto "Che" Guevara is executed for attempting to incite a revolution in Bolivia.
name: Ernesto "Che" Guevara

text: Pakistani Taliban attempt to assassinate outspoken schoolgirl Malala Yousafzai.
name: Malala Yousafzai

text: Roman Catholic forces under Henry I, Duke of Guise, defeat the Protestants, capturing Philippe de Mornay among others.
name: Philippe de Mornay

text: Triton, the largest moon of the planet Neptune, is discovered by English astronomer William Lassell.
name: William Lassell

text: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Sultanate of Muscat, Neil Innes, sends a signal to the Sultanate's forces, accompanied with oil explorers, to penetrate Fahud, marking the beginning of Jebel Akhdar War.
name: Neil Innes

text: Sheikh Muszaphar Shukor becomes the first Malaysian in space on board Soyuz TMA-11.
name: Sheikh Muszaphar Shukor

text: Aboard the Space Shuttle Challenger, astronaut Kathryn D. Sullivan becomes the first American woman to perform a space walk.
name: Kathryn D. Sullivan

text: Air Botswana pilot Chris Phatswe steals an ATR 42 from Sir Seretse Khama International Airport and later crashes it into two other aircraft at the airport, killing himself.
name: Seretse Khama

text: The Salem witch trials are ended by a letter from Province of Massachusetts Bay Governor William Phips.
name: William Phips

text: Pedro I of Brazil is proclaimed the emperor.
name: Pedro I

text: World War I: British nurse Edith Cavell is executed by a German firing squad for helping Allied soldiers escape from occupied Belgium.
name: Edith Cavell

text: World War II: Desmond Doss is the first conscientious objector to receive the U.S. Medal of Honor.
name: Desmond Doss
