text: New Zealand holds its first general election under the new mixed-member proportional representation system, which led to Jim Bolger's National Party forming a coalition government with Winston Peters's New Zealand First.
name: Jim Bolger

text: Matthew Shepard, a gay student at University of Wyoming, dies five days after he was beaten outside of Laramie.
name: Matthew Shepard

text: Princess Eugenie marries Jack Brooksbank at St. George's Chapel, Windsor Castle.
name: Princess Eugenie

text: Rinchinbal Khan becomes the Khagan of the Mongols and Emperor of the Yuan dynasty, reigning for only 53 days.
name: Rinchinbal Khan

text: First known conversation in modern Hebrew by Eliezer Ben-Yehuda and friends.
name: Eliezer Ben-Yehuda

text: Prince Arthur, Duke of Connaught and Strathearn, becomes the first Governor General of Canada of royal descent.
name: Prince Arthur

text: Seven Years' War: Frederick the Great suffers a rare defeat at the Battle of Hochkirch.
name: Frederick the Great

text: Irish nationalist Daniel O'Connell is arrested by the British on charges of criminal conspiracy.
name: Daniel O'Connell

text: American Civil War: Confederate troops under the command of A. P. Hill fail to drive the Union Army completely out of Virginia.
name: A. P. Hill

text: English aviator Claude Grahame-White lands his aircraft on Executive Avenue near the White House in Washington, D.C.
name: Claude Grahame-White

text: Flying the Bell XS-1 over Muroc Army Air Field in California, Captain Chuck Yeager breaks the sound barrier in level flight, reaching Mach 1.05.
name: Chuck Yeager

text: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, leader of India's Untouchable caste, converts to Buddhism along with 385,000 of his followers (see Neo-Buddhism).
name: B. R. Ambedkar

text: Martin Luther King Jr. receives the Nobel Peace Prize for combating racial inequality through nonviolence.
name: Martin Luther King Jr.

text: Jim Hines becomes the first man ever to break the so-called "ten-second barrier" in the 100-meter sprint with a time of 9.95 seconds.
name: Jim Hines

text: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
name: Aung San

text: Felix Baumgartner successfully jumps to Earth from a balloon in the stratosphere.
name: Felix Baumgartner

text: President Lluís Companys of Catalonia is executed by the Francoist government.
name: Lluís Companys

text: Mexican chemist Luis E. Miramontes completes the synthesis of norethisterone, the basis of an early oral contraceptive.
name: Luis E. Miramontes

text: The Black Panther Party is created by Huey P. Newton and Bobby Seale.
name: Bobby Seale

text: A coup d'état in El Salvador overthrows President Carlos Humberto Romero and begins the 12 year-long Salvadoran Civil War.
name: Carlos Humberto Romero

text: A coup d'état in Burkina Faso overthrows and kills then President Thomas Sankara.
name: Thomas Sankara

text: The United States, under the Clinton administration, returns Haiti's first democratically elected president, Jean-Bertrand Aristide, to the island.
name: Jean-Bertrand Aristide

text: Abd ar-Rahman III becomes the eighth Emir of Córdoba.
name: Abd-ar-Rahman III

text: King Otto I defeats a Slavic revolt in what is now Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
name: Otto I

text: Mathematician William Whiston's predicted comet fails to strike the Earth.
name: William Whiston

text: Brigham Young University is founded in Provo, Utah.
name: Brigham Young

text: Margaret Sanger opens the first family planning clinic in the United States.
name: Margaret Sanger

text: Kingston, Jamaica is rocked by the Rodney riots, inspired by the barring of Walter Rodney from the country.
name: Walter Rodney

text: Desmond Tutu is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
name: Desmond Tutu

text: The English capture King David II of Scotland at Neville's Cross and imprison him for eleven years.
name: David II of Scotland

text: American Revolutionary War: British General John Burgoyne surrenders his army at Saratoga, New York.
name: John Burgoyne

text: The first commercial nuclear power station is officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II in Sellafield, England.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Directed by their chief Maurice Papon, Paris police massacre scores of Algerian protesters.
name: Maurice Papon

text: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre, a Christian church in Jerusalem, is completely destroyed by the Fatimid caliph Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah, who hacks the Church's foundations down to bedrock.
name: Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah

text: Count Bernhard von Bülow becomes chancellor of Germany.
name: Bernhard von Bülow

text: First Balkan War: King Peter I of Serbia issues a declaration "To the Serbian People", as his country joins the war.
name: Peter I of Serbia

text: The USSR's nuclear program receives plans for the United States plutonium bomb from Klaus Fuchs at the Los Alamos National Laboratory.
name: Klaus Fuchs

text: German Autumn: A set of events revolving around the kidnapping of Hanns Martin Schleyer and the hijacking of a Lufthansa flight by the Red Army Faction (RAF) comes to an end when Schleyer is murdered and various RAF members allegedly commit suicide.
name: Hanns Martin Schleyer

text: Riots in Chile's capital Santiago escalate into open battles, with attacks reported at nearly all of the city's 164 Metro stations. President Sebastián Piñera later announces a 15-day state of emergency in the capital.
name: Sebastián Piñera

text: Ferdinand II of Aragon marries Isabella I of Castile, a marriage that paves the way to the unification of Aragon and Castile into a single country, Spain.
name: Isabella I of Castile

text: Ray Bradbury's Fahrenheit 451 is published.
name: Ray Bradbury

text: Watergate scandal: "Saturday Night Massacre": United States President Richard Nixon fires U.S. Attorney General Elliot Richardson and Deputy Attorney General William Ruckelshaus after they refuse to fire special prosecutor Archibald Cox, who is finally fired by Solicitor General Robert Bork.
name: Robert Bork

text: The Sydney Opera House is opened by Elizabeth II after 14 years of construction.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Liz Truss steps down as British Prime Minister and leader of the Conservative Party amid the country's political crisis, serving for the least time of any British Prime Minister [49 days].
name: Liz Truss

text: Japanese Emperor Go-Kameyama abdicates in favor of rival claimant Go-Komatsu.
name: Go-Komatsu

text: Niki Lauda claims his third and final Formula One Drivers' Championship Title by half a point ahead of McLaren team-mate Alain Prost at the Portuguese Grand Prix.
name: Niki Lauda

text: André-Jacques Garnerin makes the first recorded parachute jump, from 1,000 metres (3,300 ft) above Paris.
name: André-Jacques Garnerin

text: Hawley Harvey Crippen (the first felon to be arrested with the help of radio) is convicted of poisoning his wife.
name: Hawley Harvey Crippen

text: In East Liverpool, Ohio, FBI agents shoot and kill notorious bank robber Pretty Boy Floyd.
name: Pretty Boy Floyd

text: Maurice Papon, an official in the Vichy government during World War II, is jailed for crimes against humanity.
name: Maurice Papon

text: Alberto Santos-Dumont flies an airplane in the first heavier-than-air flight in Europe.
name: Alberto Santos-Dumont

text: Yolanda Saldívar is found guilty of first-degree murder in the shooting death of popular Latin singer Selena.
name: Yolanda Saldívar

text: William Lassell discovers the moons Umbriel and Ariel orbiting Uranus.
name: William Lassell

text: First Sino-Japanese War: Battle of Jiuliancheng: Under the command of General Yamagata Aritomo, the Imperial Japanese Army covertly crosses the Yalu River into Qing territory and launches an assault on the fortifications at Hushan.
name: Yamagata Aritomo

text: Annie Edson Taylor becomes the first person to go over Niagara Falls in a barrel.
name: Annie Edson Taylor

text: Orville Wright remains in the air nine minutes and 45 seconds in a glider at Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina.
name: Orville Wright

text: Harry Houdini's last performance takes place at the Garrick Theatre in Detroit.
name: Harry Houdini

text: War of the Austrian Succession: A British fleet under Admiral Edward Hawke defeats the French at the Second Battle of Cape Finisterre.
name: Edward Hawke

text: War of 1812: The American frigate, USS United States, commanded by Stephen Decatur, captures the British frigate HMS Macedonian.
name: Stephen Decatur

text: After 74 days on hunger strike in Brixton Prison, England, the Sinn Féin Lord Mayor of Cork, Terence MacSwiney dies.
name: Terence MacSwiney

text: A Learjet 35 crashes in Mina near Aberdeen, South Dakota, killing all six people on board, including PGA golfer Payne Stewart and golf course designer Bruce Borland.
name: Payne Stewart

text: Imjin War: Korean Admiral Yi Sun-sin routs the Japanese Navy of 300 ships with only 13 ships at the Battle of Myeongnyang.
name: Yi Sun-sin

text: Liberian President Edward James Roye is deposed in a coup d'état.
name: Edward James Roye

text: Ida B. Wells publishes Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases.
name: Ida B. Wells

text: Ngô Đình Diệm proclaims himself as President of the newly created Republic of Vietnam.
name: Ngô Đình Diệm

text: Park Chung Hee, President of South Korea, is assassinated by Korean CIA head Kim Jae-gyu.
name: Park Chung Hee

text: A wave of protests forces Robert Guéï to step down as president after the Ivorian presidential election.
name: Robert Guéï

text: Constantine the Great is said to have received his famous Vision of the Cross.
name: Constantine the Great

text: Iskander Mirza, the first President of Pakistan, is deposed by General Ayub Khan, who had been appointed the enforcer of martial law by Mirza 20 days earlier.
name: Iskander Mirza

text: Major Rudolf Anderson of the United States Air Force becomes the only direct human casualty of the Cuban Missile Crisis when his U-2 reconnaissance airplane is shot down over Cuba by a Soviet-supplied surface-to-air missile.
name: Rudolf Anderson

text: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant founder and leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi kills himself and three children by detonating a suicide vest during the U.S. military Barisha raid in northwestern Syria.
name: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi

text: Ladislaus the Posthumous is crowned king of Bohemia in Prague.
name: Ladislaus the Posthumous

text: US President Barack Obama signs the Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act.
name: Matthew Shepard

text: Constantine the Great enters Rome after his victory at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge, stages a grand adventus in the city, and is met with popular jubilation. Maxentius' body is fished out of the Tiber and beheaded.
name: Constantine the Great

text: Battle of Brustem: Charles the Bold defeats Prince-Bishopric of Liège.
name: Charles the Bold

text: Mount Hood (Oregon) is named after Samuel Hood, 1st Viscount Hood by Lt. William E. Broughton who sighted the mountain near the mouth of the Willamette River.
name: Samuel Hood

text: American Civil War: Battle of Wauhatchie: Forces under Union General Ulysses S. Grant repel a Confederate attack led by General James Longstreet in one of the few night battles of the war, protecting the Union's recently opened supply line into Chattanooga, Tennessee.
name: James Longstreet

text: Space Shuttle Discovery blasts off on STS-95 with 77-year-old John Glenn on board, making him the oldest person to go into space at that time.
name: John Glenn

text: The Arabic-language news network Al Jazeera broadcasts an excerpt from a 2004 Osama bin Laden video in which the terrorist leader first admits direct responsibility for the September 11, 2001 attacks and references the 2004 U.S. presidential election.
name: Osama bin Laden

text: ADC Airlines Flight 053 crashes after takeoff from Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja, Nigeria killing 96 people and injuring nine.
name: Nnamdi Azikiwe

text: Jeremy Corbyn, Leader of the Labour Party and of the Opposition in the United Kingdom is suspended from the Labour Party following his response to findings from the EHRC on the issue of antisemitism within the party.
name: Jeremy Corbyn

text: Nat Turner is arrested for leading the bloodiest slave rebellion in United States history.
name: Nat Turner

text: The Rudd Concession is granted by Matabeleland to agents of Cecil Rhodes.
name: Cecil Rhodes

text: Holocaust: Anne and Margot Frank are deported from Auschwitz to the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, where they die from disease the following year, shortly before the end of WWII.
name: Margot Frank

text: Jackie Robinson of the Kansas City Monarchs signs a contract for the Brooklyn Dodgers, breaking the baseball color line.
name: Jackie Robinson

text: A squad of 120 North Korean Army commandos land in boats along a 25-mile long section of the eastern coast of South Korea in a failed attempt to overthrow the dictatorship of Park Chung Hee and bring about the reunification of Korea.
name: Park Chung Hee

text: Emperor Agustín de Iturbide attempts to dissolve the Congress of the Mexican Empire.
name: Agustín de Iturbide

text: Hungarian Revolution of 1956: A Revolutionary Headquarters is established in Hungary. Following Imre Nagy's announcement of October 30, banned non-Communist political parties are reformed, and the MDP is replaced by the MSZMP.  József Mindszenty is released from prison. The Soviet Politburo makes the decision to crush the Revolution.
name: József Mindszenty

text: Empress Matilda's reign as 'Lady of the English' ends with Stephen of Blois regaining the title of 'King of England'.
name: Empress Matilda

text: During the Time of Troubles, Polish troops are expelled from Moscow's Kitay-gorod by Russian troops under the command of Dmitry Pozharsky (22 October O.S.).
name: Dmitry Pozharsky

text: Italian Sport-Club Juventus is founded by a group of students of Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio.
name: Massimo d'Azeglio

text: Abolition of the Ottoman sultanate: The last sultan of the Ottoman Empire, Mehmed VI, abdicates.
name: Mehmed VI

text: American photographer Ansel Adams takes a picture of a moonrise over the town of Hernandez, New Mexico that would become one of the most famous images in the history of photography.
name: Ansel Adams

text: Quiz show scandals: Twenty-One game show contestant Charles Van Doren admits to a Congressional committee that he had been given questions and answers in advance.
name: Charles Van Doren

text: South Vietnamese President Ngô Đình Diệm is assassinated following a military coup.
name: Ngô Đình Diệm

text: King Saud of Saudi Arabia is deposed by a family coup, and replaced by his half-brother Faisal.
name: Saud of Saudi Arabia

text: French playwright, journalist and feminist Olympe de Gouges is guillotined.
name: Olympe de Gouges

text: George II of Greece regains his throne through a popular, though possibly fixed, plebiscite.
name: George II of Greece

text: Democratic Arkansas Governor Bill Clinton defeats Republican President George H. W. Bush and Independent candidate Ross Perot in the 1992 United States presidential election.
name: Ross Perot

text: Armagnac-Burgundian Civil War: Joan of Arc liberates Saint-Pierre-le-Moûtier.
name: Joan of Arc

text: The Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II against Spanish rule in the Viceroyalty of Peru begins.
name: Túpac Amaru II

text: Sir James Young Simpson, a Scottish physician, discovers the anaesthetic properties of chloroform.
name: James Young Simpson

text: Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour, becomes the prime minister of Piedmont-Sardinia, which soon expands to become Italy.
name: Camillo Benso

text: Japanese Prime Minister Hara Takashi is assassinated in Tokyo.
name: Hara Takashi

text: In Egypt, British archaeologist Howard Carter and his men find the entrance to Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings.
name: Howard Carter

text: At the Kasakela Chimpanzee Community in Tanzania, Dr. Jane Goodall observes chimpanzees creating tools, the first-ever observation in non-human animals.
name: Jane Goodall

text: Seven Years' War: Frederick the Great defeats the allied armies of France and the Holy Roman Empire at the Battle of Rossbach.
name: Frederick the Great

text: Women's suffrage in the United States: In defiance of the law, suffragist Susan B. Anthony votes for the first time, and is later fined $100.
name: Susan B. Anthony

text: Rabbi Meir Kahane, founder of the far-right Kach movement, is shot dead after a speech at a New York City hotel.
name: Meir Kahane

text: Synod of Rome: Emperor Otto I calls a council at St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. Pope John XII is deposed on charges of an armed rebellion against Otto.
name: Otto I

text: Nguyễn Ngọc Thơ is appointed to head the South Vietnamese government by General Dương Văn Minh's junta, five days after the latter deposed and assassinated President Ngô Đình Diệm.
name: Ngô Đình Diệm

text: Cleveland Browns relocation controversy: Art Modell announces that he signed a deal that would relocate the Cleveland Browns to Baltimore.
name: Art Modell

text: A cartoon by Thomas Nast in Harper's Weekly, is considered the first important use of an elephant as a symbol for the United States Republican Party.
name: Thomas Nast

text: Jesús García saves the entire town of Nacozari de García by driving a burning train full of dynamite six kilometres (3.7 miles) away before it can explode.
name: Jesús García

text: Jeannette Rankin is the first woman elected to the United States Congress.
name: Jeannette Rankin

text: Hungarian Revolution: János Kádár returns to Budapest in a Soviet armored convoy, officially taking office as the next Hungarian leader. By this point, most armed resistance has been defeated.
name: János Kádár

text: Douglas Wilder wins the governor's seat in Virginia, becoming the first elected African American governor in the United States.
name: Douglas Wilder

text: East German Prime Minister Willi Stoph, along with his entire cabinet, is forced to resign after huge anti-government protests.
name: Willi Stoph

text: Battle of Andrassos: Byzantines under Leo Phokas the Younger score a crushing victory over the Hamdanid Emir of Aleppo, Sayf al-Dawla.
name: Sayf al-Dawla

text: Trần Thánh Tông, the second emperor of the Trần dynasty, decides to pass the throne to his crown prince Trần Khâm and take up the post of Retired Emperor.
name: Trần Thánh Tông

text: Charles Edward Stuart invades England with an army of approximately 5,000 that would later participate in the Battle of Culloden.
name: Charles Edward Stuart

text: Manolis Andronikos, a Greek archaeologist and professor at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, discovers the tomb of Philip II of Macedon at Vergina.
name: Manolis Andronikos

text: The Battle of Fujigawa: Minamoto forces (30,000 men) under Minamoto no Yoritomo defeat Taira no Koremori during a night attack near the Fuji River but he escapes safely with the routed army.
name: Minamoto no Yoritomo

text: The Treaty of Aberconwy, a humiliating settlement forced on Llywelyn ap Gruffudd by King Edward I of England, brings a temporary end to the Welsh Wars.
name: Edward I

text: Kentucky marshals abduct abolitionist minister Calvin Fairbank from Jeffersonville, Indiana, and take him to Kentucky to stand trial for helping a slave escape.
name: Calvin Fairbank

text: Ten Kingdoms: Li Bian usurps the throne and deposes Emperor Yang Pu. The Wu State is replaced by Li (now called "Xu Zhigao"), who becomes the first ruler of Southern Tang.
name: Li Bian

text: Battle of Varna: The crusading forces of King Władysław III of Poland (aka Ulaszlo I of Hungary and Władysław III of Varna) are defeated by the Turks under Sultan Murad II and Władysław is killed.
name: Władysław III

text: The passenger ship Stephen Whitney is wrecked in thick fog off the southern coast of Ireland, killing 92 of the 110 on board. The disaster results in the construction of the Fastnet Rock lighthouse.
name: Stephen Whitney

text: Longtime Bulgarian leader Todor Zhivkov is removed from office and replaced by Petar Mladenov.
name: Todor Zhivkov

text: In Nigeria, playwright and environmental activist Ken Saro-Wiwa, along with eight others from the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (Mosop), are hanged by government forces.
name: Ken Saro-Wiwa

text: President of Bolivia Evo Morales and several of his government resign after 19 days of civil protests and a recommendation from the military.
name: Evo Morales

text: Treaty of Granada: Louis XII of France and Ferdinand II of Aragon agree to divide the Kingdom of Naples between them.
name: Louis XII

text: In Jerusalem, Virginia, Nat Turner is hanged after inciting a violent slave uprising.
name: Nat Turner

text: Emperor Charles I of Austria relinquishes power.
name: Charles I of Austria

text: A military coup against President Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam is crushed.
name: Ngô Đình Diệm

text: Southern Rhodesia's Prime Minister Ian Smith unilaterally declares the colony independent as the unrecognised state of Rhodesia.
name: Ian Smith

text: Vietnam War: In a propaganda ceremony in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, three American prisoners of war are released by the Viet Cong and turned over to "new left" antiwar activist Tom Hayden.
name: Tom Hayden

text: Australian constitutional crisis of 1975: Australian Governor-General Sir John Kerr dismisses the government of Gough Whitlam, appoints Malcolm Fraser as caretaker Prime Minister and announces a general election to be held in early December.
name: Gough Whitlam

text: Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II unveils the New Zealand War Memorial in London, United Kingdom, commemorating the loss of soldiers from the New Zealand Army and the British Army.
name: Elizabeth II

text: First Balkan War: King George I of Greece makes a triumphal entry into Thessaloniki after its liberation from 482 years of Ottoman rule.
name: George I of Greece

text: American Revolutionary War: Patriot revolutionary forces under Gen. Richard Montgomery occupy Montreal.
name: Richard Montgomery

text: James Braid first sees a demonstration of animal magnetism by Charles Lafontaine, which leads to his study of the subject he eventually calls hypnotism.
name: James Braid

text: World War I: Prime Minister of Australia Billy Hughes is expelled from the Labor Party over his support for conscription.
name: Billy Hughes

text: Pioneering female journalist Nellie Bly (aka Elizabeth Cochrane) begins a successful attempt to travel around the world in less than 80 days. She completes the trip in 72 days.
name: Nellie Bly

text: Aviator Eugene Burton Ely performs the first takeoff from a ship in Hampton Roads, Virginia, taking off from a makeshift deck on the USS Birmingham in a Curtiss pusher.
name: Eugene Burton Ely

text: The Joensuu City Hall, designed by Eliel Saarinen, was inaugurated in Joensuu, Finland.
name: Eliel Saarinen

text: American physicist Theodore Maiman is given a patent for his ruby laser systems, the world's first laser.
name: Theodore Maiman

text: In the United Kingdom, Princess Anne marries Captain Mark Phillips, in Westminster Abbey.
name: Mark Phillips

text: During a British House of Commons debate, Labour MP Tam Dalyell poses what would become known as the West Lothian question, referring to issues related to devolution in the United Kingdom.
name: Tam Dalyell

text: Cambodian Prince Norodom Sihanouk returns to Phnom Penh after thirteen years in exile.
name: Norodom Sihanouk

text: Pike Expedition: Lieutenant Zebulon Pike spots a mountain peak while near the Colorado foothills of the Rocky Mountains. It is later named Pikes Peak in his honor.
name: Zebulon Pike

text: American Civil War: Union General William Tecumseh Sherman begins his March to the Sea.
name: William Tecumseh Sherman

text: Brazil is declared a republic by Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca as Emperor Pedro II is deposed in a military coup.
name: Deodoro da Fonseca

text: Craig Breedlove sets a land speed record of 600.601 mph (966.574 km/h) in his car, the Spirit of America, at the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah.
name: Craig Breedlove

text: A package from Unabomber Ted Kaczynski begins smoking in the cargo hold of a flight from Chicago to Washington, D.C., forcing the plane to make an emergency landing.
name: Ted Kaczynski

text: Canadian rebel leader of the Métis and "Father of Manitoba" Louis Riel is executed for treason.
name: Louis Riel

text: English engineer John Ambrose Fleming receives a patent for the thermionic valve (vacuum tube).
name: John Ambrose Fleming

text: English explorer, writer and courtier Sir Walter Raleigh goes on trial for treason.
name: Walter Raleigh

text: The city of Kuopio, Finland (belonging to Sweden at this time) is founded by King Gustav III of Sweden.
name: Gustav III of Sweden

text: José Miguel Carrera, Chilean founding father, is sworn in as President of the executive Junta of the government of Chile.
name: José Miguel Carrera

text: American Civil War: Siege of Knoxville begins: During the Knoxville campaign, Confederate forces under General James Longstreet besiege the city of Knoxville, Tennessee and its Union defenders led by General Ambrose Burnside.
name: James Longstreet

text: First assassination attempt against Umberto I of Italy by anarchist Giovanni Passannante, who was armed with a dagger. The King survived with a slight wound in an arm. Prime Minister Benedetto Cairoli blocked the aggressor, receiving an injury in a leg.
name: Umberto I of Italy

text: Alberto Fujimori is removed from office as president of Peru.
name: Alberto Fujimori

text: The future Frederick the Great of Prussia is granted a pardon by his father and is released from confinement.
name: Frederick the Great

text: King Christian IX of Denmark signs the November constitution that declares Schleswig to be part of Denmark. This is seen by the German Confederation as a violation of the London Protocol and leads to the German-Danish war of 1864.
name: Christian IX of Denmark

text: Susan B. Anthony and 14 other women are arrested for voting illegally in the United States presidential election of 1872.
name: Susan B. Anthony

text: Prince Carl of Denmark becomes King Haakon VII of Norway.
name: Haakon VII of Norway

text: World War I: First Battle of the Somme: In France, British Expeditionary Force commander Douglas Haig calls off the battle which started on July 1, 1916.
name: Douglas Haig

text: In Jonestown, Guyana, Jim Jones leads his Peoples Temple to a mass murder-suicide that claimed 918 lives in all, 909 of them in Jonestown itself, including over 270 children.
name: Jim Jones

text: Shiite Muslim kidnappers in Lebanon release Anglican Church envoys Terry Waite and Thomas Sutherland.
name: Terry Waite

text: Iraq disarmament crisis: United Nations weapons inspectors led by Hans Blix arrive in Iraq.
name: Hans Blix

text: Pope Tawadros II of Alexandria becomes the 118th Pope of the Coptic Orthodox Church of Alexandria.
name: Pope Tawadros II of Alexandria

text: Télé Monte Carlo, Europe's oldest private television channel, is launched by Prince Rainier III.
name: Rainier III

text: Apollo program: Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean land at Oceanus Procellarum (the "Ocean of Storms") and become the third and fourth humans to walk on the Moon.
name: Alan Bean

text: John Carpenter becomes the first person to win the top prize in the TV game show Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?
name: John Carpenter

text: John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy, and Louis of Valois, Duke of Orléans, agree to a truce, but Burgundy would kill Orléans three days later.
name: John the Fearless

text: Garnier Expedition: French forces under Lieutenant Francis Garnier captured Hanoi from the Vietnamese.
name: Francis Garnier

text: Mexican Revolution: Francisco I. Madero issues the Plan de San Luis Potosí, denouncing Mexican President Porfirio Díaz, calling for a revolution to overthrow the government of Mexico, effectively starting the Mexican Revolution.
name: Francisco I. Madero

text: Savings and loan crisis: The United States Senate Ethics Committee issues a stern censure of California senator Alan Cranston for his "dealings" with savings-and-loan executive Charles Keating.
name: Alan Cranston

text: A court in Taliban-controlled Afghanistan declares accused terrorist Osama bin Laden "a man without a sin" in regard to the 1998 U.S. embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania.
name: Osama bin Laden

text: Jimmie Johnson wins his seventh NASCAR Cup Series championship to tie Richard Petty and Dale Earnhardt for the most all-time.
name: Dale Earnhardt

text: Rebecca Latimer Felton of Georgia takes the oath of office, becoming the first female United States Senator.
name: Rebecca Latimer Felton

text: American disc jockey Alan Freed, who had popularized the term "rock and roll" and music of that style, is fired from WABC radio over allegations he had participated in the payola scandal.
name: Alan Freed

text: Vietnam War: American General William Westmoreland tells news reporters: "I am absolutely certain that whereas in 1965 the enemy was winning, today he is certainly losing."
name: William Westmoreland

text: Voters in South Korea overwhelmingly approve a new constitution, giving legitimacy to Park Chung Hee and the Fourth Republic.
name: Park Chung Hee

text: United States Navy intelligence analyst Jonathan Pollard is arrested for spying after being caught giving Israel classified information on Arab nations. He is subsequently sentenced to life in prison.
name: Jonathan Pollard

text: Robert Mugabe formally resigns as President of Zimbabwe, after thirty-seven years in office.
name: Robert Mugabe

text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is indicted on charges of bribery, fraud, and breach of trust.
name: Benjamin Netanyahu

text: Canadian journalist and politician William Lyon Mackenzie calls for a rebellion against the United Kingdom in his essay "To the People of Upper Canada", published in his newspaper The Constitution.
name: William Lyon Mackenzie

text: Rose Revolution: Georgian president Eduard Shevardnadze resigns following weeks of mass protests over flawed elections.
name: Eduard Shevardnadze

text: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is elected president of Liberia and becomes the first woman to lead an African country.
name: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf

text: Peter I of Cyprus ascends the throne of Cyprus after his father, Hugh IV of Cyprus, abdicates.
name: Peter I of Cyprus

text: Hundred Years' War: Joan of Arc unsuccessfully besieges La Charité.
name: Joan of Arc

text: Anna Sewell's animal welfare novel Black Beauty is published.
name: Anna Sewell

text: Donald Johanson and Tom Gray discover the 40% complete Australopithecus afarensis skeleton, nicknamed "Lucy" (after The Beatles song "Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds"), in the Awash Valley of Ethiopia's Afar Depression.
name: Donald Johanson

text: After a week of mass protests against the Communist regime known as the Velvet Revolution, Miloš Jakeš and the entire Politburo of the Czechoslovak Communist Party resign from office.  This brings an effective end to Communist rule in Czechoslovakia.
name: Miloš Jakeš

text: Crossair Flight 3597 crashes in Bassersdorf near Zurich Airport, killing 24 people, including singer Melanie Thornton and two members of the German band Passion Fruit.
name: Melanie Thornton

text: Five days after the general elections which resulted in a hung parliament, opposition leader and former deputy prime minister Anwar Ibrahim is officially named as the 10th prime minister of Malaysia.
name: Anwar Ibrahim

text: King Minkhaung I becomes king of Ava.
name: Minkhaung I

text: King Ferdinand VI of Spain grants royal protection to the Beaterio de la Compañia de Jesus, now known as the Congregation of the Religious of the Virgin Mary.
name: Ferdinand VI of Spain

text: Partitions of Poland: Stanisław August Poniatowski, the last king of independent Poland, is forced to abdicate and is exiled to Russia.
name: Stanisław August Poniatowski

text: Prince Carl of Denmark arrives in Norway to become King Haakon VII of Norway.
name: Haakon VII of Norway

text: Georgios Papadopoulos, head of the military Regime of the Colonels in Greece, is ousted in a hardliners' coup led by Brigadier General Dimitrios Ioannidis.
name: Dimitrios Ioannidis

text: Former Senator Benigno Aquino Jr., is found guilty by the Philippine Military Commission No. 2 and is sentenced to death by firing squad. He is later assassinated in 1983.
name: Benigno Aquino Jr.

text: A five-year-old Cuban boy, Elián González, is rescued by fishermen while floating in an inner tube off the Florida coast.
name: Elián González

text: Official opening of Thomas Telford's Pontcysyllte Aqueduct.
name: Thomas Telford

text: Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon become the first people to enter the tomb of Pharaoh Tutankhamun in over 3,000 years.
name: Howard Carter

text: The Constituent Assembly of India adopts the constitution presented by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
name: B. R. Ambedkar

text: The Berners Street hoax is perpetrated by Theodore Hook in the City of Westminster, London.
name: Theodore Hook

text: Saint Catherine Labouré experiences a Marian apparition.
name: Catherine Labouré

text: American Civil War: Confederate cavalry leader John Hunt Morgan and several of his men escape the Ohio Penitentiary and return safely to the South.
name: John Hunt Morgan

text: In Romania, the ruling Iron Guard fascist party assassinates over 60 of arrested King Carol II of Romania's aides and other political dissidents.
name: Carol II of Romania

text: Alger Hiss is released from prison after serving 44 months for perjury.
name: Alger Hiss

text: The Provisional IRA assassinates Ross McWhirter, after a press conference in which McWhirter had announced a reward for the capture of those responsible for multiple bombings and shootings across England.
name: Ross McWhirter

text: The centre-left Labour Party takes control of the New Zealand government with leader Helen Clark becoming the first elected female prime minister in New Zealand's history.
name: Helen Clark

text: Irish nationalist Arthur Griffith founds Sinn Féin as a political party with the main aim of establishing a dual monarchy in Ireland.
name: Arthur Griffith

text: The first pulsar (PSR B1919+21, in the constellation of Vulpecula) is discovered by two astronomers Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish.
name: Jocelyn Bell Burnell

text: American Civil War: Union forces under General Ambrose Burnside successfully defend Knoxville, Tennessee from an attack by Confederate forces under General James Longstreet in the Battle of Fort Sanders during the Siege of Knoxville.
name: James Longstreet

text: Colorado War: Colorado volunteers led by Colonel John Chivington massacre at least 150 Cheyenne and Arapaho noncombatants inside Colorado Territory.
name: John Chivington

text: U.S. Admiral Richard E. Byrd leads the first expedition to fly over the South Pole.
name: Richard E. Byrd

text: Great Northern War: King Charles XII of Sweden dies during a siege of the fortress of Fredriksten in Norway.
name: Charles XII

text: Crimean War: Battle of Sinop: The Imperial Russian Navy under Pavel Nakhimov destroys the Ottoman fleet under Osman Pasha at Sinop, a sea port in northern Turkey.
name: Pavel Nakhimov

text: World War II: Signing of the Sino-Japanese Treaty of 1940 between the Empire of Japan and the newly formed Wang Jingwei-led Reorganized National Government of the Republic of China. This treaty was considered so unfair to China that it was compared to the Twenty-One Demands.
name: Wang Jingwei

text: Diarist John Evelyn records skating on the frozen lake in St James's Park, London, watched by Charles II and Queen Catherine.
name: John Evelyn

text: José Núñez de Cáceres wins the independence of the Dominican Republic from Spain and names the new territory the Republic of Spanish Haiti.
name: José Núñez de Cáceres

text: Pedro I is crowned Emperor of Brazil.
name: Pedro I

text: Argentine general Juan Lavalle makes a coup against governor Manuel Dorrego, beginning the Decembrist revolution.
name: Juan Lavalle

text: Arsenal Women 11-1 Bristol City Women breaks the record for most goals scored in a FA Women's Super League match, with Vivianne Miedema involved in ten of the eleven Arsenal goals.
name: Vivianne Miedema

text: Gough Whitlam is elected the 21st Prime Minister of Australia in the 1972 Australian federal election, defeating William McMahon and leading the Australian Labor Party back into office after 23 years in Opposition.
name: Gough Whitlam

text: Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar is shot and killed by police in Medellín.
name: Pablo Escobar

text: American Revolutionary War: USS Alfred becomes the first vessel to fly the Grand Union Flag (the precursor to the Stars and Stripes); the flag is hoisted by John Paul Jones.
name: John Paul Jones

text: The Jovian moon Himalia is discovered by Charles Dillon Perrine at California's Lick Observatory.
name: Charles Dillon Perrine

text: Modern neon lighting is first demonstrated by Georges Claude at the Paris Motor Show.
name: Georges Claude

text: Väinö Linna's war novel The Unknown Soldier (Tuntematon sotilas) is published.
name: Väinö Linna

text: At Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, South Africa, a transplant team headed by Christiaan Barnard carries out the first heart transplant on a human (53-year-old Louis Washkansky).
name: Christiaan Barnard

text: Taiwan holds its first full local elections; James Soong elected as the first and only directly elected Governor of Taiwan, Chen Shui-bian became the first directly elected Mayor of Taipei, Wu Den-yih became the first directly elected Mayor of Kaohsiung.
name: James Soong

text: Austrasian king Carloman I dies, leaving his brother Charlemagne as sole king of the Frankish Kingdom.
name: Carloman I

text: Charles Edward Stuart's army reaches Derby, its furthest point during the Second Jacobite Rising.
name: Charles Edward Stuart

text: The United States House of Representatives adopts articles of impeachment against Supreme Court Justice Samuel Chase.
name: Samuel Chase

text: American Civil War: Confederate General James Longstreet lifts his unsuccessful siege of Knoxville, Tennessee after failing to capture the city.
name: James Longstreet

text: Launch of Gemini 7 with crew members Frank Borman and Jim Lovell. The Gemini 7 spacecraft was the passive target for the first crewed space rendezvous performed by the crew of Gemini 6A.
name: Frank Borman

text: Black Panther Party members Fred Hampton and Mark Clark are shot and killed during a raid by 14 Chicago police officers.
name: Fred Hampton

text: Jean-Bédel Bokassa, president of the Central African Republic, crowns himself Emperor Bokassa I of the Central African Empire.
name: Jean-Bédel Bokassa

text: Following the murder of Mayor George Moscone, Dianne Feinstein becomes San Francisco's first female mayor.
name: Dianne Feinstein

text: Terry A. Anderson is released after seven years in captivity as a hostage in Beirut; he is the last and longest-held American hostage in Lebanon.
name: Terry A. Anderson

text: Mary McLeod Bethune founds the National Council of Negro Women in New York City.
name: Mary McLeod Bethune

text: Subscriber Trunk Dialling (STD) is inaugurated in the United Kingdom by Queen Elizabeth II when she speaks to the Lord Provost in a call from Bristol to Edinburgh.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Lloyd J. Old discovers the first linkage between the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and disease—mouse leukemia—opening the way for the recognition of the importance of the MHC in the immune response.
name: Lloyd J. Old

text: Leonid Kravchuk is elected the first president of Ukraine.
name: Leonid Kravchuk

text: Commodore Frank Bainimarama overthrows the government in Fiji.
name: Frank Bainimarama

text: Charles Edward Stuart's army begins retreat during the second Jacobite Rising.
name: Charles Edward Stuart

text: in Venezuela, Hugo Chávez is victorious in presidential elections.
name: Hugo Chávez

text: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette, arranges to enter the American military as a major general.
name: Gilbert du Motier

text: Prince Rainier III of Monaco revises the principality's constitution, devolving some of his power to advisory and legislative councils.
name: Rainier III

text: Pakistan President Yahya Khan announces the formation of a coalition government with Nurul Amin as Prime Minister and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto as Deputy Prime Minister.
name: Yahya Khan

text: King Gustaf V of Sweden accedes to the Swedish throne.
name: Gustaf V of Sweden

text: Two days after coming into existence, the Irish Free State executes four leaders of the Irish Republican Army: Liam Mellows, Rory O'Connor, Joe McKelvey and Dick Barrett.
name: Joe McKelvey

text: John Lennon is murdered by Mark David Chapman in front of The Dakota in New York City.
name: Mark David Chapman

text: Damascus falls to rebels after Syrian troops withdraw and president Bashar al-Assad leaves the country as his government collapses. Israel as a result invaded into the buffer zone between Syria and the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights.
name: Bashar al-Assad

text: The Qing dynasty of China, led by Emperor Hong Taiji, invades Joseon.
name: Hong Taiji

text: The League of Cambrai is formed by Pope Julius II, Louis XII of France, Maximilian I, Holy Roman Emperor and Ferdinand II of Aragon as an alliance against Venice.
name: Louis XII

text: The Royal Netherlands Marine Corps is founded by Michiel de Ruyter.
name: Michiel de Ruyter

text: American Civil War: Sherman's March to the Sea: Major General William Tecumseh Sherman's Union Army troops reach the outer Confederate defenses of Savannah, Georgia.
name: William Tecumseh Sherman

text: Alfred Jarry's Ubu Roi premieres in Paris. A riot breaks out at the end of the performance.
name: Alfred Jarry

text: Selma Lagerlöf becomes the first female writer to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.
name: Selma Lagerlöf

text: Abdication Crisis: Edward VIII signs the Instrument of Abdication.
name: Edward VIII

text: World War II: Battle of the Philippines: Imperial Japanese forces under the command of General Masaharu Homma land on Luzon.
name: Masaharu Homma

text: Democracy is restored in Argentina with the inauguration of President Raúl Alfonsín.
name: Raúl Alfonsín

text: Mongolian Revolution: At the country's first open pro-democracy public demonstration, Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj announces the establishment of the Mongolian Democratic Union.
name: Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj

text: Nursultan Nazarbayev is sworn in as the 1st President of Kazakhstan.
name: Nursultan Nazarbayev

text: Helen Clark is sworn in as Prime Minister of New Zealand, the second woman to hold the post and the first following an election.
name: Helen Clark

text: Emperor Xian of Han is forced to abdicate the throne by Cao Cao's son Cao Pi, ending the Han dynasty.
name: Emperor Xian of Han

text: World War I: British General Edmund Allenby enters Jerusalem on foot and declares martial law.
name: Edmund Allenby

text: Abdication Crisis: Edward VIII's abdication as King of the United Kingdom and the British Dominions beyond the Seas, and Emperor of India, becomes effective.
name: Edward VIII

text: The Lufthansa heist is committed by a group led by Lucchese family associate Jimmy Burke. It was the largest cash robbery ever committed on American soil, at that time.
name: Jimmy Burke

text: Father Edward J. Flanagan founds Boys Town as a farm village for wayward boys.
name: Father Edward J. Flanagan

text: American Civil War: At the Battle of Fredericksburg, Confederate General Robert E. Lee repulses attacks by Union Major General Ambrose Burnside on Marye's Heights, inflicting heavy casualties.
name: Robert E. Lee

text: Archbishop Makarios III becomes the first President of Cyprus.
name: Makarios III

text: While Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia visits Brazil, his Imperial Bodyguard seizes the capital and proclaims him deposed and his son, Crown Prince Asfa Wossen, Emperor.
name: Haile Selassie

text: Constantine II of Greece attempts an unsuccessful counter-coup against the Regime of the Colonels.
name: Constantine II of Greece

text: American Civil War: The Confederate victory under General James Longstreet at the Battle of Bean's Station in East Tennessee ends the Knoxville Campaign, but achieves very little as Longstreet returns to Virginia next spring.
name: James Longstreet

text: Portuguese President Sidónio Pais is assassinated.
name: Sidónio Pais

text: Wilma Mankiller takes office as the first woman elected to serve as Principal Chief of the Cherokee Nation.
name: Wilma Mankiller

text: Stephen III of Moldavia defeats Matthias Corvinus of Hungary, with the latter being injured thrice, at the Battle of Baia.
name: Matthias Corvinus

text: The Pushkin House is established in Saint Petersburg, Russia, to preserve the cultural heritage of Alexander Pushkin.
name: Alexander Pushkin

text: John Paul Getty III, grandson of American billionaire J. Paul Getty, is found alive near Naples, Italy, after being kidnapped by an Italian gang on July 10.
name: J. Paul Getty

text: Hundred Years' War: Henry VI of England is crowned King of France at Notre Dame in Paris.
name: Henry VI of England

text: American Civil War: Confederate President Jefferson Davis appoints General Joseph E. Johnston to replace General Braxton Bragg as commander of the Army of Tennessee.
name: Joseph E. Johnston

text: King Kyawswa of Pagan is overthrown by the three Myinsaing brothers, marking the de facto end of the Pagan Kingdom.
name: Kyawswa of Pagan

text: Antanas Smetona assumes power in Lithuania as the 1926 coup d'état is successful.
name: Antanas Smetona

text: World War II: Battle of the Bulge: Malmedy massacre: American 285th Field Artillery Observation Battalion POWs are shot by Waffen-SS Kampfgruppe Joachim Peiper.
name: Joachim Peiper

text: Troops loyal to Emperor Haile Selassie in Ethiopia crush the coup that began December 13, returning power to their leader upon his return from Brazil. Haile Selassie absolves his son of any guilt.
name: Haile Selassie

text: The United States celebrates its first Thanksgiving, marking the recent victory by the American rebels over British General John Burgoyne at Saratoga in October.
name: John Burgoyne

text: Surrender of the frigate La Lutine by French Royalists to Lord Samuel Hood; renamed HMS Lutine, she later becomes a famous treasure wreck.
name: Samuel Hood

text: Soviet Soyuz Programme: Soyuz 13, crewed by cosmonauts Valentin Lebedev and Pyotr Klimuk, is launched from Baikonur in the Soviet Union.
name: Pyotr Klimuk

text: William Pitt the Younger becomes the youngest Prime Minister of the United Kingdom at 24.
name: William Pitt

text: French Revolutionary Wars: Two British frigates under Commodore Horatio Nelson and two Spanish frigates under Commodore Don Jacobo Stuart engage in battle off the coast of Murcia.
name: Horatio Nelson

text: King Constantine I is restored as King of the Hellenes after the death of his son Alexander of Greece and a plebiscite.
name: Alexander of Greece

text: German serial killer Fritz Haarmann is sentenced to death for a series of murders.
name: Fritz Haarmann

text: Three Indian revolutionaries, Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh and Ashfaqulla Khan, are executed by the British Raj for participation in the Kakori conspiracy.
name: Ashfaqulla Khan

text: Irish-born physician John Bodkin Adams is arrested in connection with the suspicious deaths of more than 160 patients. Eventually he is convicted only of minor charges.
name: John Bodkin Adams

text: Assassination of Luis Carrero Blanco: A car bomb planted by ETA in Madrid kills three people, including the Prime Minister of Spain, Admiral Luis Carrero Blanco.
name: Luis Carrero Blanco

text: The United States invasion of Panama deposes Manuel Noriega.
name: Manuel Noriega

text: Elizabeth II becomes the oldest monarch in the history of the United Kingdom, surpassing Queen Victoria, who lived for 81 years and 243 days.
name: Elizabeth II

text: Pope Honorius II is consecrated, having been elected after the controversial dethroning of Pope Celestine II.
name: Honorius II

text: James Naismith, a Canadian-American gym teacher at Springfield College, publishes the first rules for the game now known as basketball and brings it to his class, which then plays the first game of basketball.
name: James Naismith

text: American anarchist Emma Goldman is deported to Russia.
name: Emma Goldman

text: The house of former British Prime Minister Edward Heath is attacked by members of the Provisional IRA.
name: Edward Heath

text: Romanian Revolution: Communist President of Romania Nicolae Ceaușescu is overthrown by Ion Iliescu after days of bloody confrontations. The deposed dictator and his wife Elena flee Bucharest in a helicopter as protesters erupt in cheers.
name: Ion Iliescu

text: General Walton Walker dies in a jeep accident and is replaced by General Matthew Ridgway in the Eighth United States Army.
name: Matthew Ridgway

text: First successful kidney transplant is performed by J. Hartwell Harrison and Joseph Murray.
name: Joseph Murray

text: The first film adaptation of Väinö Linna's novel The Unknown Soldier, directed by Edvin Laine, premieres.
name: Väinö Linna

text: The Immaculate Reception is caught by Franco Harris to win the Pittsburgh Steelers their first ever playoff victory, after defeating the Oakland Raiders.
name: Franco Harris

text: Reginald Fessenden transmits the first radio broadcast; consisting of a poetry reading, a violin solo, and a speech.
name: Reginald Fessenden

text: Air France Flight 8969 is hijacked on the ground at Houari Boumediene Airport, Algiers, Algeria. Over the course of three days three passengers are killed, as are all four terrorists.
name: Houari Boumediene

text: Roman Emperor Constantine the Great elevates his youngest son Constans to the rank of Caesar.
name: Constantine the Great

text: Eleven-year-old John IV Laskaris of the restored Eastern Roman Empire is deposed and blinded by orders of his co-ruler Michael VIII Palaiologos.
name: John IV Laskaris

text: Battle of Tucapel: Mapuche rebels under Lautaro defeat the Spanish conquistadors and executes the governor of Chile, Pedro de Valdivia.
name: Pedro de Valdivia

text: Halley's Comet is sighted by Johann Georg Palitzsch, confirming Edmund Halley's prediction of its passage.  This was the first passage of a comet predicted ahead of time.
name: Johann Georg Palitzsch

text: Northwest Indian War: General "Mad Anthony" Wayne and a 300 man detachment identify the site of St. Clair's 1791 defeat by the large number of unburied human remains at modern Fort Recovery, Ohio.
name: Anthony Wayne

text: B. R. Ambedkar and his followers burn copies of the Manusmriti in Mahad, Maharashtra, to protest its treatment of Dalit people.
name: B. R. Ambedkar

text: Admiral Chester W. Nimitz, appointed commander of the U.S. Pacific Fleet on December 17, arrives at Pearl Harbor.
name: Chester W. Nimitz

text: Second Battle of Anandpur: In the Second Battle of Anandpur, Aurangzeb's two generals, Wazir Khan and Zaberdast Khan executed two children of Guru Gobind Singh, Zorawar Singh aged eight and Fateh Singh aged five, by burying them alive into a wall.
name: Guru Gobind Singh

text: Babe Ruth of the Boston Red Sox is sold to the New York Yankees by owner Harry Frazee, allegedly establishing the Curse of the Bambino superstition.
name: Babe Ruth

text: Cardinal József Mindszenty is arrested in Hungary and accused of treason and conspiracy.
name: József Mindszenty

text: The Communist Party of the Philippines is established by Jose Maria Sison, breaking away from the Partido Komunista ng Pilipinas-1930.
name: Jose Maria Sison

text: Regina Jonas is ordained as the first female rabbi in the history of Judaism.
name: Regina Jonas

text: Protestant paramilitary leader Billy Wright is assassinated in Northern Ireland, United Kingdom.
name: Billy Wright

text: Riots erupt in Mombasa, Kenya, after Mwai Kibaki is declared the winner of the presidential election, triggering a political, economic, and humanitarian crisis.
name: Mwai Kibaki

text: Constance Markievicz, while detained in Holloway prison, becomes the first woman to be elected Member of Parliament (MP) to the British House of Commons.
name: Constance Markievicz

text: Maurice Richard becomes the first player to score eight points in one game of NHL ice hockey.
name: Maurice Richard

text: American businesswoman Muriel Siebert becomes the first woman to own a seat on the New York Stock Exchange.
name: Muriel Siebert

text: USS Constitution, under the command of Captain William Bainbridge, captures HMS Java off the coast of Brazil after a three-hour battle.
name: William Bainbridge

text: American Civil War: The Battle of Chickasaw Bayou ends in a Union defeat as forces under General William T. Sherman are repulsed with heavy losses by Confederate troops under General John C. Pemberton.
name: John C. Pemberton

text: Cecil B. DeMille starts filming Hollywood's first feature film, The Squaw Man.
name: Cecil B. DeMille

text: Sir Muhammad Iqbal's presidential address in Allahabad introduces the two-nation theory and outlines a vision for the creation of Pakistan.
name: Muhammad Iqbal

text: Filipino patriot and reform advocate José Rizal is executed by a Spanish firing squad in Manila.
name: José Rizal

text: Canadian ice hockey player Ernie McLea scores the first hat-trick in Stanley Cup play, and the Cup-winning goal as the Montreal Victorias defeat the Winnipeg Victorias 6-5.
name: Ernie McLea

text: The Discovery Expedition under Robert Falcon Scott attained a Farthest South at 82°17′S in Antarctica.
name: Robert Falcon Scott

text: Subhas Chandra Bose raises the flag of Indian independence at Port Blair.
name: Subhas Chandra Bose

text: King George II of Greece declares a regency, leaving the throne vacant.
name: George II of Greece

text: Cold War: King Michael I of Romania is forced to abdicate by the Soviet Union-backed Communist government of Romania.
name: Michael I of Romania

text: Proposed budget cuts by Benjamin Netanyahu spark protests from 250,000 workers who shut down services across Israel.
name: Benjamin Netanyahu

text: James, Duke of York is named Duke of Normandy by Louis XIV of France.
name: Louis XIV

text: A coup d'état in Ghana removes President Hilla Limann's PNP government and replaces it with the Provisional National Defence Council led by Flight lieutenant Jerry Rawlings.
name: Jerry Rawlings

text: Captain David Beatty is promoted to rear admiral, and becomes the youngest admiral in the Royal Navy (except for royal family members) since Horatio Nelson.
name: David Beatty

text: Battle of Nancy: Charles the Bold is defeated and killed in a conflict with René II, Duke of Lorraine; Burgundy subsequently becomes part of France.
name: Charles the Bold

text: Contralto Marian Anderson becomes the first person of color to perform at the Metropolitan Opera in Giuseppe Verdi's Un ballo in maschera.
name: Marian Anderson
